stories.title: Why former IAS Divya Mittal chooses Mirzapur Sadar seat:Eyes 1.5 lakh Vaishya voters; could pose challenge for BJP and SP
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh IAS officer Divya Mittal has announced the launch of her own political party, named ‘Jan Neeti Bharat’. She will contest the 2027 Assembly elections from the Mirzapur Sadar seat. Two of Divya Mittal’s decisions are currently drawing attention. First, she has not joined any existing political party. Second, instead of contesting as an independent candidate, she has formed her own party. She has also chosen Mirzapur Sadar, a constituency where upper-caste voters have a significant influence. On September 30, Divya Mittal announced her entry into politics. She said, “I will stay in Uttar Pradesh. I will not be afraid; I will ask questions. I will not join any party. I will walk alone. My aim is not to change politicians but to change politics entirely. I do not need money or muscle power.” First, let us look at why Divya has chosen Mirzapur Sadar. Three major reasons appear to explain her decision. 1. A strong base of Vaishya voters The Mirzapur Sadar Assembly constituency has around 1.20 lakh to 1.50 lakh Vaishya voters. Divya Mittal herself belongs to the Vaishya community. This is considered one of the largest concentrations of Vaishya voters in a single constituency in eastern Uttar Pradesh. During her earlier tenure as the District Magistrate of Mirzapur, Divya Mittal built a public image through her administrative work. This could help her connect with Vaishya voters. 2. Advantage of direct public connect Divya Mittal, who has served as District Magistrate of Mirzapur and Deoria, is known as a strict officer who maintained direct contact with the public. She has been active in the Mirzapur Sadar constituency for some time. She has been reaching out to people by participating in Garba and Dandiya celebrations with women and organising public meetings in villages and small towns. Her earlier connection with the district is helping her strengthen her political base. Mirzapur Sadar Seat — BJP won 3 times, SP won 3 times in 6 Elections (Note: The year 2009 listed in the image refers to the 2007 election cycle) 3. A vision for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections Political observers believe Mirzapur Sadar may only be the first step for Divya Mittal. Through the 2027 Assembly elections, she could seek to establish her political credibility and build a stronger foundation for a possible claim to a Lok Sabha seat in Mirzapur or another prominent constituency in eastern Uttar Pradesh in 2029. Understanding the caste equation in Mirzapur Sadar Mirzapur district has five Assembly constituencies: Chhanbey, Chunar, Majhwan, Marihan and Mirzapur Sadar. The social composition of Mirzapur Sadar appears to suit Divya Mittal’s political strategy. Divya's entry could pose a challenge for both BJP and SP In the 2022 Assembly elections, BJP candidate Ratnakar Mishra Matiyari won the Mirzapur Sadar seat with 1,18,263 votes. He defeated Samajwadi Party candidate Kailash Chaurasia, who secured 77,921 votes, by a margin of around 41,000 votes. According to political analysts, the consolidation of Brahmin and Vaishya voters in favour of the BJP helped the party secure a decisive victory in 2022. However, the equation could change in 2027. Divya Mittal's entry could split Vaishya votes, which have traditionally been considered part of the BJP's core support base. If she manages to gain support among OBCs, Dalits and women, the Samajwadi Party could also face the challenge of retaining its traditional support base. If the BJP fields sitting MLA Ratnakar Mishra again, Brahmin voters could consolidate behind him. In that situation, gaining support from non-Vaishya and non-Brahmin communities, including Bind, Nishad, Muslim and Dalit voters, would be particularly important for Divya Mittal. Mirzapur Sadar seat — upper-caste voters decide who becomes MLA BJP MLA seen distributing fruit at a hospital On November 14, the BJP MLA had said that he wanted votes only from people who chanted “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”, “Jai Shri Ram” and “Vande Mataram”. He said he did not want votes from those who did not believe in Bharat Mata. He added that he would accept votes only from those who were devotees of Lord Ram and worshipped Bharat Mata. He also said he did not want support from people who ate food here but sang songs against the country. After Divya Mittal announced her decision to contest the election, videos of Ratnakar Mishra distributing fruit to people at a government hospital surfaced on November 15. Why did she form a party instead of joining an existing one? Instead of joining an established party such as the BJP, SP, BSP or Congress, Divya Mittal has chosen to follow an independent political path. There are strategic reasons behind this decision. She wants to expand her political reach beyond a single constituency. Had she contested as an independent candidate, her political identity might have remained limited to Mirzapur Sadar. By forming her own party, she can present herself as a potential star campaigner across Uttar Pradesh. Moreover, major regional parties in Uttar Pradesh are often associated with caste-based politics or past controversies. A new party gives Divya a platform centred on clean governance and a fresh political approach. It also allows her to implement her policies independently rather than working within the organisational structure and disciplinary framework of an established party. Focus on women voters, party agenda announced During Thursday's press conference, Divya Mittal's speech focused largely on women. She made it clear that women's safety, rights, education and self-reliance would be among the main priorities of the ‘Jan Neeti Party’. Appealing for direct public engagement, she said she would spend the coming months visiting villages and blocks to interact with people. The party announced three key commitments to attract public support and also shared an outline of its proposed governance policies. UP has 27 Vaishya MLAs, along with ministers and MPs The Vaishya community accounts for around 7% to 8% of Uttar Pradesh's total population but has considerable political influence. The current Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 27 MLAs from the Vaishya community. The state government also has one Cabinet minister and two Ministers of State with independent charge from the community. In the Lok Sabha, three MPs from Uttar Pradesh belong to the Vaishya community. Divya Mittal's new political experiment raises questions about the future direction of Vaishya politics. Will she be able to challenge traditional party loyalties and offer voters a new alternative? That will be worth watching in the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: Rape, robbery accused turn ‘Babas’ to evade police:Claim to help couples have children through rituals in UP, truth exposed on camera
stories.summary: Jhansi’s divine court… Followers prostrate themselves amid occult rituals. Officials and politicians bow before the self-styled holy man, who sits on a high platform and offers ‘spiritual guidance’. It took the police 22 years to discover that this man, who claimed to offer spiritual guidance, was accused of robbery and kidnapping. Seven days ago, the police arrested Kali Sarkar Baba, whose real name is Pradeep Shukla, in Jhansi. After his identity was exposed, Dainik Bhaskar conducted an investigation and found that several criminals in Uttar Pradesh had become self-styled holy men to evade the police. Taking advantage of religious faith, they operated without attracting police action. Our investigation also found that the men facing criminal cases had tried several businesses to earn money before becoming holy men. Some sold fish, while others worked as blacksmiths. One tried his hand at politics and even contested an election. When they failed to succeed elsewhere, they became babas. Now, they are exploiting people's trust and putting their lives at risk. Read the full investigation… Munawwar Baba’s house stands amid fields in Maharajganj A house belonging to Munawwar Baba stands amid fields in Khosta village in Maharajganj. There is a shrine inside the house. We were told that the baba awakens spiritual powers here. His phone number was written on a wall. There were no followers inside, only three or four family members. They said the baba had gone to Nepal and would return after eight days. His phone was switched off, so people were travelling from distant places to meet him. Gabbar Baba lives next door to Munawwar Baba. He also gives out amulets and claims that special prayers can cure infertility and remove problems caused by ghosts and evil spirits. Villagers said the baba did not attend anyone's religious ceremonies. A girl had accused him of rape, and a case had also been registered against him for kidnapping a minor. They said he had fled because of these cases. The police later arrested him and sent him to jail. The girl reveals the truth about Munawwar Baba The girl who filed the rape complaint told Dainik Bhaskar about her ordeal. She said, “On the morning of 29 July 2026, at around 9 am, I was going to school to fill out a scholarship form. On the way, I met Munawwar and Gabbar, who are brothers. They forced me into a vehicle and made me drink water mixed with an intoxicating substance. I lost consciousness. “Near the Nepal border, Munawwar asked me where my Aadhaar card was. I told him it was with my aunt. He threatened me, saying I should get the card or they would kill me or sell me in Nepal. I was scared, so I called my aunt and asked her to send a copy of the Aadhaar card to my phone. “He also threatened me and said that if we met security personnel at the border, I should tell them that we were going to Nepal to get medicine and that the man accompanying me was my uncle.” However, Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel became suspicious after seeing the girl's condition and detained Munawwar. In her statement to the police, the girl also alleged that Munawwar had raped her on 20 July, before the kidnapping. FIR registered against Munawwar Baba Munawwar is accused of trying to take the minor girl to Nepal on 28 July. SSB personnel deployed along the India-Nepal border stopped the girl and called her family. They detained Munawwar and his brother Gabbar. A case was registered at Chowk police station. During the investigation, the police found that Gabbar had no connection with the case, but Munawwar wanted to take the girl to Nepal. Munawwar was sent to jail. Gabbar also fled to Nepal out of fear. Gangaram Baba charges ₹200 for registration Inside the ashram of Gangaram Baba, we found a room that served as a reception area. A poster on the wall listed the rules and regulations, along with a mobile number for appointments. Just as patients register and get a token at a doctor's clinic, visitors to the tantric Gangaram's ashram also have to take a number. A registration fee of ₹200 is charged. There was also a counter selling cloves and incense sticks. We first met Gangaram's driver, Saheb Singh, who was sitting at the reception. Saheb Singh says: ‘Baba can solve problems over the phone, too’ Reporter: When can we meet the baba? Is there a fee? Saheb Singh: Tokens are issued on Wednesdays and Fridays. You have to register by paying ₹200. Reporter: One person is unable to get a job and is also facing a lot of legal cases. Saheb Singh: Yes, bring him here. The problem will be solved. Reporter: How much will it cost? Will ₹2,000 to ₹4,000 be enough? Saheb Singh: Yes, it costs at least that much. Sometimes, it costs more. Reporter: Does it work? How many people come here? Saheb Singh: People come from very far away. After speaking to him, we left and met some villagers. Our conversation with them exposed the truth about tantric Gangaram. ‘He has been to jail and beaten up… now he has become a baba’ Reporter: Do people benefit from his rituals? Villager: No one benefits. It is all nonsense. Reporter: Has the baba always lived here, or did he come from somewhere else? Villager: No, he came here from Gagaha, a rural area in Gorakhpur. He bought land, built an ashram and started this business. Reporter: How long has he been here? Villager: Four or five years. Earlier, he lived in Dubiyari village. There, the village head, Ramnath, beat him up and drove him away. He then came here, bought land and built the ashram. He also stayed in Kauriram for some time. Reporter: What did he do before? Villager: He used to sell fish. He started this business after coming to our village. He has been to jail several times. First, he asks you to come back. Then he says to pay ₹10,000, ₹20,000 or ₹50,000. That is how he operates. Reporter: Don't you people visit him? Villager: No, we don't take him seriously. He got the words ‘Gangaram Baba Tantric’ written on the signboard at the crossroads himself. People see it and come here. Reporter: Has anyone benefited from his services? Villager: No one knows. He has ruined many people after taking their money. He charges ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh. Many people abuse him, too. FIR registered against Gangaram Baba A married woman who was unable to conceive visited Gangaram's ashram. She explained her problem and asked him to perform religious rituals. The baba allegedly told her, “I have helped many people have children. If occult rituals do not work, I will help you conceive through another method.” Gangaram then allegedly started calling the woman repeatedly. However, she did not fall for his claims and refused his treatment. The tantric allegedly threatened her over the phone. An FIR was registered against Gangaram in September 2022. Vijay Mishra Baba charges ₹100 for registration Ballo Khas village is around 10 km from Maharajganj district headquarters. Vijay Mishra Baba has built an ashram here called Siddhpeeth Ballodham. Visitors must pay ₹100 to register before meeting him. They then have to wait three to four hours for their turn. The baba claims to solve people's problems through occult rituals. He also gives them herbal medicines under his own brand, claiming they can cure illnesses. The ashram sees more visitors on Mondays and Fridays. To uncover the truth, we used a hidden camera. Villagers then revealed some shocking details. ‘A girl used to live at the baba's ashram; she was found hanging from a tree in a field’ Reporter: Do you trust the baba? Villager 1: We do not trust him. You can go and see for yourself. Reporter: Has he not managed to trap the villagers yet? Villager: We know everything, so why would we fall for it? People come from far away. We don't know what he does with them. Reporter: Why spend money if there is no benefit? Villager 2: That is true. As soon as you enter, you have to pay ₹100 for a registration slip. If you visit every day, you have to pay every day. Reporter: Does the baba actually have any spiritual powers, or is this business just running like this? Villager: Please don't ask us about all this. Reporter: What did he do before becoming a baba? Villager: He used to work in politics. Then he started performing rituals to drive away ghosts and evil spirits. He told everyone in the village that he would build an 11-foot Shivling. He uploaded a video of it on the internet and then started going from village to village collecting donations. This made him known in distant areas. Reporter: Has anything happened at the ashram that should not have happened? Villager: A few years ago, a girl used to live there. She was found hanging by a rope around her neck, some distance from her home. There was a huge uproar. Later, the matter was settled after money was paid. It has been three years since the baba met the villagers. He stays inside his house. Reporter: How does he perform these rituals? Villager: If you go there, he will ask you to bring cloves, camphor and incense sticks. He charges ₹3,000 to ₹4,000 for the ritual. He sprinkles water on the deity and then finishes the worship. FIR registered against Vijay Mishra Baba A girl used to live at Vijay's ashram. Her body was found hanging from a tree on 19 June 2024. Allegations were made that Vijay had raped her and that she had been murdered. However, the police investigation found that the girl had not been murdered and had died by suicide. Shiva Vishwakarma used to repair bicycles We then reached the village of the fourth baba, Shiva Vishwakarma, in Chauri Chaura. Shiva Vishwakarma used to work as a blacksmith. He has built a Kamakhya Devi temple in a village field. He now performs occult rituals in the name of worshipping Goddess Durga and Kali. When we reached the spot, Shiva Vishwakarma was not there. The temple gate was locked. We met some villagers nearby and spoke to them. ‘He used to repair bicycles; now he has become a baba’ Reporter: Do people benefit from his services? Villager: Some people benefit, while others do not. Reporter: You live in the village, so you must know the truth. Villager: The villagers don't go to him. Everyone knows he is useless. Reporter: How long has he been doing this? Villager: It has been more than two or three years. Reporter: What did he do before? Villager: He used to repair bicycles. Gradually, he entered this line of work. Reporter: Someone told us he is a very powerful baba and that the problem would be solved with a 100% guarantee. Villager: Sir, only God can give a 100% guarantee. Even doctors don't offer that. How can he guarantee anything? Reporter: Some people say he is a fraud and advise others not to visit him. Villager: These babas are among the biggest frauds. Reporter: If people spend money, will they benefit? Villager: Visit him first, but don't pay him. He charges ₹300 as a fee. There is a huge crowd, and people come from distant places. Reporter: Do politicians also visit him? Villager: Politicians don't come here, but he keeps meeting them. Reporter: Is the baba also involved in politics? Villager: Anyone who has money will get involved in politics. They are not going to do farming or labour work. Reporter: Is he associated with any political party? Villager: He is associated with Chairman Sunny Jaiswal and keeps travelling around with him. Babas earn ₹10 lakh to ₹11 lakh a month The babas charge registration fees. Visitors pay between ₹100 and ₹300 for a registration slip. Between 50 and 100 people visit each baba every day. Each baba has fixed days for visitors, when the crowd can reach 500 people. The babas also persuade devotees to pay for special rituals. They perform these rituals for 10 to 15 people every day, charging between ₹1,000 and ₹20,000 per person. This brings in lakhs of rupees every month.

stories.title: Muskan and Sahil’s conduct was ‘disgusting and lustful’:Judge says method of cutting up and hiding husband’s body shook conscience; 10 key points from verdict
stories.summary: In Meerut’s blue drum murder case, Saurabh Rajput’s wife Muskan and her lover Sahil have been sentenced to death. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra has prepared a 163-page judgment. The judgment states that murdering a husband in his own home, dismembering his body and concealing the evidence was an act that shook society’s conscience. Muskan and Sahil have shown no remorse for their crime. Instead, their conduct after the murder reflects their repulsive nature and lustful desires. There is no possibility of Muskan and Sahil reforming and returning to society. Therefore, there is no reason to grant them any leniency in sentencing. Read the 10 major points from the judgment order… 1. The law’s purpose is to protect society The district judge began his conclusions with verse number 49 from the Udyoga Parva of the Mahabharata. He wrote that without society, the law is destroyed. A society without punishment also falls apart. Therefore, the law and punishment must protect society, while society must incorporate law and punishment within itself. 2. Murdering someone in their own home and dismembering the body is an extremely cruel and ruthless act The crime committed by the convicts (Muskan and Sahil) is extremely cruel and grotesque. The victim was killed in his own home, where he had returned from abroad after several years with the hope of living with his family. In that very house, his wife, along with her lover, murdered him brutally and dismembered his body in a repulsive and extremely cold-blooded manner. This was an exceptionally cruel and ruthless way of committing a crime. The bloodstains on the walls and ceilings at the crime scene confirm this cruelty. It may be recalled that Muskan and Sahil climbed onto Saurabh’s chest and stabbed him three times. They then cut his neck and both wrists, separating them from his torso. The blood that flowed from the body covered even the room’s walls. After dismembering the body, the two took the remains to Sahil’s house. Muskan and Sahil slept in Sahil’s room throughout the night with the dismembered remains of Saurabh. 3. The method used to conceal the body shakes society’s conscience “The manner in which the body and evidence were concealed after Saurabh’s murder is extremely shocking. It shakes society’s conscience.” It may be recalled that after dismembering Saurabh’s body, Muskan and Sahil placed his head and wrists in separate pillowcases. The following day, they put the body parts into a blue plastic drum and sealed them with a cement mixture. 4. Muskan and Sahil’s conduct reflects their repulsive nature and lustful desires “The convicts (Muskan and Sahil) have no remorse for their crime. Instead, their conduct after the crime reflects their repulsive nature and lustful desires.” It may be recalled that after murdering Saurabh and disposing of his body in a blue drum, Muskan and Sahil went on a 15-day honeymoon trip to Manali, Shimla and Kasol. They celebrated Sahil’s birthday, danced while intoxicated, attended a Holi party and made objectionable videos. 5. The crime has given rise to deep hatred and anger in society “From society’s perspective, it is difficult even to imagine that a married woman would join hands with someone with whom she had a relationship before marriage, her lover, and murder her husband so brutally and cunningly to fulfil her immoral objectives. This is not merely a betrayal of an individual’s trust, but an act that completely destroys social trust. It is an extremely repulsive and horrific crime that gives rise to deep hatred and anger in society.” It may be recalled that Muskan had married her childhood sweetheart, Saurabh, against the wishes of both families. After getting married, she resumed her affair with Sahil, her former schoolmate, in her husband’s absence. She murdered her husband, Saurabh, because of her relationship with Sahil. 6. The crime has caused deep outrage in society “This is harmful to social balance. Such a crime falls within the category of offences described in the Machhi Singh case as extremely ruthless, grotesque, satanic, repulsive and cowardly. It has caused deep outrage in society. The crime was committed in a satanic, ruthless and cowardly manner.” It may be recalled that after the blue drum case came to light, it was widely discussed everywhere, from social media to other platforms. People also condemned the crime. 7. The gravity of the crime outweighs the circumstances that could reduce the sentence “In the view of this court, the circumstances aggravating the seriousness of the crime in this case far outweigh the circumstances that could reduce the sentence.” It may be recalled that after murdering Saurabh and adopting such methods to conceal his body, Muskan and Sahil went on a 15-day trip to celebrate their honeymoon. Even in jail, neither showed any remorse for the crime. In other words, the gravity of the crime is so great that it outweighs the circumstances that could justify a lesser sentence. 8. This crime falls under the rarest of rare category The district judge wrote in the order: “This crime falls under the rarest of rare category. The court holds this view without any hesitation.” It may be recalled that the manner in which Muskan and Sahil murdered Saurabh, concealed his body, dismembered it and slept alongside the body parts throughout the night constituted an extremely serious crime. 9. There are no circumstances warranting leniency “The court has reached the conclusion that there is no possibility of the convicts reforming and returning to society. Therefore, there is no reason to grant them any leniency in sentencing. In my opinion, there are no circumstances that warrant a lenient approach.” It may be recalled that even after committing such a heinous murder, Muskan and Sahil never showed any change in their behaviour. Reports received from the jail stated that both were mentally normal. They showed no signs of stress or anxiety. Both were living comfortably in jail and had no remorse for what they had done. 10. The crime completely destroys social trust “This crime is not merely a betrayal of an individual’s trust, but also an act that completely destroys social trust.” It may be recalled that Muskan betrayed her husband’s trust. Following this case, several other incidents involving husbands being murdered with the help of their wives’ lovers have continued to come to light. Read the exact order sentencing them to death After giving the utmost consideration to all the guiding principles laid down by the Supreme Court, this court has reached the conclusion that, in view of the facts and circumstances mentioned above, a sentence of life imprisonment would be inadequate for the convicts, Sahil Shukla and Muskan Rastogi, in the present case. In such circumstances, this court finds no other punishment justifiable for the convicts apart from the death penalty. In carrying out the death sentence, the convicts shall be hanged by the neck and kept suspended until they are dead. The judgment order is divided into two parts The first 126 pages of the judgment order contain the case brief. The order is divided into two parts. The first 126 pages describe the sequence of events and the gruesome details of the case. These 126 pages were typed by the night of 30 September 2026, the date on which the district court convicted Muskan and Sahil of murder. The district judge had told Muskan and Sahil: “Both of you have murdered Saurabh Rajput. Both of you are convicted of murder. The sentence will be pronounced after 14 days.” This section contains statements from 22 witnesses, details of the evidence, and a summary of the proceedings and arguments in the case. In his judgment, the judge referred to more than 35 earlier Supreme Court rulings. The second part of the judgment is 37 pages long. These 37 pages contain the conclusions and the order imposing the death penalty. They were typed on the evening of 14 October 2026, after Muskan and Sahil were sentenced to death.

stories.title: Ravita gets death sentence for killing husband:Had released snake; lover also sentenced to death; Meerut court awards capital punishment to four people in three days
stories.summary: A court in Meerut has sentenced Ravita and her lover Amardeep to death for murdering her husband and making it appear that he died of a snakebite on Friday. Before the sentence was announced, the court heard their final statements on Friday through video conferencing, as both are in jail. The judge asked them, “You both have been convicted of murder. What sentence do you want?” Ravita replied that she had three young children and requested that someone take care of them. She then fell silent. Amardeep said his parents were old and had no one to look after them. He requested that their care should not be neglected. After this, both broke down and began crying. Strangled husband and staged snakebite On the night of April 17, 2025, Ravita and Amardeep allegedly strangled her husband, Amit Kashyap, to death. They then left a snake on the bed to make it appear that he had died from a snakebite. However, the post-mortem report revealed that Amit had been strangled. Snake charmers also told investigators that the snake had no fangs and could not have caused his death. Charge sheet filed within 60 days Police filed the charge sheet 60 days after the murder. The case was heard in the court of ACJM-12 Jayveer Singh Nagar. Over 551 days, the court held 87 hearings and recorded statements from more than 12 witnesses. On October 7, the court found Ravita and Amardeep guilty of murder. The court has now sentenced both to death. The judge also directed that the District Magistrate of Meerut ensure the care of the couple's three children. Sentence announced after lunch Ravita and Amardeep was produced before the court. Special Public Prosecutor Farzana Maqsood represented the prosecution, while Ravita and Amardeep's lawyer Omkar Singh Bhati and the lawyer representing deceased Amit presented their arguments. The hearing could lasted around an hour. Ravita and Amardeep counselled in jail, found mentally stable Ravita and Amardeep have been behaving normally in jail. Both eat and sleep on time and follow prison rules and discipline. Ravita works in the jail kitchen and helps with cleaning. She is also skilled at applying mehendi. During a mehendi competition organised in the jail on Hariyali Teej recently, she won first prize. Amardeep, meanwhile, used to work making sports equipment in jail. When both learnt that Muskan and Sahil had been sentenced to death, they were somewhat disturbed but later returned to normal. The jail administration has increased surveillance over them. They underwent counselling, during which their mental condition was found to be normal. Amit's mother says the murderous daughter-in-law and her lover should be hanged Amit's mother, Munesh Devi, said, “The way my son was brutally murdered and made to appear as though he had been bitten by a snake, I want my murderous daughter-in-law and her lover to be hanged. Just as they made my son suffer, they should also die in agony. Only then will my soul find peace. The heartless Ravita destroyed my son's married life and left three children orphaned.” The mother said, “My son Amit was the father of three children. Since his death, the memory of my son's laughter and voice makes me cry every moment. His three innocent children still ask, ‘Where is our father? Where is our mother?’” His father could not bear the shock of his son's murder either and died after suffering in silence. “I want my son's killers to be hanged. If they are not sentenced to death, I will appeal in the High Court. I will ensure justice for my innocent grandchildren and myself,” she said. Brother says Ravita could have left Amit if she did not want to live with him Amit's brother, Sandeep, said, “If Ravita did not want to live with Amit, she could have told him or left him. But she brutally murdered my brother. The post-mortem also confirmed that Amit died from strangulation. “We came here hoping that the court would deliver its verdict today. The court must ensure justice for us. We want no punishment less than the death penalty. I will continue fighting to ensure that my brother's killers are sentenced to death.” Government lawyer says Ravita and Amardeep guilty of murder and destroying evidence Farzana Maqsood, the government lawyer who represented Amit in the case, said, “The court has convicted Amardeep and Ravita and fixed 16 October for sentencing. We presented 12 witnesses in this case. “Among them were the complainant, Monu Kashyap, and Munesh, who were also eyewitnesses. On the night of the murder, they saw Ravita coming in and going out of her son's room. Ravita was having an illicit relationship with Amardeep, who used to visit her house. “There were arguments on several occasions. Later, the two conspired to eliminate Amit Kashyap, after which Ravita became deeply involved in worship and religious rituals. A few days later, Ravita planned to get a snake for the worship. A snake charmer then supplied a horse-whip snake. Amit was subsequently strangled to death.” Lawyer says both accused were located at the house on the night of the murder Balraj, the lawyer representing Amit, said Ravita and Amardeep's mobile phone locations placed them at the scene of the crime. Both were seen coming and going from the location. Their illicit relationship had been going on for a long time. They had also been warned about it, and Amit's mother had seen them visiting each other. On this basis, both were found guilty, he said. Now, read the full story of the husband's murder and the snake used to stage his death Wife had claimed: ‘He did things to me worse than rape’ While being taken to jail, accused wife Ravita had said, “He (her husband Amit) used to beat me every day. He did things to me that were worse than rape. He would say he would turn me into a prostitute and make me work in the sex trade. He knew that I spoke to Amardeep on the phone. My husband himself had arranged for me to speak to Amardeep over the phone. He then told me that he would call Amardeep to our house and that I would have to help him kill him. He said he would kill me too afterwards.” Lover had claimed: ‘Amit sent men after me to kill me, so I killed him’ Before being sent to jail, Ravita's lover Amardeep had said, “A few days ago, Amit and I had an argument over a transaction involving ₹3,500. Some people then helped us settle the dispute. Even after that, Amit sent some men after me to kill me. “When I learnt about this, I conspired to murder Amit to save my own life,” he said. Amardeep added, “There is a village called Mohammadpur in the Mawana area, where many snake charmers live. I bought the snake from them for ₹1,000. One of their associates came here and sold it to me.” 3 key pieces of evidence that formed the basis for the conviction 1. The snake charmer from whom the two bought the snake told the court that Amardeep had obtained it by saying he needed it for worship at a devotional gathering. It was an old horse-whip snake with no fangs. Its bite could not cause anyone's death. 2. Amit's post-mortem report showed scratch marks on his face and hands. The injuries and findings confirmed that he had been strangled and suffocated to death. No snake venom was found. 3. Testimony from mobile phone companies was also crucial to the case. One of the main grounds for the conviction was the phone conversations between the two. The number Amardeep used to speak to Ravita was not registered in his name. Instead, the number and mobile phone were registered to a man living in Jagriti Vihar. Within 24 hours of Amit's murder, Ravita and Amardeep spoke to each other 65 times through phone calls and WhatsApp calls. Before that, they had exchanged more than 2,000 calls over six months using the same number. Call records also showed conversations late at night.

stories.title: 5kg of drugs sent on Raksha Bandhan, ₹1.29 crore collected:Cash found in Scorpio’s secret compartment in Mandsaur; accused caught before returning to UP
stories.summary: ₹1.29 crore was recovered from a Scorpio-N in Barkheda Uda village in the Shamgarh area of Mandsaur. The cash had been hidden in a secret chamber built into the vehicle's body. A new disclosure emerged in the case on Thursday. Mohammad Islam and Suryaprakash, who had come from Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh, had arrived to collect outstanding money. It is being reported that around Raksha Bandhan, Bhawanishankar Meena had ordered approximately 5 kg of brown sugar from them. The two had come to collect the outstanding amount. They were about to return to UP when the police arrested all three. However, there has been no official confirmation of the transaction or the purchase and sale of brown sugar. Police raid house after receiving information about narcotics Acting on information received on Thursday about drug trafficking in Barkheda Uda village, a team from three police stations raided Bhawanishankar Meena's house under the direction of SP Vinod Kumar Meena. The team included Shamgarh police station in-charge Kapil Saurashtriya and Bhanpura police station in-charge Vinay Bundela. Bhawanishankar Meena (49), Bareli resident Mohammad Islam (47) and Suryaprakash (59) were found at the house. A Scorpio-N was also parked there. The vehicle had no number plate. A number plate bearing the words 'Gov. Of India' was found inside. ₹1.29 crore recovered from secret chamber The police took the vehicle to Shamgarh police station. It was thoroughly inspected with the help of a mechanic. A secret chamber made by welding was found in the body behind the back seat. When the vehicle's parts were opened, bundles of notes were found inside. It took around 1.5 hours to count the cash using a machine. The police seized ₹1 crore 29 lakh. The vehicle was identified as belonging to Mohammad Islam through its engine and chassis numbers. Cash source under investigation; Income Tax Department informed SP Vinod Kumar Meena said the police had received credible information about the purchase and sale of narcotics at the house. During the operation, cash hidden in the vehicle was found. The two people who had come from Bareilly and the owner of the house have been arrested. The Income Tax Department has been emailed to ascertain the source of the cash. The police are investigating the narcotics trade and the criminal records of the accused. One of those arrested also has a previous criminal record. Family linked to liquor trade According to sources, Bhawanishankar Meena's family is involved in the liquor trade. Liquence licences in Melkheda and Khadawada are in the name of his son, Arvind. Bhawanishankar's wife is the village sarpanch. He is said to be associated with the BJP. In 2025, Arvind was accused of attacking Sub-Inspector Avinash Soni, who was posted at Shamgarh police station, with a stick. The sub-inspector received 18 stitches to his head in the incident. The police are currently investigating the source of the cash, the role of the accused and their possible links to the narcotics trade.

stories.title: EC orders voter list revision in 17 states-UTs:List includes MP and UP; parties to be informed about additions deletions
stories.summary: The Election Commission on Thursday directed 17 states and Union Territories to conduct a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls. The states include Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa and Uttarakhand, which are scheduled to hold Assembly elections next year. The order comes amid nationwide protests by the Opposition against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the matter also pending before the Supreme Court. Under the SSR, new names will be added to voter lists and errors in existing entries will be corrected. Young people who turn 18 in 2027 will also be able to apply for inclusion. Political parties will be informed about additions and deletions from the electoral rolls. Under the SSR, new names will be added to electoral rolls, and errors in existing entries will be corrected. Young people who turn 18 in 2027 will also be able to apply for inclusion. The order comes amid controversy and protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). What is the objective of SSR? According to the Election Commission, the objective of SSR is to keep electoral rolls up to date and ensure that no eligible citizen is left off the list. Special attention will be given to young people and first-time voters. Young people who turn 18 on 1 April, 1 July or 1 October 2027, in addition to those who turn 18 on 1 January 2027, will also be able to apply in advance. The Commission has directed officials to make efforts to receive applications from all eligible voters. 1. Young people who turn 18 on 1 April, 1 July or 1 October 2027, in addition to 1 January 2027, will also be able to apply in advance to register as voters. 2. The Commission has directed officials to make efforts to obtain applications from all eligible voters. 3. If more than 2% of names are deleted at any polling booth, the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) must personally investigate. The ERO must also investigate if a person files objections seeking the deletion of more than five names. 4. All records of additions, deletions and corrections will be preserved. Physical lists of claims and objections will be provided to political parties every week. 5. Minutes of meetings and signatures of political party representatives will also be preserved. SSR order does not mention a separate process to add names omitted during SIR The Election Commission’s order on SSR does not specify a separate procedure for adding the names of people left off electoral rolls during the SIR. However, under the SIR rules, anyone whose name is missing from the draft electoral roll can claim inclusion by submitting Form 6. The applicant must also provide the required documents. The name will be added only if the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) accepts the application after verifying the applicant’s eligibility. Number and location of polling stations to be reviewed Officials’ posts must not remain vacant; transfers also restricted The Commission has directed the chief secretaries of states and Union Territories to ensure that Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs), District Election Officers (DEOs), Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are provided with adequate staff and resources during the SSR. The posts of CEOs, DEOs, EROs and AEROs must not remain vacant during this period. These officials cannot be transferred without the Commission’s approval. If a transfer is necessary, a proposal explaining the reasons must be submitted to the Commission. Under Section 13CC of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, officials involved in preparing, revising and correcting electoral rolls will work under the Election Commission’s control and supervision during this period. Voters’ addresses to be recorded in a standard format The Election Commission has directed officials to record voters’ addresses in a uniform format in electoral rolls. This will make it easier to identify voters’ homes and their respective polling areas. Assembly elections due in five states, including Uttar Pradesh, next year Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa are scheduled to hold Assembly elections in 2027. SSR will be conducted in all five states. The term of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly ends on 22 May 2027. The terms of the Assemblies of Manipur, which has 60 seats; Goa, with 40 seats; Punjab, with 117 seats; and Uttarakhand, with 70 seats, will end on different dates in March 2027. SSR schedule for these states and Union Territories to be announced later The SSR schedule for Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Delhi, Odisha, Sikkim, Tripura and Telangana will be announced later.

stories.title: Yogi renames Atiq’s Kasari-Masari area:Performs bhumi pujan; 602 flats to be built for poor on seized land
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced that Kasari-Masari, the area associated with mafia don Atiq Ahmed, would be renamed Shri Krishna Puri. Speaking in Prayagraj on Thursday, Yogi said the name Kasari-Masari sounded like it was associated with butchers. He also performed the bhoomi pujan for the flats to be built on government land freed from the possession of Atiq and his henchmen. Yogi said: "The government is now building homes for the poor on land belonging to the mafia. The land on which mafia figures Atiq and Ashraf once set foot would become theirs. The state government used to bow before them." A 14-storey building will be constructed as part of the Prayagraj Development Authority's (PDA) 9,811-square-metre housing project. It will have a total of 602 flats. Each flat will have two bedrooms, a hall and a kitchen. Each flat will have an area of 56.45 square metres. The project will also include parking, rainwater harvesting and a solar system. Other facilities will include a swimming pool, community hall and commercial complex.

stories.title: Two-storey house collapses after blast in Varanasi:3 injured, firecracker factory owner flees with mother
stories.summary: An explosion in firecrackers caused half of a two-storey house to collapse in Varanasi on Thursday evening. The blast was so powerful that a neighbouring house was also damaged. The incident took place at around 5 pm in the densely populated Paigambarpur area. Firecrackers were allegedly being manufactured and stored illegally at the house without a licence. Following the incident, teams from the police, the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) reached the spot. Before their arrival, neighbours had rescued three people from the house and taken them to hospital. The condition of the mother and son is critical. The house owner, Raju Khan, and his 65-year-old mother, Munni, were reportedly not found at the scene. Both had fled before the police arrived. According to eyewitnesses, the explosion was so powerful that they felt as though an earthquake had struck. Neighbours claimed that they had previously complained to the police about the illegal firecracker factory. See pictures related to the incident… Read the full story A powerful explosion occurred on Thursday evening at an illegally operated firecracker factory in the Paigambarpur area of Panchkoshi, Sarnath. The blast was so intense that the house was reduced to rubble. Around 6 members of firecracker trader Raju Khan's family, including Khan himself, were reportedly trapped under the debris. The explosion terrified nearby residents and triggered panic in the area. As soon as the incident was reported, Sarnath police, the fire brigade and an NDRF team reached the spot. Raju Khan's son Adil (16), Chandni (39) and Arabia (10) were injured in the explosion. They have been admitted to the divisional hospital. Raju had been released from jail only a few days ago Raju Khan and his mother, Munni Khan, reportedly fled through the back door. Raju had been released from jail only a few days ago. An explosion occurred in the Jalalipura area 40 years ago, in which Raju was jailed and his father, Matiullah Khan, died. The force of the blast can be gauged from the fact that the outer portion of the neighbouring house also collapsed. The explosion spread panic among residents of nearby houses, and a crowd gathered at the scene. Given the presence of firecrackers inside the house and the possibility of further explosions, rescuers were proceeding cautiously during the operation. Bombs were being made next to our house: Neighbour Neighbour Sunil Kumar said, “Bombs were being made next to our house. There has been a bomb blast. Our house is right beside it. I have just returned from duty. My family would know about it. I have only just come back from work. We had lodged complaints. The police also came and conducted raids several times. But what can we do? Nothing happened.” The road was shaking violently, Eyewitness Eyewitness Pankaj said, “I live here. There was an illegal firecracker manufacturing factory here. A blast occurred. We were walking along the road when the explosion happened in that lane. It was so loud that it felt like an earthquake. The road was shaking violently. We were passing by when a boy, Raju Khan's son, told us, ‘There has been a blast at our house. My grandmother, mother and other family members are trapped inside.’” DCP says handmade firecrackers were found Varuna Zone DCP Rajesh Pandey said, “We received information at 5 pm that a two-storey house had collapsed. When we reached the spot and inspected the site, we found handmade firecrackers scattered around. It is suspected that an incident of this kind occurred while firecrackers were being manufactured, causing the house to collapse. “There was initially no clear information about anyone being injured, but it is being reported that a woman may be trapped under the debris. The SDRF, NDRF and our fire service team are conducting a rescue operation, as you can see, to remove anyone who may be trapped. Since the police arrived, no other information about injuries has been received.”

stories.title: Cricketer Rinku Singh’s dog goes missing in Aligarh:Went out for a walk, sister appeals for help
stories.summary: Cricketer Rinku Singh's pet dog, Brudo, has been missing since October 12. The five-year-old Labrador went out for his morning walk as usual but did not return home. The family searched for him in their housing society, the nearby park and surrounding areas, but could not find him. CCTV footage showed Brudo leaving the house and heading towards a nearby park. However, the family has been unable to trace him since then. On Wednesday evening, Rinku's sister, Neha Singh, shared Brudo's pictures and videos on social media in Aligarh and appealed to people to help find him. Rinku and his brother brought Brudo home when he was 15 days old Rinku Singh's elder brother, Sonu Singh, said, "When Brudo was just 15 days old, Rinku and I brought him home. He is now five years old and has been living with the family ever since. Whenever Rinku is at home, Brudo spends most of his time with him." The family lives in the Golden State housing society in the Ozone City complex in Aligarh. Brudo is not just a pet to them but a member of the family. His disappearance has left everyone at home worried and upset. Went for his usual morning walk but did not return Brudo usually went for a walk in a nearby park at around 10 am every morning. On October 12, he left home as usual but did not return. The family began searching for him around the society, in the park and near houses that were under construction. They also asked two or three nearby families if they had seen him, but found no clues. Family watches four hours of CCTV footage Sonu Singh said the CCTV footage showed Brudo leaving the house and heading towards a nearby park. The family watched around four hours of footage but could not find any information about where he went after that. They suspect that someone may have taken him away, although this has not been confirmed. According to Sonu, the family is currently searching for Brudo on its own and has not yet informed the police. If they are unable to find him, they will consider seeking police help. Rinku Singh has also been informed about Brudo's disappearance. Sister appeals to people to help find Brudo On Wednesday, Neha Singh shared Brudo's picture on social media and appealed to people to help locate him. "Our Brudo has been missing since yesterday. He went missing from Ozone City, where we live. We searched extensively for him, but have not found any trace of him yet," she said. Neha added that Brudo has a red belt around his neck, which can help people identify him. She requested anyone who spots him to contact the family as soon as possible, take a picture and send it to her through a direct message. She also said her social media ID had been shared in the caption. The family is hoping that someone who has seen Brudo will come forward and help bring him home.

stories.title: Elderly man falls for woman 45 years younger:Couple gets engaged in Auraiya; she says they will marry after Navratri
stories.summary: The relationship between 75-year-old Ramsugar and 30-year-old Reena Rajput in Auraiya, Uttar Pradesh, has been making headlines due to their 45-year age gap. According to their neighbours, the two got engaged about a week ago and are now preparing for their wedding, while a video of their engagement has surfaced on Instagram, prompting mixed reactions from users, with some calling it a stunt to gain views and others describing it as true love that transcends age. See 3 pictures... Elderly man's daughter said, "Reena used to visit our house" Reena Rajput is an Instagram blogger. She is a resident of Dayalpur in the Sadar Kotwali area of Auraiya district. Ramsugar, meanwhile, is a resident of Ariyari village in the Sahar area of the district. Following their engagement, preparations for their wedding are now being discussed. According to Ramsugar, Reena Rajput had been visiting his house for the past two years. During this time, the two grew close and he fell in love with Reena. Ramsugar's daughter Radha is also a YouTuber. Radha said that her mother died about seven years ago. Rani used to visit their house. They would all shoot videos together. During this time, her father and Rani developed feelings for each other. Claim that the engagement took place at a beauty parlour According to Radha, her father Ramsugar and Rani Rajput got engaged at a beauty parlour in Auraiya around a week ago. Preparations are under way to conduct their wedding according to traditional rituals. However, no clear information has emerged on when the wedding will take place. Various reactions to this alleged love story are emerging on social media. While some people are calling it true love that transcends age barriers, others consider it a stunt to increase views and popularity on Instagram. There is also speculation that activities related to the engagement were being filmed at a beauty parlour. However, this has not yet been confirmed. Reena says-Age does not matter in love Reena said she had no objection to the age gap and was extremely happy with the decision. She believes that age has no significance in love and that anything is possible. Ram Sugar and she are both fully prepared for this relationship. According to Reena, she and Ram Sugar are already engaged, but the exact wedding date has not yet been decided. The date will be finalised after Navratri, following which the two will get married in a grand ceremony.

stories.title: Muskan cries in Meerut jail after death sentence:Refuses food, gets prisoner number 396; boyfriend Sahil works in fields
stories.summary: Muskaan Rastogi and her lover Sahil, who were sentenced to death in the Saurabh murder case in Meerut on Wednesday evening, are now subject to the prison’s new rules as convicted prisoners, with Thursday marking their first day in this category. Muskaan has been assigned prisoner number 396, while Sahil has been given number 395; she has reportedly been in shock since the sentencing, cried throughout the night and refused to eat, following which prison authorities arranged counselling for her during the night. She asked the counsellor, "What will happen to us now? Is there any way to escape the death penalty?" On Thursday morning, she wore the cream-coloured suit issued to female prisoners. Muskaan is also desperate to meet her elder daughter, Pihu. She will write a letter to her parents for this. Meanwhile, Sahil has begun adapting to the new rules. On Thursday morning, he wore the prisoners' uniform – a white kurta-pyjama. He worked in the fields alongside the other prisoners. Muskaan cried all night and did not eat either As soon as Muskaan and Sahil were sentenced to death on Wednesday evening, they were sent to their respective barracks. At night, the jail authorities shifted Sahil to barrack number 15 for prisoners sentenced to death. Muskaan, who is staying with her 11-month-old daughter, has been kept in her old barrack, 12-B, for now. After the sentence was announced, Sahil and Muskaan reached their respective barracks and did not eat dinner. Sahil lay down after reaching his new barrack, but Muskaan continued crying. Muskaan had breakfast but left more than half of it On Thursday, Sahil and Muskaan got up at 6:30 a.m., along with the other prisoners and detainees. Even while everyone was being counted, Muskaan was seen sitting in the barracks and crying. Some time later, when she saw the prisoners receiving breakfast, Sahil also took his meal. Muskaan, however, did not even look at the breakfast. She was counselled again afterwards. Only then did Muskaan take her breakfast. However, she could not finish it and left more than half of it. According to jail sources, Muskaan is far more distressed than Sahil after being sentenced. She starts crying over the slightest thing. At times, she cries when she looks at her daughter, while at other times, she curses herself. Muskaan was also the one who asked the counsellor the first question. Muskaan told counsellor, "How can I escape the gallows?" Muskaan is desperate to meet her elder daughter. The jail authorities do not have any contact number for Muskaan's family. She has therefore been told to write a letter. Muskaan will soon send a letter from jail to her parents, pleading with them to arrange a meeting with her daughter. Muskaan's elder daughter is with her maternal grandparents. Her younger daughter was born in prison and is with Muskaan. Muskaan asked the counsellor, "What will happen to me now? I have two young daughters. Is there any way to avoid the death penalty?" The counsellor then explained the entire process of appealing in a higher court. Only then did Muskaan calm down. Sahil went to work in the fields with prisoners in the rain In the jail, Muskaan is being referred to as Prisoner No. 396 and Sahil as Prisoner No. 395. Both will also have to work like the other inmates. Muskaan will do sewing and embroidery with the women. Sahil, meanwhile, has been assigned to look after the vegetables in the fields. Despite the rain on Thursday morning, Sahil went to work in the fields with the other inmates. Monitoring of Both Increased, Counselling Schedule Set Senior Jail Superintendent Dr Viresh Raj Sharma said, "Monitoring of Muskaan and Sahil's barracks was increased late on Wednesday night itself. Counselling for both of them has also begun. Sahil is returning to normal, while Muskaan will take some time. Muskaan's counselling schedule has been finalised. She is receiving counselling twice a day. Both of them are also undergoing medical check-ups twice a day." Read how Muskaan murdered Saurabh

stories.title: 2 videos of millionaire Shiva emerge after Shraddha:Lucknow model says, 'I'll call police next time'
stories.summary: Two videos of Lucknow millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma, recorded before his death, surfaced on Thursday. In the videos, a woman is threatening Shiva. She is claimed to be Shraddha Dubey, although the police have not confirmed this so far. Shraddha accuses him of stealing three gold chains and a bracelet. She asks Shiva to return around ₹6 lakh. Shiva assures her that he will return the money. He says, "I am giving it in writing that I will return the money. Keep my car and give me the money." In the video, he can be heard saying that he will return the money within a month. Find out what both VIDEOS contain... FIRST VIDEO: I will return the money within a month Shraddha: When did you steal from my place? What time did you do it? Was it in September or October? When was it? I am asking you very politely. I have not called the police yet. I will call them after this, but first you tell me. Shiva: In September... and when I was going to the washroom... Shraddha: What was I doing in the washroom? Approximately how long did it take me? Shiva: It took around 20-25 minutes. Shraddha: It took 20-25 minutes, so did you steal the jewellery all at once or in separate instances? Shiva: I took them together. Shraddha: Together? Three chains and a bracelet? Shiva: Yes. Shraddha: Where did you sell them? Shiva: At Chowk. Shraddha: Whose shop at Chowk? Shiva: I sold them inside the Gol Darwaza area at Chowk. I do not know which shop it was, because the boy took me there and sold... I mean, the items... Shraddha: He sold them and gave you the money? Shiva: (He nods in agreement.) Shraddha: So the total value of my money is around ₹6 lakh. By when will I get it back? Shiva: You will get it within a month. Shraddha: Does your mother know about this? Shiva: No. Shraddha: That you stole them? Shiva: No one knows. Shraddha: No one knows anything about this? Shiva: Nobody knows. Shraddha: Really! And I am not forcing you to make this video, am I? Brother, you admitted it yourself... Shiva: Yes, I did not have it made... SECOND VIDEO: Shiva said, "Keep my car" Shraddha: When will you return the money? Shiva: Within one month. Shraddha: Really! Shiva: So I will give it to you in writing. Until then, please keep my car. I will pay the money and take my car back. Shraddha released a VIDEO for Shiva's mother, said: "You lost your son, I lost my boyfriend" Accused model Shraddha Dubey has fled to Nepal. She has released three videos from there so far. In the third video, she is heard telling Shiva's mother, "You have lost your son; I have lost my boyfriend." In the video, Shraddha appealed to the media not to spread rumours about the case. She claimed that Shiva's mother had accused her and other people of murder without knowing the full details of the incident. Shraddha questioned why anyone would push someone from their own apartment. Shraddha claims: Shiva was under pressure to repay debts According to Shraddha, Shiva had borrowed money from several people. The lenders used to call him. Shraddha claims that Shiva would tell her that if he failed to repay the loans, he would commit suicide. Shraddha said the two had met before the incident. According to her, Shiva called her and asked to meet. They went to a café, where Shiva ordered coffee for her and juice for himself. They then went to Shraddha's home. Shraddha explained what happened on the morning of 9 October According to Shraddha, the two woke up and made tea on the morning of 9 October. Shiva then went to the bathroom and locked the door. Shraddha claims that after some time, his sister opened the door, after which Shiva jumped from the balcony. Shraddha also accused Shiva's mother of arguing with his driver at the hospital. She said the incident would have been recorded on the hospital's CCTV cameras. Now read the full account

stories.title: Rajnath Singh distributes relief kits to flood-hit residents in Lucknow:Says he came to assure them 'we stand with you', not deliver a speech; promises 10,000 more kits
stories.summary: Defence Minister and Lucknow MP Rajnath Singh arrived in Lucknow on Thursday. He distributed relief materials to 1,000 flood-affected families in the Faizullaganj area of the city. He spoke to residents and enquired about their well-being. Addressing them from the stage, he said, “I have not come here to deliver a speech. I have come to tell you that we stand with you.” He added that another 10,000 relief kits would be distributed. A stage was set up for Rajnath Singh in flood-hit Daudnagar. A green carpet had been laid over the floodwater up to a point some distance from the stage, where the Defence Minister arrived in his convoy. He then inspected the relief camp and met flood-affected residents, enquiring about their well-being. Before his arrival, the roads along his route had been dried using several pumping sets. Rajnath Singh to attend these programmes over 3 days Lucknow BJP metropolitan president Anand Dwivedi said that after meeting flood-affected people, the Defence Minister will meet representatives of social organisations at his residence on Kalidas Marg tomorrow. He will then visit the homes of bereaved families in different parts of the city to meet their relatives and offer his condolences. At 6 pm, he will attend a Durga Puja programme at Ram-Ram Bank Chauraha in Sector E, Jankipuram. After the programme, he will return to his residence and stay there overnight. On the final day of his visit, 17 October, Rajnath Singh will again meet representatives of social organisations at his residence. He will then leave for Lucknow Airport at 11.30 am and return to Delhi from there.

stories.title: Bonded doctors lie at police officers’ feet in Lucknow:ACP sits on ground with folded hands; urges them to end protest
stories.summary: Bonded doctors staged a protest in Lucknow on Thursday as well, demanding equal pay. Earlier, the doctors had arrived with stethoscopes around their necks and tape over their mouths; they were seen pleading with the police with folded hands and lying at their feet. The doctors said they had been protesting for 42 days, but their demands had still not been accepted. When the doctors began moving towards the Chief Minister's residence from 1090 Chauraha in a human chain, the police stopped them. As the doctors began sitting on the road, the ACP himself sat on the ground. With folded hands, he asked the doctors to end their protest. It may be noted that during the protest on 2 September, Health Minister Brajesh Pathak had assured the doctors that equal pay would be implemented. 4 pictures from the protest ... Doctors said: Give us one bond, one salary A large number of bonded doctors took part in the protest. They were carrying placards that read "One Bond One Salary" and "Give justice to bonded medical officers". The police and doctors continued arguing for a considerable time. The police accused the doctors of staging a demonstration without permission and blocking the road. The doctors, however, said they were protesting democratically for their rights. They alleged that the Deputy Chief Minister had promised to provide equal pay, but the promise has not yet been fulfilled. The doctors said they had been protesting over their demands for the past 42 days. Despite this, no concrete solution has been found. The Deputy Chief Minister had met the doctors on 2 September Bonded MBBS doctors from the 2018, 2019 and 2020 batches of government medical colleges are staging the protest. The doctors say they are being paid different salaries despite having the same degrees, bonds and service conditions. They are demanding pay parity and payment of their outstanding arrears. They say Deputy Chief Minister Brijesh Pathak had assured them on 2 September that their demands would be met and a government order would be issued within 24 hours. The government order has not been issued yet. Doctors travelled 300 km to take part in the protest Protesting doctor Akshay said he had come to Lucknow from Mirzapur. It is very difficult for him to take part in the protest after coming from another district. He travels around 300 kilometres to attend, but is disappointed every time. He said, "The Deputy Chief Minister had promised to fulfil our demands within 24 hours, but that did not happen." Akshay said, "We are doctors. We are called gods, but we do not receive the same respect. If we were truly considered gods, we would not be treated this way." ₹50,000 salary, other doctors receive ₹1.10 lakh Dr Nida, who came from Deoria, said they had taken to the streets out of compulsion. Under the bond service, they must complete two years of compulsory service or meet the obligation of a ₹10 lakh bond. During this period, they are posted at CHCs, PHCs and other government health facilities in rural and remote areas. In return, they receive an honorarium of around ₹50,000 to ₹55,000 per month. Doctors' demand: If the degrees are the same, why the difference in salaries? Doctors claim that some doctors serving bonds at government medical colleges under the same MBBS degree, bond, counselling and selection process are being paid up to ₹1.10 lakh per month. Calling this disparity in pay, the protesting doctors are demanding the implementation of equal pay scales and payment of outstanding arrears.

stories.title: A 52-year-old lawyer was shot dead in Prayagraj's Karnalganj police:Wife alleges he was killed in front of police, demands death for death; CCTV shows attackers with faces covered
stories.summary: A 52-year-old lawyer was shot dead in Prayagraj's Karnalganj police station area around noon on Thursday. He was shot in the abdomen and collapsed on the ground, covered in blood. He was rushed to SRN Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The lawyer's wife, Varsha, alleged that her husband, Satish Srivastava, was shot in front of the police. Demanding strict action against the accused, she said they should be killed in an encounter. "I want blood for blood and death for death," she said. Family protests for four hours, demands action Following the murder, the lawyer's family protested for around four hours, demanding action against those responsible. The family members calmed down after DCP City Sagar Jain assured them of appropriate action. The body was then sent for a post-mortem examination. Accused is also a lawyer; CCTV footage emerges According to the police, the accused, Devendra Nath, is also a lawyer. CCTV footage of one of the attackers has emerged, showing the assailants leaving the scene with their faces covered. Police are investigating the case. Here is the full story in detail The lawyer, his wife and daughters were at college Satish Kumar Srivastava, who lives in Salori, has a wife, Varsha, and two daughters, Vaishnavi and Vaishali. Satish Kumar Srivastava was a lab attendant at Ishwar Sharan Degree College, around 200 metres from their home. His wife Varsha teaches at an intermediate college. Their daughter Vaishnavi is also a teacher at a private college. Varsha Srivastava said, "Devendranath Mishra has been trying to occupy our land for the past year. We had also submitted petitions in this matter to several officials, including Chief Minister Yogi, the DCP and the ACP." "Those people were also involved in an incident with my daughter on 10 December. We had gone to Gorakhpur and met Yogiji. He had consoled us and assured us that action would be taken. However, DCP Vivekchandra Yadav was siding with the accused." Wife says, "The attackers entered the house and vandalised it" Today, my husband, I and my daughters were at college. The house was locked. At around 12 noon, my husband called me and said that Devendranath Mishra had entered the house in Salori with several people. He told me to reach there quickly, saying that they were also on their way. We rushed home. We saw Devendranath vandalising our house with around 20 people. They had broken the boundary wall of the plot behind the house. We objected, after which he pushed my husband and then attacked him with an iron rod. His son Nipendranath Mishra, alias Bachchu, Amarendranath Mishra, alias Anupam, and 7-8 other people were with him. Devendranath's wife was also there. All of them pelted stones at us. They knocked me to the ground, beat me with kicks and punches, and attacked me with a chair. Shot her husband in the stomach with a revolver The wife said, "After this, Amarendranath took out a revolver. He shot my husband in the stomach. Outpost in-charge Vinay Yadav also assaulted my husband. I want an FIR to be registered against the accused and for them to be killed in an encounter." Varsha said, "The land belongs to us. I have all the documents. Devendranath had asked me to give him space to park his car. We had been friends for 50 years, so my husband allowed him to park his car. He continued parking it there for two years. After that, Devendranath began encroaching on the land. When the dispute escalated, we went to the police and the court. How was I to know that he would turn into a scorpion?" Family members created a ruckus for four hours Meanwhile, as soon as news of Satish Srivastava's murder reached them, his fellow lawyers and family members arrived at the scene. They left the hospital carrying Satish's body, saying that the funeral would not take place until the accused were killed in an encounter. As soon as they received the information, DCP Yamunanagar Vivekchandra Yadav and DCP City Sagar Jain reached the scene. They tried to persuade the family members. Meanwhile, a heated exchange also took place between the police officers, lawyers and family members. Satish's daughter Vaishnavi told the DCP, "When we went to you with a complaint, you scolded us and sent us away. My father was shot in front of the outpost in-charge. The attackers had climbed onto my house." The family members remained firm for about four hours, demanding action while carrying the body. They later calmed down after police officers assured them that action would be taken. DCP says three teams have been formed; some accused detained DCP Vivekchandra Yadav said, "Devendranath Mishra and Satish Srivastava had been embroiled in a dispute over Nazul property for some time. Devendranath is an Additional Government Advocate (AGA). At around 11:45 a.m. on Thursday, Devendranath arrived at the disputed property." There, he broke the lock that had already been put up by Satish Srivastava's side. A dispute then broke out between the two sides. During the incident, firing was carried out by Devendranath Mishra's side. One bullet struck Satish Srivastava in the abdomen. He sustained serious injuries. His family took him to Raj Nursing Home. Given his critical condition, he was referred to Swaroop Rani Nehru (SRN) Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Following a complaint by Satish's family, a case has been registered at Colonelganj police station. Some of the accused involved in the incident have been detained and are being questioned. Three police teams have been formed to search for the other accused. CCTV footage from the surrounding area is also being examined. Following the registration of the case, anyone found guilty during the investigation will be arrested.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav inducts Brij Bhushan's close aide into SP:Says 'See no evil, hear no evil' on absconding model Shraddha Dubey
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has once again accused the Election Commission of working for the BJP. He said only those who are BJP members are being registered as voters. The Election Commission is treating only BJP members as citizens of India. With the support of the commission and the administration, BJP workers are carrying out large-scale fraud. At a press conference at the Samajwadi Party office on Thursday, Akhilesh listed 10 of the BJP's electoral tactics. He said the BJP's tactics include getting fake votes added, getting opponents' votes deleted, having guns pointed on polling day, tampering with EVMs, rigging the vote count, issuing a certificate of victory to a losing candidate, creating divisions within the Opposition, and forming a government by breaking up the Opposition. key points from Akhilesh Yadav's press conference 1- BJP hides behind the Election Commission when it starts losing elections Akhilesh said that when the BJP appears to be losing or weakening among the people, it hides behind the Election Commission. The two are jointly deceiving the Constitution and the people. He said that since 2022, he had been repeatedly alleging that the Election Commission was working at the BJP's behest. Preparations are being made for a large-scale scam with the administration's support. 2- The commission is not even sharing information The SP chief said party workers had worked to stop alleged attempts at manipulation within the administration. More than 100 forms had been filled out in Sarojini Nagar in the name of Dashrath. The Election Commission had to accept that the complaint was valid. In Sultanpur, applications were submitted to have Nandlal's name removed from the electoral roll using forged signatures. 3- Akhilesh claims: 19 lakh fake voters detected Akhilesh Yadav claimed that, in addition to the 16 lakh fake voters identified so far, another three lakh had been detected. This brought the total number of fake voters detected to 19 lakh. He said the highest numbers had been created in Loni, at 15,000, and Sahibabad, at 13,000. Akhilesh alleged that the most irregularities were being carried out in places where the BJP believed it was losing the election. The SP had lost Moradabad by 722 votes. Therefore, 8,000 fake voters had been added there so far. He claimed that fake voters were being added in places where the BJP's defeat appeared certain. 4- 29 BLOs died during SIR Akhilesh said that 10 fake votes had been created in the name of a young man in Azamgarh. That person will cast one vote, while BJP workers will get the remaining nine votes cast. He said that 29 BLOs had died during the entire process. It is now being reported that the entire SIR process has been nullified. He said 87 lakh Form 6 applications had been submitted. As many as 84,000 names had been added. Information about 67,000 names was made public, while the remaining information was not shared. 5- Fraud may work in by-elections, but we will not allow it in all 403 constituencies Akhilesh Yadav said that 420-style fraud might work in the by-election, but he would not allow it in 403. The BJP will lose and flee. God himself will defeat liars. He alleged that not a single person from the PDA community had been assigned election duty. The BJP was resorting to tactics such as getting fake votes added, having the names of opponents removed and arranging food and drink before voting. 6-The Election Commission's credibility has been destroyed Asked about the Supreme Court issuing a notice, Akhilesh said that the Election Commission should still resign. The Commission's credibility has been destroyed. It appeared to be standing with the BJP. He alleged that the Kundarki election had been looted. Akhilesh said that people have the right to march and hold sit-ins in a democracy. Wherever political leaders sit, that place will become Jantar Mantar. 7- Workers should remain at booths on 17 and 24 October Akhilesh appealed to workers to remain at the booths on 17 and 24 October to prevent fake voters from being added and ensure that the names of those left out are added to the electoral roll. He said the Election Commission had launched a special campaign on these dates. Everyone would have to remain cautious at every step. A total of 120 forms had been submitted through a person named Dashrath. He questioned why voter lists were not linked to Aadhaar when the government had complete data. 8- For the first time, so many gods have joined our party together Bhavani Shukla of Gonda joined the Samajwadi Party along with his five sons. His sons are named Shri Bhagwan Shukla, Krishna Bhagwan Shukla, Shiv Bhagwan Shukla, Vishnu Bhagwan Shukla and Shankar Bhagwan Shukla. Akhilesh Yadav said, "For the first time, so many Bhagwans have come together to the party office. No one in our society can forget these names. Sanatanis, in particular, can never forget them." Akhilesh thanked Bhavani Shukla for joining the SP. The joining of Vinay Purari, Meerut BSP leader Manmohan Singh Saini and some leaders from Gonda was also mentioned during the event.
