stories.title: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal launches new political party:Names it Jan Neeti Bharat, will contest the election from Mirzapur Sadar
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh IAS officer Divya Mittal has announced the launch of her own political party. The party has been named ‘Janniti Bharat’. In a video posted on Facebook at 1 pm on Thursday, she announced that she will contest the 2027 Assembly elections from the Mirzapur Sadar constituency. Divya Mittal said: In Janniti Bharat, the rule will be yours. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections. The government will run according to your wishes for five years. Earlier, on September 30, Divya Mittal had announced her entry into politics. She had said that she would remain in Uttar Pradesh, would not be afraid and would continue to raise questions. She had also said that she would not join any political party and would walk alone. Her aim, she said, was not to change politicians but to change the entire political system. “I do not want money or muscle power,” she had said. Divya, a 2013-batch IAS officer, had written on Facebook two days ago, on Tuesday, that she would announce the next step in her political journey on October 15. Since then, there had been speculation about her future plans. Divya had studied BTech at IIT Delhi and an MBA at IIM Bengaluru before taking up a high-paying job in London. Here is what Divya Mittal said in the video, word for word: 1. First pledge of ‘Janniti Bharat’ — From people to policy, from policy to India Divya Mittal said, “I am forming my own political party. You may ask, are there not enough political parties already? There is no shortage of parties; there is a shortage of people being heard. “I am standing in front of the Ganga. In the Ganga, every drop is equal. All the drops together determine the course. I want to build a party in the same way, where every person is a drop and every drop has a role. The party that has emerged from this idea is called ‘Janniti Bharat’. “In Janniti Bharat, the rule will be yours. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections. The government will run according to your wishes for five years — not just for one day, but at every step. “Janniti Bharat has three pledges. People will be at the centre of the country’s policies and people themselves will decide the policies. “You may remember Devkali Devi. Despite not having water at home, she had asked me for a school. After my video, work on the school began. The foundation was being laid, but then it was discovered that the land belonged to the forest department, so the work was stopped. The children whose future was supposed to be built on that foundation are still waiting. “The question is, when the country’s biggest industrialists need a road to be built, the forest gives way in 80 days. But when a poor person needs a school, a road or a factory, why does that file remain pending for 80 years? “The second policy is justice — where everyone is heard. Ask the people where they should get justice. Ask the people how policies should be made. A mother eats one less roti but makes sure her child has enough to eat. A father cuts down on his own expenses but sends his child to school. This is the kind of thinking our policies will reflect. “There will be a farming policy with farmers at the centre. Farmers know what problems they face from the field to the mandi and where prices collapse. Similarly, trade policy will focus on small traders and the problems they face from their businesses to the ports. “A girl is looking at the moon from the roof of her house today. One day, she will reach it.“The first pledge of Janniti Bharat — from people to policy, from policy to India.” 2. Every decision will be based on need, not identity “The second pledge of Janniti Bharat — every decision will be based on need, not identity.” She said, “A road was being built and hope had emerged in the village. Then someone pointed a finger and changed the direction of the road. On one side, thousands of people would have benefited; on the other, there was one person. The road was diverted towards the other side, where there were hundreds of houses. Courtyards were destroyed and homes were demolished. The road was built for someone. “In Janniti, everyone will be able to point to a location on the map. If there is a dark stretch where girls are afraid to pass, where will they report it? They will mark the location on a mobile app. When 100 people mark the same spot, there will be lights, patrolling and cameras there. The decision will not be taken by the police or a politician, but by those girls. “Whether it is a hand pump, a road or a paved lane, people will point out where the work is needed most and work will begin there. There will be no caste, religion or status involved. Everyone will decide together.” 3. Decisions based on need and equality in decision-making The third pledge of Janniti Bharat is — decisions based on need and equality in decision-making. She said, “The public will keep an account of every piece of work. At present, people do not even know about the work, while the middleman gets to know first. “A woman applied for a permanent house, but she did not know that her house had been approved. A middleman came to her and said, ‘Mother, I will get it done. Give me Rs 5,000.’ If the woman knows about the approval first, then who will the middleman approach? “Every piece of work carried out in that village through any fund should be visible on a mobile phone. But what happens now is that the person who carried out the faulty work is asked whether everything was done properly. What answer will he give? He will say everything is fine. “If you give children their own notebooks to check, they will say everything is fine. Who is the first person to know that a road is in bad condition? The people who use that road. “If we use three colours for a bad road — green means good, yellow means average and red means bad — the same colours can be used for places people depend on every day, such as schools, hospitals and ration shops. “Were books provided at the school? How was the teaching? The same three colours. These three colours can be used for hospitals as well. These three colours can cover the entire block and district. The officer will know, the minister will know and the entire district will know. “This is the third pledge of Janniti Bharat — the public will have the right to demand an account, and that accountability will lead to improvement.” 4. We will fight together — not do politics, but practise Janniti She said, “If you are going to do everything yourselves, then what will the MLAs do? What will the MLAs of Janniti Bharat do? The MLA’s job will be to go to your doorstep. To write for those who cannot write and to mark things on the phone for those who cannot do it themselves. “Today, the MLA sits between the people and the government, but faces the government. In Janniti Bharat, the MLA will sit in the same place, but will face the people. “You may ask, if this is so easy, why has it not happened until now? There is a phone in every hand. If train tickets can be booked on a phone, why can’t this be done on a phone? Because the question here is not about convenience, but about power. “The person who takes Rs 5,000, the person who leaves a road incomplete, the person who investigates his own wrongdoing and the person who changes the direction of a road are not different people. They are the four legs of the same chair. “I had said earlier that you are the sun. The sun does not need anyone’s permission to rise. The day the sun rises, the rule will belong to every person. “This party has neither money nor s. Therefore, this fight will not be fought through posters, but from house to house. Every house will be an office and every person will be a campaigner. “Invite me to your village or town as well. We will fight this battle together. “I had said earlier that you are the sun. I have opened one window; you open three more windows. Send this video and message to three people and write three words — ‘Not politics, but Janniti.’” Four days ago, she visited Mirzapur for the first time after announcing her entry into politics Earlier, Divya Mittal had reached Mirzapur on Sunday, the first day of Navratri. It was her first visit to the district after announcing her entry into politics. Her supporters gave her a grand welcome. Slogans of “Divya Didi Zindabad” were raised. Women presented her with garlands of roses and showered flowers on her. Divya became emotional when people touched her feet. She told the people, “You have weighed me down with flowers and garlands. This is your love. You make me emotional every time. It feels as if Mirzapur has taken a contract to make me cry. Mirzapur should always keep smiling. No one should cry.” Divya Mittal was Mirzapur DM and had helped bring water to Lahuriyadah Divya Mittal became the District Magistrate of Mirzapur in September 2022. She was discussed for her work involving public outreach programmes and drinking-water initiatives in rural areas. The initiative to provide piped water to Lahuriyadah village was also undertaken during her tenure. Her farewell after she was transferred from Mirzapur also attracted attention. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Later, her tenure in Deoria also made headlines after a dispute over powers between elected representatives and the administration. After resignation was accepted, she wrote — ‘Move forward, move forward’ Former IAS officer Divya had resigned from service on August 30. Her resignation was accepted on September 14. After her resignation was accepted, Divya wrote, “My resignation from the IAS has been accepted.” She also quoted lines from poet Jaishankar Prasad’s play Chandragupta: “Prashast punya panth hai, badhe chalo, badhe chalo.” “Prashast punya panth hai” means that the path of protecting and gaining freedom for the motherland is vast, clear and sacred. “Badhe chalo, badhe chalo” is a call by the poet to the brave sons and soldiers of the country to continue moving forward on this sacred path without stopping or being afraid. Divya left her London job to join the civil services Divya is originally from Rewari in Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she worked in London. She met Gagandeep Singh there. The two had a love marriage. However, after a few years, the couple left their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC examination. She cleared the IPS examination on her first attempt without coaching and was allotted the Gujarat cadre. She continued preparing for the IAS examination even during her IPS training. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya’s husband is from Punjab, cleared UPSC in his first attempt Divya’s husband Gagandeep Singh’s family is from Gidderbaha in Punjab’s Bathinda district. He studied chemical engineering at IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002 and management at IIM Bengaluru from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt in 2010 and was selected for the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned as Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

stories.title: Model accused of murder says Shiva died by suicide:Claims she saw him jump with her own eyes; releases three videos from Nepal in 12 hours
stories.summary: Another video of model Shraddha Dubey, accused in the murder of Lucknow millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma, has emerged. Shraddha, who has fled to Nepal, has released her third video in the past 12 hours. In the video released on Thursday, she says, "It was not murder; it was suicide. I saw him jump with my own eyes." "If the CCTV cameras there are checked, everything will come out. It will show how he jumped. It is not that we are not distressed. At that time, I was in no condition to say anything. My health deteriorated badly because someone from my house attempted suicide, so it was natural for my condition to worsen." 7 October incident This happened on the 7th, when Shiva, through a tea seller in Kapurthala... There is a tea seller at Kapurthala's main crossroads where we used to often have tea. Through him, Shiva had my driver called. Shiva Sharma and I had had no contact for, let us say, six or seven days before the 7th. We had not spoken for five or six days. He had my driver called through the tea seller. During that call, he was crying a lot. Then I called him twice from my number. He did not answer at the time. At 2:00 a.m., I received a call from Shiva. I asked him, "What happened? Why are you crying?" He said, "Where are you?" I replied, "I am standing at Dainik." He came to Dainik in his BMW and met me. He also said on the call-if the call details are obtained, they will show that he said, "Babu, I am coming, okay?" He came and spoke with me. He had drunk a lot of beer, okay? We went to Paddlers Café. At Paddlers Café, he ordered matcha for me and juice and other things for my driver, and got something for himself as well. After that, he went home with me. We drove home as we usually did. He was driving my car, while my driver was driving his car, okay? Reference to his sister's arrival and meeting friends After 7, on 8... Navratri was approaching, and it was on 11. My sister came to my house on 8 to discuss something related to the puja. She came to my house in the morning on 8. My sister has absolutely no connection with this case. She did not even know Shiva well. If her call details are obtained, they will show that she had neither spoken to Shiva nor anything else. She knew very little about Shiva Sharma. My sister... my sister had absolutely nothing to do with it. She had come to my house after so many days, okay? Even when my sister came on the 8th, we continued to relax and everything remained fine. We went out. In the evening, some of Shiva Sharma's friends came, one of whom was named Ashwini Mishra and the other Harsh. If Shiva Sharma had been subjected to any kind of torture or anything else, why did his friends not go to the police and report that he was being tortured? There was no such torture; nothing of the sort happened to Shiva. Shiva and I were happy and were doing very well. I had known Shiva Sharma for only two months; he had been my friend for four months. We had been in a relationship for the past two months, so we knew each other, okay? He... His mother said that he lived with me in a live-in relationship. Sometimes he stayed for 15 days, and sometimes he would disappear for two to four days; that is what he used to do. Five days before I met him, when we were not in contact, he had gone to Kedarnath or somewhere else on a trip with his sister and brother-in-law. Claim of debt and suspicion of suicide I have some screenshots that I will share with you. They clearly show that Shiva had accumulated a huge debt-outstanding loans of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. Whenever he sat with us, calls from creditors would start coming in. If his call records are retrieved-I have sent Shiva Sharma's phone to the police-and everything is checked, they will show that Shiva Sharma was receiving calls from a large number of creditors. He had become so troubled by his debt that he would tell me, "If I am unable to repay the debt, I might even commit suicide." Right? He was extremely distressed, but at the time we were taking what he said lightly. Just think for yourself: why would a girl kill someone and throw them down from her own flat, right? So, my request to the media is: please do not spread such things or circulate such rumours about anyone. I was not in that condition because, while our driver and we were rushing around, her mother arrived there. We called her mother, 112 and 108. Her mother arrived and then began assaulting my driver there, which will have been recorded on the hospital's cameras, all right? Without knowing anything, she directly accused us of murder. I mean, without thinking or finding out the facts, she immediately blamed us for murder. She made such a serious allegation against us that we may never be able to escape that blame for the rest of our lives, all right? Reference to the events of 8 and 9 October So, on the 8th, we... and on the 9th, we remained normal as well. On the 8th, we went out and drove around, going on a long drive. During that time, there were several conversations with Shiva Sharma, her mother, her brother-in-law and her sister. Calls came in in front of me, and conversations took place, all right? Then, on the 9th, he was depressed-I do not know myself what was going on. When we wake up, we have tea served in the drawing room. Shiva went inside to use the washroom, but whenever he went to the washroom, he never closed my main gate. As soon as he closed the main gate, I became suspicious because he had already told me that he had so many debts. I immediately sent my sister to go and check what he was doing. By the time my sister opened the gate, he had jumped from the balcony. It is not as though you have lost your son; I have lost my man too. I am also extremely distressed. Please, I request the media not to harass me, please. You have lost one life, and if you continue to torture me like this, I will kill myself. I really will kill myself.

stories.title: Model Shraddha Dubey escapes police again:Nepal CCTV surfaces; cops suspect insider leak
stories.summary: Police are searching for model Shraddha Dubey, an accused in the murder case of Lucknow resident Shiva Sharma, after she allegedly crossed into Nepal with her sister and a friend. CCTV footage reportedly shows the three heading towards a bus station in Nepal after leaving their SUV near the India-Nepal border. Two videos featuring Shraddha have also surfaced from Nepal, in which she claims to be innocent. Police suspect that she is receiving information about their investigation and movements. Investigators are trying to find out who is helping her evade arrest and how she is getting updates about the police operation. Meanwhile, Shraddha's Instagram followers have increased from around 141,000 to 142,000 since the incident, while the number of accounts she follows has fallen from 421 to 410. Police teams fail to trace her in Sitapur and Lakhimpur Three teams from the Lucknow Police Crime Branch and Hazratganj police station are searching for Shraddha. The teams include an inspector, six sub-inspectors and 16 police personnel. According to the police, when a team reached Sitapur to find her, she had already left. Her location was subsequently traced to Lakhimpur, but the police failed to find her there as well. Investigators believe Shraddha travelled to Rupaidiha on the India-Nepal border with her sister, Rashmi, and friend Adil. Her Scorpio SUV was found abandoned in a private parking area. The three allegedly crossed the border on foot and reached Mahim Nagar in Nepal. CCTV footage reportedly shows Shraddha, Rashmi and Adil crossing a road and entering a bus station. They are believed to have spent the night there before leaving by bus the following morning, before the police team arrived. Who is leaking information about the police operation? Investigators suspect that Shraddha is receiving updates about police movements and the progress of the investigation. According to police sources, screenshots containing information about the reward announced for her arrest and other developments may also have been sent to her. The police are trying to identify those allegedly passing on the information. Action may be taken against them if their involvement is established. The release of two videos while Shraddha remains at large has also raised questions about who is helping her record and circulate the clips. In the videos, she claims to be innocent. The police are investigating how she is obtaining information about the case and whether anyone is helping her evade arrest. Instagram followers increase after the incident Shraddha's Instagram account has also drawn attention since the case came to light. Her follower count reportedly increased from around 141,000 to 142,000, while the number of accounts she follows dropped from 421 to 410. The report suggests that some high-profile accounts may have been blocked or unfollowed. However, it is unclear whether Shraddha herself made these changes. Shraddha's sister Rashmi also remains on the run Rashmi Dubey, Shraddha's sister, is also absconding in connection with the case. According to details emerging during the investigation, Rashmi previously worked at a private bank. She later became interested in social media influencing after seeing her sister's growing popularity, reels and large following. Rashmi began posting more actively on social media. Her Instagram account reportedly features videos of her dressing up and attending late-night parties. The report also describes her as someone who enjoys parties and hookah. See three pictures of Shraddha's sister... What happened in the Shiva Sharma murder case? On 9 October, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments in Lucknow's Hazratganj area. He had reportedly been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the previous four months. According to the report, Shiva was found wearing only underwear, with lipstick on his face and several cigarette burn marks on his body. His mother, Ranjana Sharma, filed a murder complaint against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver, Adil. The family has alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. The allegation is part of the ongoing investigation and has not been established in court. stories.title: Weekly special train to run between Udaipur and Delhi Sarai:Six trips each way from October 21 to November 26 to ease festive rush
stories.summary: To meet the rising demand for train travel during the festive season, the Railway has decided to operate a weekly special train between Udaipur and Delhi Sarai. The special train will make six trips in each direction between 21 October and 26 November. The train will depart from Udaipur at 9:15 p.m. every Wednesday and from Delhi at 1:45 p.m. every Thursday. The operation of this new train will make it much easier for thousands of passengers travelling to and from Delhi from areas around Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Bhilwara, Ajmer and Jaipur to get confirmed tickets during major festivals such as Diwali and Chhath. North Western Railway Chief Public Relations Officer Amit Sudarshan said that train number 09617, the Udaipur City-Delhi Sarai weekly special, would operate from 21 October to 25 November. The train will depart from Udaipur City at 9:15 p.m. every Wednesday and reach Delhi Sarai station at 11:15 a.m. the following day. Special train to operate on the return journey from 22 October On the return journey, train number 09618 Delhi Sarai-Udaipur City Weekly Special will operate from 22 October to 26 November. The train will depart from Delhi Sarai at 1:45 p.m. every Thursday and reach Udaipur City at 4:00 a.m. the following day. The special train will stop at a total of 14 major stations in both directions along the route. These include Mavli, Chanderiya, Bhilwara, Bijainagar, Ajmer, Kishangarh and Phulera. It will also halt at Ringas, Neem Ka Thana, Narnaul, Ateli, Rewari, Gurugram and Delhi Cantt stations. The halt at Ringas will directly benefit devotees travelling to Khatu Shyamji. A total of 22 coaches have been attached to the train for passengers' convenience. It caters to passengers travelling in every class, from AC to general. The train will have two Second AC, six Third AC and two Third AC Economy coaches. In addition, it will have six Sleeper Class and four General Class coaches. It will also include one guard coach and one power car.

stories.title: 31kg of cannabis worth ₹15 lakh hidden in animal feed:One arrested in Varanasi; stock intended for festival supply
stories.summary: The Varanasi Police Commissioner has directed the Varanasi police to crack down on drugs ahead of the festival. Acting on these instructions, Siga Police in Varanasi on Wednesday surrounded the area near the old iron tank in Pachpedwa and arrested a notorious interstate smuggler. The smuggler had brought a consignment of ganja to Varanasi concealed in a vehicle carrying animal feed. It was intended to be sold during the festivals. The 31-kilogram consignment of ganja has been valued at ₹15 lakh. The arrested smuggler, Rajkishore Gaur, is a resident of Buxar, Bihar. He also supplies ganja under the guise of transporting animal feed. He will be sent to jail on Thursday. Siga police lay trap near Pachpedwa Siga Inspector Shivakant Mishra said while revealing details of the case that the police had received information from an informer that a large consignment of prohibited narcotics was being brought into the city in a pickup vehicle for sale. As soon as they received the information, the Siga Police team went on alert and intensified checking near the old iron tank in Pachpedwa. Meanwhile, police signalled a goods-laden pickup vehicle approaching under suspicious circumstances to stop. On seeing the police, the driver tried to flee, but the alert police team cordoned off the area and caught him at the spot. Smuggler from Bihar, cannabis packed in 30 packets Police questioning and investigation revealed that the arrested accused was identified as Rajkishore God. Inspector Shivakant Mishra said the accused, Rajkishore God, was a resident of Nawadera in Bihar's Buxar district. He had been involved in the illegal trade for a long time and supplied narcotics across the border. When police thoroughly searched the seized pickup vehicle, they found 10 sacks of animal feed (cattle feed) loaded inside it. At first glance, it appeared to be an ordinary goods vehicle. However, when police removed the sacks of animal feed and checked underneath, they recovered 30 packets of cannabis hidden there. Weighing revealed that the total quantity of cannabis seized was 31.275 kilograms. New method of smuggling The inspector said that during questioning, the shrewd criminal revealed that he constantly adopted new tactics to evade the police. This time, he used animal feed as a cover to deceive the police. Animal feed has a strong odour of its own, which easily masks the smell of cannabis. The accused hoped that the police would see the sacks of bran and let the vehicle pass without checking it, but his plan failed due to the vigilance of the Sigra police.

stories.title: Passenger arrives at Lucknow airport with gold hidden in underwear:Arrives from Sharjah carrying 472g gold in multiple pouches
stories.summary: Customs officials at Lucknow’s Amausi airport have seized gold worth around Rs 70 lakh from a passenger arriving from Sharjah. On Wednesday, officials noticed the passenger limping and approached him for questioning. He appeared nervous and gave evasive answers. During a search, officials found 472.100 grams of gold in paste form packed inside a plastic pouch and concealed in his underwear. He had tied the pouch around his waist like a waistband to avoid suspicion. The seized gold was valued at Rs 70,81,500. Officials have seized the gold and detained the passenger, identified as Kedar Mahto, a resident of Gopalganj in Bihar. He is being questioned to determine who had instructed him to bring the gold to Lucknow and to whom he was supposed to deliver it. Here is the complete sequence of events: Gold suspected to have been brought in without paying customs duty Officials suspect that the passenger concealed the gold to bring it into the country without paying customs duty. Further investigation is underway to examine other aspects of the case.

stories.title: Cross-examination of witness completed in Gorakhpur:Confirms shop CCTV footage in case involving rape and murder of 10-year-old girl
stories.summary: In the case involving the abduction, rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl from Gorakhpur District Hospital, the defence completed its cross-examination of witness Ashhar Jameel on Wednesday. He proved in court the footage from the CCTV cameras installed at his plywood shop on Bank Road. During the investigation, the police had secured this footage on a pen drive. The defence began its cross-examination after the witness's examination-in-chief was recorded on Tuesday, but it remained incomplete due to a lack of time. The remaining questions and answers were completed on Wednesday. Special Public Prosecutors Raghavendra Tripathi and Ram Milan Singh represented the prosecution in the case. Brijesh Singh, the defence's Chief Legal Aid Defence Counsel, and Deputy Counsel Bhagat Gaur questioned the witness. The court has scheduled 15 October for the next hearing in the case. CCTV footage proved in court Ashhar Jameel, who runs a plywood shop opposite V-Mart on Bank Road, confirmed the CCTV camera footage from his shop in court on Tuesday. The police had preserved the footage on a pen drive during the investigation. According to the prosecution, the footage is important evidence in the investigation of the case. On Wednesday, the defence continued questioning the witness. His cross-examination was completed. Witness questioned for two days Special Public Prosecutors Raghavendra Tripathi and Ram Milan Singh recorded Ashhar Jameel's examination-in-chief on Tuesday. The defence lawyers then began cross-examining him. The entire process could not be completed on Tuesday due to a lack of time. On Wednesday, the defence asked the remaining questions and completed the witness's cross-examination. The next hearing in the case will be held on 15 October. What is the full case? On the night of 28 July, a 10-year-old girl went to Gorakhpur District Hospital to give food to her elder sister, who was admitted there. During this time, the girl suddenly went missing. When her family began searching for her, they learnt that a young man wearing a police uniform had taken her with him. Police then advanced the investigation with the help of CCTV footage and surveillance. The investigation indicated that constable Abhishek Yadav, a resident of Ghazipur and posted with Dial 112, was accused of abducting the girl. Body found along the Rohin River in Rohin on 30 July According to police, during interrogation in custody, the accused confessed to raping and killing the girl. The girl's body was recovered on 30 July along the Rohin River in Chiutaha. After the case came to light, the accused constable was dismissed from service and sent to jail. The hearing in the case is now proceeding in court on the basis of witness statements and evidence.

stories.title: UP weather to change, rain alert in 23 districts:Flood-hit Lucknow still has up to 4 feet of water in lanes; 10 new dengue cases reported
stories.summary: Weather conditions are set to change once again in Uttar Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms, rain and hail over the next 48 hours. Lightning is also likely in several areas. Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist in Varanasi, said, A fresh western disturbance has become active over the hilly regions, while easterly winds are bringing moisture from the Bay of Bengal. Under its influence, the rain system has strengthened over western UP today. Tomorrow, eastern and central UP may receive rain accompanied by strong winds. After that, the weather will clear up. Meanwhile, floods continue to trouble Lucknow. Although the water level in the Gomti has started falling, more than 3 lakh people in the Faizullaganj area remain affected. Homes have remained inundated with 3–4 feet of water for the 19th consecutive day. Boats are still operating in the streets and localities. The risk of dengue is also rising, with 10 new cases reported in the past 24 hours. Water enters more than 40,000 homes The floods have affected thousands of families. According to information, three to four feet of water has entered more than 40,000 homes. As a result, a population of more than 3 lakh people has been affected. With water entering their homes, people are facing a crisis in meeting their everyday needs. In several areas, people are struggling to reach safe locations and arrange essential supplies. Normal movement has been disrupted as roads and lanes are flooded. Several families are trapped in their homes and are also finding it difficult to buy essential supplies. Due to the persistent waterlogging, people are worried about stagnant water, filth and the spread of diseases in their homes.

stories.title: Brother-in-law dies by suicide after sister-in-law’s settlement at panchayat:Shoots himself in head in Sultanpur; she was refusing to live with her husband
stories.summary: In Sultanpur, a brother-in-law shot himself in the head after returning from a panchayat meeting concerning his sister-in-law. At the panchayat meeting in Jaunpur, a settlement had been reached between the sister-in-law's husband and her parental family, but her brother-in-law Digvijay did not agree with the decision. After returning home on Tuesday (13 October), he shot himself in the head with his father's licensed rifle. On Wednesday, his four-year-old son performed his father's last rites. Digvijay had gone to the panchayat meeting alone. His wife said that after returning home, he did not tell her anything about what had happened at the meeting. She said that as soon as her mother called, Digvijay went into the room and shot himself. The incident took place in the Lambhua area, around 37 km from the district headquarters. What exactly happened at the panchayat that left Digvijay upset? Read the full report... Read what happened... Digvijay shot himself with a rifle in Sultanpur on Tuesday evening. He had returned home from his in-laws' house just 10 minutes before the incident. Hearing the sound of the gunshot, his wife ran to the room, where she found her husband writhing on the floor, covered in blood. His wife telephoned the family and informed them about the incident. The family then took the young man to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. At the time of the incident, only the young man's wife and children were at home. On Wednesday evening, his four-year-old son performed his father's last rites. Had 18 bighas of land under cultivation Digvijay Singh (32), son of Lal Pratap Singh, lived in Dhanecch village and worked in agriculture. The family owned 18 bighas of land. Digvijay was the only son of his parents. His father, Lal Pratap Singh, also worked in agriculture but has been paralysed for 10 years. Digvijay married Amrita Singh, a resident of Sunjanganj in Jaunpur, eight years ago. Digvijay and Amrita had three children - Dhruvi (6), Surbhi (5) and their youngest son, Shaurya (4). Two years ago, Digvijay arranged the marriage of his sister-in-law Moni to Ayush, who also lived in the village. Ayush's house is 400 metres from Digvijay's home. Moni and Ayush began arguing soon after their marriage. Had tried several times to broker a reconciliation Initially, Digvijay tried several times to reconcile the two. However, six months ago, Moni left her marital home and returned to her parents' home. Digvijay made several attempts to reason with both sides, but no solution was found. Since Digvijay had arranged the marriage, he convened several village councils in an effort to persuade his sister-in-law to continue living at her marital home. Moni had made it clear that she would not live with Ayush. Ayush, too, had said that he would no longer go to bring Moni back. On Tuesday, Ayush was travelling to Jaunpur to try to reach a settlement. Digvijay also went to his in-laws' home to attend the village council. Both were supposed to travel there from the village, but they went separately. Digvijay was not in favour of brokering a settlement Talks of a settlement between Moni and Ayush began in Jaunpur. Digvijay was no longer in favour of a settlement. He said that after the panchayat and repeated efforts to reason with them had failed, the two should now live separately. When Digvijay refused, his mother-in-law and Ayush abused him. Ayush and Moni agreed to live together. When Digvijay returned home, he was angry. After reaching home, he did not tell his wife anything. He had not even changed his clothes. Just then, his mother-in-law called again from her home. As soon as he answered, Digvijay hurled an abuse and handed the mobile phone to his wife, Amrita. Amrita went to the tractor parked outside the house and began talking on the phone. Shot himself with his father's licensed rifle Digvijay went inside the house and took out his father's licensed rifle. He shot himself in the head. He fell to the ground covered in blood immediately after being shot. His wife rushed inside and raised the alarm. Local residents and family members took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination on Wednesday. On Tuesday night, former BJP MLA Devmani met the family and consoled them. Neighbours said that Digvijay owned around 18 bighas of land and worked as a farmer. Last year, he took out a loan to buy a tractor for farming. He had now begun preparing to repair the house. He was the family's sole breadwinner A villager said that 10 years ago, Digvijay's father, Lal Pratap Singh, shot himself in the leg to frame another villager. He has been paralysed ever since and remains bedridden. Digvijay was the family's sole breadwinner. Cousin Sonu Singh said that Digvijay had arranged his sister-in-law's wedding in this village. After talks in Alaiya village, a settlement was reached to bring the woman back. After returning home from her in-laws' house, he shot himself. I was in the fields when my nephew called. We took him to hospital, but he died. Lambhua CO Hrithik Kapoor said The body was handed over to the family after the post-mortem. No written complaint has been received from the family so far. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Imran says workers sometimes make mistakes amid uproar:SP alliance won’t mean surrender; will contest on respectable number of seats
stories.summary: UP Congress working president Imran Masood has outlined his strategy for the 2027 Assembly elections and his views on the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance soon after taking charge. On the commotion at the party office, he said party workers sometimes make mistakes but stressed that former state president Ajay Rai’s contribution should not be overlooked. On seat-sharing, Masood said the alliance would not amount to surrender and that Congress would contest a respectable number of seats with strength. He also said Rahul Gandhi’s narrative would change Congress’s position in Uttar Pradesh. What role will Imran play in the 2027 elections? Read the full interview… Question: There was some commotion and shoes were thrown when you took charge today. Imran: No, it was not like that. Such things happen among party workers occasionally. Sometimes, a few workers make mistakes. The contribution of our former state president, Ajay Rai, cannot be undermined under any circumstances. He worked very hard to build the party ahead of the last election. Question: Regarding seat-sharing for the 2027 Assembly elections, figures such as 200, 150 and 80 seats have been discussed. Where will the negotiations settle? Imran: Look, the party leadership will decide this, not us. However, we want an agreement that ensures respect for both sides. It should not appear that Congress has completely surrendered. We want a strong alliance and intend to contest the elections together. We will work to form the government in Uttar Pradesh. The atmosphere is very favourable, so I do not think there will be any problem. Question: Has Akhilesh Yadav asked for a list of your candidates? Imran: No, no list has been requested or submitted yet. Discussions will begin now. I think that after the ongoing agitation, we will try to finalise the list in October. Question: If there is no alliance, will Congress contest all 403 seats? Imran: I do not think we need to consider an ‘if’ here. The alliance is in place, so I do not see the need for that question. Question: Congress was reduced to just two seats in 2022. What is the target for 2027? Imran: Look, in politics, you never know who will be reduced to a handful of seats or who will rise. The government in Delhi was in power for 15 years before it fell in a moment. Kejriwal won 67 of the 70 seats. You can never predict these things. It is a game of narratives, and Rahul Gandhi has built a narrative across the country. The entire INDIA alliance stands with him. I do not think Congress is in the same position it was in earlier. Congress is in a very strong position with the 2027 elections in mind. Question: If the alliance wins the election, will you be a candidate for the Deputy Chief Minister’s post? Imran: No, no. I am not a candidate for any post. My job is to strengthen the party and build the organisation, and that is what I will do. I will continue in that role. Question: Does Congress consider you an equal stakeholder in Uttar Pradesh? Imran: Look, if it did not consider me an equal stakeholder, it would not have appointed me working president under these circumstances. This was a courageous and significant decision. Congress does not believe in the politics of merely using Muslims; it believes in taking everyone along. Question: You have been given major responsibilities in UP. What will you focus on first? Imran: The party has given me this position with certain expectations. My first priority is to fulfil those expectations. We need to strengthen the organisation further and work to win as many seats as possible in the coming elections. Question: What role do you expect to play in selecting candidates for the 2027 elections? Imran: I do not know what role the party will assign me. That is for the party to decide. Question: Samajwadi Party fielded only two candidates in the Rajya Sabha elections, one of whom was Dhanraj. What is Congress’s view on this? Imran: That is an internal matter of their party. We cannot interfere in everything. Question: When your party’s candidates contested in Jharkhand, their father was involved, and he won after defeating them… Imran: Look, both you and I know what happened. It is not necessary for me to comment on everything.

stories.title: Owaisi targets 37 Purvanchal seats:AIMIM got just 3% votes in Azamgarh in 2022, without preparation; will SP suffer losses?
stories.summary: After failing to form an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP), Asaduddin Owaisi is now eyeing Muslim-majority constituencies considered SP strongholds. On 11 October, Owaisi met people in Azamgarh. Before this, he had addressed a public meeting in Moradabad. Focusing on Muslim issues in his politics, Owaisi secured 62,831 votes in Azamgarh in 2022. This accounted for 3% of the total votes. At the time, AIMIM did not even have a strong organisational presence in the Azamgarh constituencies. This is why Owaisi has visited Azamgarh ahead of the 2027 elections. He knows that the results in the 5 Azamgarh constituencies where the victory margin was 17,000 votes or less in the 2022 elections could be changed relatively easily. If Muslim voters unite behind his party, the political tide could turn in AIMIM's favour. Owaisi is active not just in Azamgarh but also across 37 constituencies in the neighbouring districts of Jaunpur, Ballia, Ghazipur and Mau. In the 2022 elections, AIMIM fielded candidates in 12 of these 37 constituencies. Nine of these candidates contested against the SP and reduced its winning margins. At the time, AIMIM contested 95 seats in Uttar Pradesh. For 2027, Owaisi is preparing to contest more than 200 seats. He is also preparing to field candidates in these 37 constituencies in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Read this report to understand the possible impact on the 2027 Assembly elections. SP's influence: Won 29 seats in 2022 In the 2022 elections, the SP was in an alliance with the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP). Together, they won 29 of the 37 constituencies across Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Ghazipur and Jaunpur. In 12 of these 37 constituencies, the victory margin was less than 10,000 votes. However, two changes have taken place this time that could pose a challenge for the SP. If the Owaisi factor comes into play, the SP is likely to suffer directly. This is because the Muslim-Yadav combination has been a key winning factor for the SP in eastern Uttar Pradesh. If a section of Muslim voters shifts from the SP to AIMIM, the SP could face difficulties. Let us understand this in greater detail through the example of Azamgarh. Political analyst Rajendra Kumar says AIMIM does not merely want to win seats of its own. Weakening the SP's MY (Muslim-Yadav) equation is also among its objectives. However, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has advised his party spokespersons not to speak openly against AIMIM, as the BJP could benefit from such attacks. Understand why the SP is powerful in Azamgarh and neighbouring districts through the results of the 2022 Assembly elections. AIMIM could change the electoral equation in these constituencies

stories.title: Delivery boy found hanging, sister alleges affair with woman:Phone unlocked using her fingerprint; alleges he was murdered in Varanasi
stories.summary: A delivery boy who was living alone at home in Varanasi was found hanging in his bedroom. On Sunday, his younger sister Ranjana told Dainik Bhaskar at the post-mortem centre that her brother was having an affair with a married woman from the neighbourhood who has two children. She alleged that he was murdered. Shubham’s feet were positioned awkwardly, with one leg hanging towards the floor and the other bent on the bed. Blood was coming from his private parts. There were also scratch marks on his neck. The woman unlocked his mobile phone using her fingerprint and quickly cut the rope to bring down his body. His father, Umesh Prasad Maurya, said, “My son called me on Friday. He said, ‘Papa, I have to go to Bengaluru. I have a ticket for Monday.’ I told him to come to our village, Nevada, and meet me before leaving. I never imagined he would never return. On Saturday, I received a call saying that Shubham’s body had been found hanging.” Neighbour called sister and said her brother was unwell Umesh Prasad Maurya, a native of Nevada in Bihar, has been living for several years in a house he built at Vijayipura Chauraha in Koniya, under the Adampur area of Varanasi. His wife has died. His two daughters, Kalpana and Ranjana, are married and live in Mughalsarai in Chandauli and Varanasi, respectively. His youngest and only son, Shubham Maurya (27), worked as a delivery boy. His younger sister Ranjana said, “I run a boutique and a beauty products shop in Annapurna Nagar Colony in Varanasi. At 3.49 pm on Saturday, a man from the neighbourhood called and said that Shubham was unwell and asked me to come over. I sent my son there.” Sister says rope was not tied like a suicide noose Ranjana said, “A little later, I closed my shop and reached the house. There was a large crowd outside. The door was latched from the outside. When we opened it and went in, Shubham was hanging from a rope in the room. One of his legs was hanging towards the floor, while the other was bent on the bed. Blood was coming from his private parts, and there were scratch marks on his neck. The rope was also not tied in the way someone would normally tie it to hang themselves.” Neighbour unlocked brother’s phone with her thumb Ranjana said Shubham had been living alone at home, as their father had gone to Nevada. “My brother was having an affair with a woman from the neighbourhood. He had been with her for the past five days, and in the evening, his body was found hanging. When we arrived, we tried to unlock his mobile phone, but it would not open because his body had become stiff. When the neighbour came, she unlocked his phone in front of us using her thumb.” She alleged that the same woman cut the rope and brought down the body before the police arrived. Ranjana also said the woman’s husband had run away with another girl and had returned only 10 days earlier. He was now living with his wife. Father says, ‘My son was not weak’ Sitting in a corner of the hospital, Shubham’s father was devastated by the death of his only son. With tears in his eyes, he said, “My son was not weak enough to hang himself. I was in Nevada.” He said his son had called him on Friday and told him that he needed to go to Bengaluru. “He said he had a ticket for 12 October. We had asked him to come home to Nevada on 11 October. I told him to come and meet me before leaving. I never thought this would happen.” Shubham’s father then broke down in tears. He has appealed to the Chief Minister for justice. Adampur Station House Officer Vimal Mishra said the body had been sent for post-mortem and handed over to the family. He said the family had alleged that Shubham was having an affair with the woman and claimed that he had been murdered. Police are examining the deceased’s mobile phone and CCTV footage from the surrounding area. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

Omanakuttan NK, general secretary of the Lord Ayyappa Service Society, lodged a theft complaint at the Gomti Nagar police station on 10 October. He said an unidentified person broke the lock on the temple door, entered the premises and stole the cash kept in the donation box after breaking its lock. ₹5,145 recovered from accused Police registered an FIR in the case and began searching for the accused. On Sunday, acting on a tip-off from an informant, a police team arrested Arslan on the road leading towards the railway line in Vineet Khand-5. ₹5,145 was recovered from him. Police produced the accused in court and sent him to jail. He used to splurge the money During questioning, the accused said he committed thefts to fund his expensive tastes. stories.title: Snake and mongoose fight in Lakhimpur:Mongoose bites cobra’s mouth as snake strikes back with hood; fight lasts 45 minutes
stories.summary: A video of a fight between a cobra and a mongoose in Lakhimpur emerged on Sunday. The two were seen attacking each other in a field. The mongoose clamped the snake's hood in its jaws, causing the snake to writhe. Somehow freeing itself, it began hissing at the mongoose. The mongoose repeatedly evaded its attacks. Each time, the mongoose appeared to overpower the cobra. The snake was badly injured in the mongoose's attack. The struggle between the two continued for about 45 minutes. In the end, the mongoose won and the cobra died. The incident took place at 2 p.m. on Sunday in the South Nighasan Forest Range. Snake-mongoose fight in 3 pictures Villagers recorded the video on their mobile phones Some villagers had gone to collect fodder for animals in a sugarcane field near the road from Ludhauri to Semra Purwa village. During this time, they noticed a cobra and a mongoose fighting. Seeing the two animals clash, the villagers began recording the video on their mobile phones. Mongoose repeatedly attacked the cobra's hood The video shows the mongoose repeatedly attacking the cobra's tail and hood. The cobra kept hissing and trying to protect itself from the mongoose. To escape the mongoose's attacks, the cobra also tried to climb a sugarcane stalk, but the mongoose gave it no opportunity. Mongoose kills cobra in 45 minutes According to eyewitnesses, the cobra was found injured and wrapped around a sugarcane stalk after the fight, which lasted around 45 minutes. The cobra subsequently died. The villagers then began sharing the recordings they had made on their mobile phones.

stories.title: Three-way contest in Bithoor chairman by-election:BJP and Congress field candidates as SP leader runs as an independent; polling on 13 October
stories.summary: Polling for the by-election to the Bithoor Nagar Panchayat chairperson's post will be held on 13 October. There are now three candidates in the contest. The BJP and Congress have fielded their candidates on party symbols, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) has not given any candidate an official party symbol. Adarsh Dwivedi, a leader associated with the SP, is contesting the election as an independent candidate. The seat fell vacant after the death of former Nagar Panchayat chairperson Dr Nirmala Singh. She had served as Nagar Panchayat chairperson for five consecutive terms. At the time of her death in June 2026, around 13 months remained in her term. See three pictures... Son Rana Samrendra Singh also in the electoral fray Dr Nirmala Singh's son, Rana Samarendra Singh, is contesting the by-election for the chairman's post. Her younger son, Abhijeet Singh Sanga, is the MLA from the Bithoor Assembly constituency. Given Dr Nirmala Singh's long political career, the by-election is being considered significant for local politics. The Congress has nominated Pradeep Dwivedi for the chairman's post. Pradeep has been associated with the party for around 30 years. He had also contested the Nagar Panchayat chairman's election held in 2023. Samajwadi Party-linked Adarsh Dwivedi contests as an independent Adarsh Dwivedi is contesting the election as an independent candidate. He is the Kanpur Rural vice-president of the Samajwadi Party's Lohia Vahini. He is also a Samajwadi Party councillor from Ward Number 5, Dhruvnagar, of the Bithoor Nagar Panchayat. The Samajwadi Party has not given him the party's official symbol in this by-election. Adarsh Dwivedi is the nephew of former Bithoor MLA Munindra Shukla. Seven candidates initially filed nominations for the by-election to the post of chairperson of the Bithoor Nagar Panchayat. However, after the electoral process moved forward, only three candidates now remain in the contest. The candidates' fate will be decided after polling on Tuesday. Now, learn about Bithoor Nagar Panchayat... Bithoor Nagar Panchayat has 10 wards and around 10,000 voters. In the 2023 election for the chairperson's post, 12 candidates had entered the fray. So far, seven candidates have filed nominations for this by-election. However, the final number of candidates will become clear only after the deadline for withdrawal of nominations. Dr Nirmala Singh has continuously served as chairperson of Bithoor Nagar Panchayat since 2000. Before her, Surendra Pal Singh, also known as Kaka Ji, was the chairperson here. After his death, the then vice-chairman, Ghasitelal, was made chairman. The 10 wards of Bithoor Nagar Panchayat include Brahmnagar, Subedarnagar, Peshwa Nagar, Maharshi Valmiki Nagar, Tatya Tope Nagar, Dhruv Nagar, Laxmibai Nagar, Mainavati Nagar and Lav-Kush Nagar. By-election polling on 13 October, counting on 15 October The nomination process for the by-election to the post of Bithoor Nagar Panchayat chairman began on 18 September. Nomination papers were filed until 24 September, with a total of seven candidates submitting nominations. The scrutiny of nomination papers was conducted on 25 September. The withdrawal process took place on 28 September. According to the election schedule, polling for the post of Bithoor Nagar Panchayat chairman will be held using ballot papers on 13 October. Voting will take place from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Counting will begin at 8 a.m. on 15 October, after which the election results will be announced.

stories.title: Couple found hanging from the same noose in Unnao:Lovers were cousins; woman had married a year ago
stories.summary: A young man and woman in a relationship died by suicide in Unnao after hanging themselves. They were found hanging from a tree by the same rope. They were related as maternal and paternal cousins. Villagers passing through the orchard saw the bodies hanging and informed the police. A crowd gathered at the scene. The police had both bodies brought down and sent them for post-mortem. They also questioned the villagers. The incident took place at 2 p.m. on Sunday in the Bihar police station area. The girl got married a year ago Babulal Pasi, who lives in Chhattakheda village, has a son, Abhay Kumar (24), and a daughter. Abhay worked at a factory. His paternal aunt's house is in Mahramau village, near his own village. His aunt had five children-three sons and two daughters. Priti (22) was the youngest. Her elder sister is Aarti, and her three brothers are Kuldeep, Sachin and Sandeep. Priti's father is a farmer. Her brother Kuldeep works in a private job in Delhi. Sachin works at a roadside eatery, while Sandeep has a job in Dubai. Abhay and Priti were in a relationship. However, their families got Priti married on 30 November 2025 in Shahtan village, under the jurisdiction of Bighapur police station. Priti had been staying at her parents' home in recent days. At around 10 a.m. on Sunday, Priti and Abhay quietly left their respective homes. In the afternoon, the two reached a mango orchard near a railway crossing in Dhamnikheda village. They spoke to each other for some time and then both hanged themselves. When Priti did not return home for a long time, her family filed a complaint at Purwa police station. Station House Officer Rahul Singh said, “The initial investigation suggests that the two were having an affair. They were related as brother and sister. We have spoken to their family members and villagers. No suicide note was found at the spot. The reason for their deaths is not yet clear.”

stories.title: Two tourists clash in Taj Mahal garden:Dispute over stepping on each other’s feet in a queue leads to a fight
stories.summary: Two groups of tourists got into an argument at Agra's Taj Mahal after one tourist stepped on another's foot while they were standing in a queue. The argument soon turned into a physical fight. The tourists from both groups continued fighting until they reached the restricted garden area of the Taj Mahal. Here, CISF personnel intervened and separated the two sides. Women from both groups also tried to calm the dispute. A video of the incident is rapidly going viral on social media. The incident is said to have occurred at around 3:15 p.m. Tourists had come from Rajasthan, CISF personnel calmed the situation According to CISF personnel Devendra Bhadoria, one tourist's foot stepped on another tourist's foot while they were queuing at the Taj Mahal. This led to a dispute between the two groups. What began as a verbal altercation soon escalated into a scuffle. The tourists from both groups fought their way into the garden. During the incident, women from both sides intervened. After receiving information, CISF personnel also stepped in, separated the two sides and brought the dispute under control. It was reported that both groups comprised tourists from Rajasthan. Two men, one from each side, had clashed during the dispute. The CISF brokered a settlement between the two sides and calmed them down. The presence of tourists in the garden during the incident created a chaotic situation. The incident has drawn attention after a video of the fight emerged.

stories.title: Young man and woman jump from Gomti bridge in Lucknow:Police from two stations launch search as SDRF reaches the spot
stories.summary: A young man and woman jumped into the Gomti river from the Gomti Bridge at Ghaila in Madiyaon, Lucknow, on Sunday evening. According to eyewitnesses, the young man jumped from the bridge first. The woman then took off her slippers and jumped into the river. A crowd gathered on the bridge after the incident. On receiving the information, police arrived and launched a search for both with the help of divers. Woman jumped after the young man According to eyewitnesses, the woman also jumped from the bridge after the young man entered the river. As soon as information about the incident was received, the Madiyaon and Thakurganj police reached the spot. Divers are searching for both in the river with the help of a boat. The young man and woman could not be traced until late evening. Identities still unknown The identities of the young man and woman who jumped into the Gomti have not been established. Police are trying to identify both while also investigating the reason for the incident. Madiyaon Inspector Shivanand Mishra said that the boy's shoe was found on the bridge. He said they suspected that the two had jumped after a quarrel, although their identities have not yet been established. The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) has also reached the spot. Thakurganj police said they had received information that the young woman had jumped from the bridge. A slipper was found at the spot, and a team is working to establish her identity.

stories.title: Security guard arrested for shooting dog in Lucknow:Fired licensed gun; identified through CCTV footage
stories.summary: Police arrested on Sunday the security guard accused of shooting and killing a street dog in Lucknow's Talkatora area. The accused has been identified as 42-year-old Sandeep Kumar Tiwari, a resident of Muneshwarpuran, Badshahkheda. He works as a security guard at Principal Security and Allied Services Private Limited. Police seized the licensed DBBL gun used in the incident, one spent cartridge case, four live cartridges and the arms licence. According to police, a motorcyclist shot the street dog in the Talkatora area on 6 October, killing it. Charu Khare, on behalf of AASRA The Helping Hands Trust, and animal rights activist Anu Bose lodged a complaint at the Talkatora police station in the case. See two pictures... Police traced the accused through CCTV footage Considering the seriousness of the incident, police examined footage from CCTV cameras installed at and around the scene. The routes used by the accused to reach the scene and leave after the incident were investigated. Based on the footage and other evidence, police identified Sandeep Kumar Tiwari. Fired after being chased by dogs During questioning, the accused told the police that on 6 October, while returning home after his night duty, dogs began chasing him. In a fit of anger, he fired his licensed gun. The dog died after being hit by the bullet.

stories.title: Kangana Ranaut calls Yogi her brother in Ayodhya:Visits Ram Lalla, says she will return with family
stories.summary: Bollywood actress and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut arrived in Ayodhya on Sunday. At 1:30 p.m., she paid obeisance at Hanumangarhi and offered prayers to Ramlalla. At the Ram temple, Kangana kept gazing at the idol of Ramlalla. During the visit, Kangana also hinted that she might marry soon. She said, "It now seems that I will have to come here at least once with my family." This was Kangana's third visit to Ayodhya. Before this, she inaugurated a showroom. Kangana said roads had been built in Ayodhya and facilities like those at an airport had been developed. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision is now becoming a reality. Kangana described Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as her brother. She said the people of Ayodhya were benefiting from his service. Ayodhya Dham is becoming famous around the world today. Those who live here are blessed. Kangana arrived in Ayodhya wearing a South Indian outfit; see 2 pictures... Kangana toured the Ram temple for 30 minutes Kangana first visited the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi complex. The temple trust presented her with a Ramnami robe and gave her prasad. She spent around 30 minutes offering prayers and touring the temple. She then paid obeisance at Hanumangarhi. Kangana said, "Ayodhya, the land of Ram Lalla, is sacred. It is always a privilege to come here. Coming here has been an extremely holy and divine experience, which is difficult to put into words." Kangana also praised the grand complex of the Ram temple. She said, "The temple complex is extremely vast and beautiful. Families should spend at least two to three days in Ayodhya to experience spiritual peace and satisfaction. Only then can the divinity of this place be fully felt." She said that she now felt she would have to visit the place with her family at least once. See three more pictures... Kangana on CJP protest: A conspiracy is under way to harass the people of the country A day before arriving in Ayodhya, Kangana Ranaut came to Lucknow. There, she hit out at the CJP's call for a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. She said, "The challenges posed by anti-national elements, terrorist forces and international conspiracies are a serious cause for concern." Kangana alleged that conspiracies were being hatched to harass the country and its citizens under various pretexts. When has Kangana visited Ayodhya?

stories.title: Roadways bus runs over vegetable trader in Kanpur, killing him:Family says police PRV was nearby but failed to take him to hospital in time
stories.summary: A vegetable trader was killed after a speeding Roadways bus hit him in Nawabganj, Kanpur, late on Saturday night. It is alleged that the driver ran over the trader while trying to flee after the collision. After the accident, the injured man lay on the road covered in blood. His family alleged that a police PRV was present nearby, but he was not taken to hospital in time. He was later taken to LLR Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Angered by the incident, the family surrounded the Nawabganj police station and created a commotion. They demanded the bus driver's arrest and compensation. After officials assured them of action, the police registered a case and began searching for the accused driver. The trader was returning home on foot after closing his shop Thirty-five-year-old Sunit Nishad, who lived near the zoo in the Nawabganj police station area, ran a wholesale vegetable business at Amrood Mandi. His family comprises his wife, Kajal; daughter, Kirti; son, Rudransh; mother, Shakuntala; father, Kanhaiyalal; and brothers, Sunil, Sudhir and Amarjeet. According to the deceased's brother Sunil, Sunit was walking home after closing the shop late on Saturday evening. He had reached near a petrol pump behind the road leading to the Ganga Barrage when a speeding roadways bus coming from behind hit him. He fell on the road and suffered serious injuries. The family alleges that instead of stopping to help the injured man, the bus driver tried to flee and ran him over in the process. Sunit lay on the road covered in blood. 'His life could have been saved if he had been taken to hospital in time' The family alleges that a police PRV was present some distance from the scene, but no steps were taken to immediately take the injured man to hospital. They said Sunit's life could have been saved if he had received timely treatment. According to the family, police personnel took Sunit to LLR Hospital at the request of passers-by, where doctors declared him dead. On learning of this, the family became enraged and reached Nawabganj police station, where they staged a protest. The family members demanded the arrest of the accused bus driver, strict action against him and compensation for the family. The commotion outside the police station continued until late at night. ADCP assures action After receiving information about the commotion, ADCP Central Dr Archana Singh reached the spot with police personnel. She spoke to the family members, heard their complaint and assured them of action. The family members then calmed down. Based on the family members' written complaint, the police registered a case and began searching for the accused bus driver. ADCP Central Dr Archana Singh said a case had been registered on the basis of the family members' written complaint. The body was being sent for a post-mortem examination. Further action would be taken based on the post-mortem report and the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Coaching centre owner dies by suicide in Meerut:Found hanging at coaching centre; police launch investigation
stories.summary: A coaching centre operator died by suicide inside his coaching centre in Meerut's Kankarkheda police station area on Sunday. His body was found hanging from a noose. The landlord informed the police after seeing the body. On receiving the information, the police reached the spot, brought the body down and sent it for post-mortem examination before launching an investigation. Ashwani, a resident of DC Enclave in the Kankarkheda police station area, ran a coaching centre in New Sainik Colony's Gali Number 1. He left home for the coaching centre on Sunday and died by suicide after hanging himself there. The landlord informed the police after seeing Ashwini's body hanging from the noose. With the help of local residents, the police brought Ashwini down and took him to Kailash Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. No one was present at the coaching centre at the time of the incident. The reason behind Ashwani's suicide has not yet been ascertained. The police have informed the deceased's family about the incident. As soon as the family learnt of the incident, chaos broke out among its members. The family members have left for the scene, while the police sent the body for a post-mortem examination and are investigating the case.

stories.title: Mirzapur residents shower flowers on Divya Mittal, leaving her emotional:Says ‘no one should cry now’; visits after entering politics for first time
stories.summary: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal reached Mirzapur on Sunday, the first day of Navratri. It was her first visit after announcing her entry into politics. Supporters gave her a rousing welcome as soon as she arrived. As soon as her car stopped, slogans of 'Long live Divya Didi' were raised. Women garlanded her with roses and showered her with flowers. A video of the welcome has also emerged. In it, people can be seen touching her feet. Divya Mittal also appeared emotional during the occasion. Divya told the people, You have weighed me with flowers and garlands. This is your love. You make me emotional every time. It feels as though Mirzapur has taken it upon itself to make me cry. Mirzapur should always keep smiling. No one is allowed to cry. After this, former IAS officer Divya Mittal visited the shrine of Maa Vindhyavasini. She joined ordinary devotees without any VIP protocol and offered prayers after standing in the queue. IAS officer Divya Mittal of the 2013 batch resigned on 30 August. On 29 September, she clarified that she was entering politics. See 4 pictures... Bhaskar poll: People said Divya Mittal should contest from the Samajwadi Party and prepare to fight from Mirzapur Which party should former IAS officer Divya Mittal contest for, and from where? Daily Bhaskar asked its readers two questions on 2 October. The first question was: Which party could give Divya Mittal the greatest success in politics? There were four options: the BJP, the Samajwadi Party, Raja Bhaiya's party and an independent run. The Samajwadi Party was chosen by the highest number of readers, at 30%. In other words, nearly three out of every 10 readers believed that Divya Mittal should enter politics with the Samajwadi Party. The BJP finished second, securing 28% of the votes. The option of contesting as an independent was also chosen by 28% of respondents. Meanwhile, 14% of readers chose the option of backing Raja Bhaiya's party. This means the gap between the SP and BJP was just 2%. The independent option received the same number of votes as the BJP. Interestingly, Divya Mittal has said that instead of joining any party, she would enter politics as the 'voice of the people'. She said she would decide her political path in consultation with the people. Mirzapur's district magistrate and had brought water to Lahuriyadah Divya became Mirzapur's district magistrate in September 2022. She attracted attention there for her work on public outreach meetings and drinking water in rural areas. The initiative to supply piped water to Lahuriyadah village was also undertaken during her tenure. Her departure remained a topic of discussion even after her transfer from Mirzapur. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Her tenure in Deoria also drew attention. A dispute over powers between public representatives and the administration there once again put her in the spotlight. Entered politics after quitting her IAS job Divya, a 2013-batch IAS officer, resigned from her job on 30 August. Her resignation was accepted on 14 September. Speculation about her future plans had been rife ever since. After earning a BTech from IIT Delhi and an MBA from IIM Bengaluru, Divya had taken up a job in London with a package worth lakhs. Divya left her job in London to join the civil services Divya's husband is from Punjab and had cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt

stories.title: Pickup runs over scooter rider in Kanpur:Drags him 200 metres while fleeing; man narrowly escapes death
stories.summary: A pickup truck hit a young man riding a scooter in Kanpur. As it tried to flee, it dragged the scooter rider along for 200 metres. Fortunately, the man narrowly escaped with his life, but the scooter was completely wrecked. The man said, "For a moment, I felt that I would not survive. But by the grace of Mata Rani, my life was saved." CCTV footage of the incident has emerged. The victim reached Ghatampur police station and filed a written complaint. Police are searching for the pickup truck. The accident took place on 10 October on Moosanagar Road. See 2 pictures Stopped at the municipal market to buy some goods Shubham, a resident of Jawahar Nagar West in the Ghatampur police station area, said that he works in Hamirpur. He was returning home on his scooter late on Saturday evening. He stopped at the municipal market on Moosanagar Road to buy some household items. At around 9 p.m., as he turned the scooter to leave, it went under the bonnet of a pickup. Instead of stopping the vehicle, the pickup driver accelerated and dragged him for around 200 metres. I was shouting, "Save me! Save me!" but the pickup driver did not stop the vehicle. During this, the scooter came loose from the pickup. People raised an alarm, but by then the pickup driver had fled the scene with the vehicle. The scooter was damaged in the incident. Fortunately, I survived. The man reached Ghatampur police station late at night, submitted a complaint and demanded action. Ghatampur Inspector Manoj Singh Bhadoria said: We received information. stories.title: Jhansi’s Kali Baba revealed as history-sheeter, arrested:Wore army-style uniform, held divine court; devotees came from abroad
stories.summary: History-sheeter Kali Sarkar Baba, alias Pradeep Shukla, was arrested in Jhansi during a raid on Sunday afternoon. He had been living in a temple in disguise. He wore an army-style uniform and held a divine court, claiming to cure every illness. People from across the country and abroad visited his divine court. He has more than 1 lakh followers on the social media platform Instagram. Kali Sarkar Baba is a resident of Chauhan Thok in Hardoi. Three years ago, the Hardoi court issued a warrant against him after he failed to appear in a case of assault. He had been absconding ever since. Read the full case in detail History-sheeter at Hardoi Kotwali police station Accused, Pradeep Shukla alias Natroj, son of Mayaram Shukla, is a resident of Chauhan Thok in the Kotwali police station area of Hardoi. He is a history-sheeter at the Kotwali police station and has several cases registered against him. In 2014, police arrested him in connection with a robbery case in the Kotwali area and sent him to jail. Later, in 2018, a case of assault was registered against him. The accused was not appearing in court in either case. Court No. 2 in Hardoi, presided over by a Judicial Magistrate, issued a permanent warrant in the robbery case, while the Judicial Magistrate First Class issued one in the assault case. Hardoi police had been searching for him for nearly three years. Changed his name and became a baba Accused Pradeep Shukla fled Hardoi and moved to Jhansi. There, he became a baba at the Kali Sarkar temple in Kuraincha village, under the Mauranipur police station area. He changed his name to Satyanand Shukla alias Kali Sarkar and established himself as a saint. He also began holding Divya Darbars, which started attracting hundreds of people. Hardoi police received information about him some time ago. During the search, the police reached Jhansi and traced his location after an investigation. On Sunday, the Mauranipur and Hardoi police arrested Pradeep Shukla. One lakh followers on Instagram About a year ago, the accused also created an Instagram page under the name Kali Sarkar. It has more than one lakh followers. The accused held Divya Darbars on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, while a separate session for local residents was held on Wednesdays. He claimed to cure every illness and resolve other problems through these sessions.
