stories.title: Son kills mother’s lover for marrying her:Returns from New Zealand, shoots him dead in broad daylight in Rampur; CCTV footage emerges
stories.summary: A 30-year-old trader in Rampur was killed by his step-son along with his paternal aunt's son. The son was upset over his mother's second marriage. The trader's father, Nishan Singh, alleged that his step-sons conspired with their paternal aunt's son to carry out the murder. CCTV footage of the incident has also emerged. At around 5 p.m. on Saturday evening, two attackers who arrived by car opened rapid fire at trader Navjot Singh, who was sitting at his shop. Navjot fell to the ground as soon as he was hit. The attackers then fled in the car. The incident took place in Kumhariya Tah village, under the jurisdiction of Milak Khanam police station, around 40 kilometres from the district headquarters. Navjot's father has filed a complaint with the police against seven accused, including his step-son Avdeep, his brother and his paternal aunt's son Rajandeep. Both step-sons live in New Zealand. Additional SP Anurag Singh said: Navjot's step-son Avdeep carried out the murder along with his paternal cousin Rajandeep. Both are absconding. The police are searching for them. Stepsons were angry over their mother's second marriage Navjot Singh owned a shop called 'Gill Washing Hub' in Kummharia Tah village. His father, Nishan Singh, is a farmer. One sister works in Canada. According to the police's preliminary investigation, Navjot entered into a love marriage with a 40-year-old woman, Kamal Kaur, around a year ago. The woman's first husband had died around three years earlier. Her two sons, Avdeep and Jogango, work in New Zealand. Navjot's father said that both of Navjot's stepsons were opposed to the marriage. They did not want their mother to remarry. According to him, Avdeep had returned from New Zealand just five days earlier. He planned the murder with his cousin Rajandeep, his paternal aunt's son. The father has also said that his daughter-in-law's life is at risk and sought protection for her. Now read what the CCTV footage shows... In the CCTV footage, Navjot can be seen sitting near the counter inside his shop. Another person is also present in the shop. Navjot is standing and talking to him. During this time, a silver Alto car arrives and stops outside the shop. Two people with their faces covered get out of a car. One of them enters the shop carrying a pistol. The person sitting inside runs away and hides. Seeing the weapon, Navjot runs to catch the attacker. During the struggle, the attacker fires at him. The two grapple with each other. Just then, the second attacker comes from behind and opens fire. After being shot, Navjot falls to the ground. The second attacker fires again. Navjot then gets up and runs inside the shop, but collapses there. Both attackers try to fire at him again, but the gun does not discharge. The two then calmly get into the car and flee the scene. Father files complaint against five people, including two stepsons After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and took the injured Navjot to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police are searching for the accused. Station House Officer Naresh Kumar said: The family remained at the police station until around 11 p.m. on Saturday. The trader's father has filed a complaint against seven people, including his stepson.

stories.title: Prayagraj STF officer sought cattle as bribe:Also demanded German Shepherd, ₹35,000 for furniture; corruption case filed
stories.summary: A case has been registered in Hisar, Haryana, against a sub-inspector posted with the Prayagraj STF on corruption charges. Sub-inspector Ranendra Kumar Singh demanded two cows and a German Shepherd dog in exchange for removing the accused's name from a liquor smuggling case. During a phone call, the sub-inspector said, "Give me ₹35,000 to buy a chair and table, and give me a buffalo as well. I will remove your name from the case." The complainant submitted 45 audio recordings of conversations with the sub-inspector and screenshots to the Haryana Anti-Corruption Bureau. The bureau's investigation found the available recordings and other evidence to be genuine. Following this, a case was registered against the sub-inspector in Hisar on 6 October under Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. In fact, a case had been registered against Manveer Singh at Nawabganj Police Station in Prayagraj on 2 September 2023 for allegedly smuggling illicit liquor. The sub-inspector demanded the bribe in exchange for removing his name from this case. Case registered against complainant at Nawabganj police station Complainant Manveer Singh, also known as Mannu, is a resident of Byanakheda village in Haryana's Hisar district. A case was registered against him at Prayagraj's Nawabganj police station on 2 September 2023 on charges of smuggling illegal English liquor. According to police records, Sub-Inspector Ranendra Kumar Singh had filed the complaint in the case. Manveer's name also emerged during the investigation. Manveer alleged that the sub-inspector demanded a cow, buffalo, dog and other items from him in exchange for having his name removed from the case. On 17 February 2026, Manveer lodged a complaint with the Anti-Corruption Bureau, Hisar Range. He also submitted an audio recording of his conversation with the sub-inspector and screenshots. According to the investigation report, in a recording dated 1 February 2026, the sub-inspector asked for ₹35,000 to buy a chair and table by sending a scanner to his mobile phone through another youth. In a second recording, he asked for ₹10,000 to be deposited into the scanner of a youth named Himanshu. Case registered after approval from the DG's office The investigation found that the sub-inspector called Manveer on 1 February and asked him to give him two cows. On 3 February, Manveer sent two cows to the sub-inspector. Manveer also submitted the audio recording to the Anti-Corruption Bureau. On 9 February, the sub-inspector called Manveer again and said, "Send one more cow and one buffalo." After this, your name would be removed from the case. On 15 July, the Hisar division of the Anti-Corruption Bureau sent its investigation report to the office of the Director General of Police, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Haryana, in Panchkula. Approval to register a case was received on 14 August. Based on this approval, a case was registered at the Anti-Corruption Bureau police station in Hisar division on 6 October. Liquor was being transported from Haryana to Bihar According to police records, a case was registered against Manveer Singh at Nawabganj police station in Prayagraj on 2 September 2023 on charges of smuggling illicit liquor. Police records state that Sub-Inspector Ranendra Kumar Singh had filed the complaint in the case. It said that English liquor was being illegally smuggled from Haryana to Bihar. Based on information received from Manveer, the sub-inspector and his team seized the liquor in Nawabganj. Manveer's name later emerged during the investigation. As he was wanted in the case registered at Nawabganj police station in Prayagraj on 2 September 2023, a reward of ₹50,000 was announced for his arrest by the Additional Commissioner of Police, Prayagraj, on 16 July 202. He was subsequently arrested again and sent to jail in August, but was later released on bail. Now, a corruption case has been registered against the sub-inspector in Haryana on allegations that he demanded a bribe in exchange for removing Manveer's name from the same case.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets BJP over men beating girls:Says the party learnt this from Hitler; Brajesh Pathak asks how long he will defame UP
stories.summary: On Sunday, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav shared a video of a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. He claimed that the people treating a daughter in this manner in the video belong to UP. Targeting the BJP, Akhilesh said, “Can these monochrome people, who go around challenging others, not see this video showing how a daughter is being treated? These are people from UP. It is being heard that they reside around Ghaziabad.” Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders have learned from Hitler. He said, "Hitler used to dress up his political workers to take revenge on workers of other political parties. Even during Hitler's era, troopers used to similarly humiliate workers of other political parties and lathi-charge them." The SP chief made these statements in Lucknow. He had arrived at the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre (JPNIC), where he garlanded the statue of Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan on his birth anniversary. The BJP hit back at Akhilesh, asking — "how long will you defame UP?" See 2 pictures… Brajesh Pathak said: UP's image was tarnished during SP rule Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak asked, “How long will Akhilesh Yadav continue to defame Uttar Pradesh? Whenever the Samajwadi Party is in power, the image of Uttar Pradesh deteriorates across the entire country and the world. At that time, a situation like 'One District, One Mafia' gets created.” He added that under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in the Bharatiya Janata Party government, Uttar Pradesh has progressed on every front. Law and order prevail in the state, and the youth of Uttar Pradesh have established their identity not only in the country but also globally on the strength of their working capacity and skills. Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi said that after looking at the caste and religion of the accused, Akhilesh Yadav has now started looking at region as well. He accused Akhilesh of trying to tarnish the state's image by alleging that those misbehaving in Delhi belong to UP. "Akhilesh Yadav is trying to defame the people of UP. 'Boys will be boys, they make mistakes'—this has been the principle of the SP. By making remarks about the youth of UP, Akhilesh has pitted them against himself. Trying to ruin UP's image will prove costly for Akhilesh," Tripathi stated. Nand Kishor Gurjar targets Akhilesh Yadav, says: Look within before pointing fingers The SP shared photos of two young men seen in the video alongside Nand Kishor Gurjar, the BJP MLA from Loni in Ghaziabad. Gurjar hit back at Akhilesh Yadav over this. Nand Kishor Gurjar stated that the SP's social media handle posted his picture along with those of the two youths in an attempt to send a message that the individuals involved in the assault were connected to him. Targeting Akhilesh Yadav, he said that the SP chief should look within before accusing others. Gurjar claimed that Akhilesh's photos have also surfaced alongside controversial figures multiple times in the past. Akhilesh says: Only 40 days left for the government; the public is going to defeat them On the birth anniversary of Jayaprakash Narayan, Akhilesh was able to garland his statue after 3 years. Following his announcement to visit JPNIC, a heavy police force was deployed at JPNIC on Saturday night. On Sunday morning at 11:00 AM, Akhilesh reached JPNIC with party workers. During this time, the presence of police personnel was sparse and the barricades had also been removed. Seeing Akhilesh, the police opened the gate, and he went inside. Although police tried to stop some party workers, they managed to enter as well. Akhilesh garlanded the statue of Jayaprakash Narayan and offered roses. Following this, he said, "People in the government want to sell everything. How many rupees must this have been sold for? The public is going to defeat them in 2027. Change has begun, and now only 40 days remain." Regarding the CM's offer to contest from Ayodhya, the SP chief remarked: Everyone will be swept away by Pawan's (Pawan Pandey's) wind. Arrogant people will not survive. Ask the BJP people—does the CM distribute tickets? He himself has to stand in line. Doesn't he ask for a ticket for himself? He stands in line to ask for tickets for his people too. Prior to this, Akhilesh had garlanded Jayaprakash Narayan's statue at JPNIC in 2023, when he scaled an 8-foot-high gate to enter the center. In 2024 and 2025, the administration did not grant him permission to go inside JPNIC. Akhilesh's 4 major points— 1- JP's movement shook the government of that time Akhilesh Yadav said—"Jayaprakash ji always stood up for the oppressed and downtrodden. The greater the pain, the sooner the change will come. It is because of change itself that we have come this far. JP ji was the father of Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti). His movement shook the government of that time, leading to the formation of the Janata Party government for the first time. "JP ji provided leadership against peak inflation and administrative dictatorship in the country, which brought about change. Driven by socialist values, he gave the call for a Total Revolution advocating economic equality and unity for all. Today, we are following his principles. JP ji fought alongside Gandhiji against the British." 2- A government that harbors fear commits injustice "A government that harbors fear commits injustice. Who doesn't know that the BJP people commit injustice? The job of the Election Commission is to facilitate maximum voting, but they are working to prevent voting in elections. Who doesn't know that the Election Commission facilitated vote theft?" 3- The Chief Election Commissioner should resign voluntarily "The Chief Election Commissioner should resign voluntarily. Everyone has understood the dishonesty of the BJP. Everyone is about to leave. Why did they pay off JPNIC's contractors and take them along? Name any other government that has built a structure like JPNIC. The helipad here is not for those with faint hearts. There is car parking for 1,200 vehicles here. If you compare it to the airport for just one hour, the government could earn 800 crore rupees right from here." 4- They kept the barrage closed, drowning Faizullaganj; then they submerged the Riverfront Akhilesh said—"When I praised the Riverfront, they opened all the gates of the barrage. It was completely submerged. Water reached all the way to the Riverfront and Palassio. Before that, they had kept the barrage closed, so Faizullaganj got flooded. The reality is that there is an ongoing conflict between the Municipal Corporation, the LDA, and the Irrigation Department. The officials of the departments are unable to calculate where the water will flow. Someone else is constructing the embankments in Faizullaganj. An engineer is not designing it—the Chief Minister is designing it. The CM gives the order to open the gates as well, while the Irrigation Department is doing nothing. You tell me, what will happen if the CM starts designing drains and bridges?"

stories.title: Businessman dies after Chinese manjha slices his neck in Varanasi:Returning from Navratri prayers; second kite-string death in UP in 20 hours
stories.summary: A 55-year-old sari trader died after Chinese manjha slit his neck while he was returning from a temple in Varanasi on Sunday (11 Oct) morning. The man fell off his motorcycle onto the road as he began bleeding profusely. A young man who saw him writhing in pain rushed him to a hospital on a motorcycle, but doctors declared him dead. The victim’s younger brother, Sushil Kumar, said his brother had left home around 7 am to visit a temple. While returning, the kite string cut his neck on the Kazzakpura flyover. He had gone to the temple because his son was unwell. Police have sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The incident comes a day after a young man died in Gorakhpur when Chinese manjha slit his neck on Saturday (10 Oct) afternoon. Businessman dies after Chinese manjha cuts his neck while returning from temple Sunil Kumar Gujarati (55), a sari trader from Ashapur, had ridden his motorcycle to Gopal Temple in Chowkambha on Sunday morning to offer prayers. While returning home, a Chinese kite string became entangled around his neck on the Kazzakpura flyover, causing a fatal cut. Vikas Kumar Sonkar, who was passing by with his family, said, “We were returning home via the Kazzakpura Bridge. When we reached the top, Sunil Kumar was lying on the road in a pool of blood. He was writhing in pain, with blood flowing from his throat. I immediately stopped some motorcyclists, and with their help, we took him to Kabirchaura Hospital. However, doctors declared him dead.” Aman Jaiswal said he was out for a walk on the bridge when the incident occurred at around 9 am. “A kite string suddenly got entangled around the neck of Sunil Jaiswal, who was riding a motorcycle. Before we could understand what had happened, he fell to the ground and began writhing in pain. Blood was spurting from his neck. We called the police and immediately took him to the hospital on a motorcycle,” he said. Younger brother says businessman had gone to temple to pray for his ailing son The businessman’s younger brother, Sushil Kumar, said, “My elder brother lived with his family in a separate house in Ashapur and ran a sari business. His son, Yash Gujarati, had been unwell for the past two days, so my brother had gone to the temple to offer prayers.” The accident occurred while he was returning from the temple. Sushil Kumar said the family learnt about the incident when two young men reached Chowkhambha looking for them and informed them that his brother had met with an accident.

stories.title: Model girlfriend first met him at Lucknow club:Mother alleges blackmail, threats and cigarette burns
stories.summary: The mother of a 28-year-old man who died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment in Lucknow has accused his girlfriend, model Shraddha Dubey, of blackmailing and physically abusing him. “My son first met her at a club in Lucknow. As they grew closer, they started dating. She had connections with influential people and used to threaten him because of them. My son got caught up in a case, after which she started blackmailing him. Towards the end, she even burnt him with cigarettes. Several marks were found on his body. She had applied lipstick to his face,” said Ranjana Sharma, the deceased’s mother. Police have registered a case based on Ranjana’s complaint against Shraddha, her sister Rashmi Dubey, a man named Adil and two unidentified people. The allegations are yet to be established. “Anyone would cry after being beaten as badly as my son was. He was beaten so much, and I used to see it every day, but…” Ranjana said. 3 pictures of the accused girlfriend that show her luxurious life: Mother says girlfriend blackmailed him for four months Ranjana said Shraddha had been blackmailing her son for around four months. According to the police investigation, the two met through mutual friends at a club in Gomti Nagar and later began dating. They frequently met at a café in Kisan Bazaar. In September, Shiva reportedly told mutual friends that he was being harassed and blackmailed. Ranjana alleged that Shraddha had burnt her son with cigarettes at several places on his body. She said she objected when the initial panchnama (inquest report) did not mention the alleged cigarette burns. The marks were subsequently shown, according to the report. ‘He was afraid of the influence of powerful people’ Ranjana said she had requested a full-body examination of her son and handed over some of the chats between Shiva and Shraddha to the police. According to the report, the police are investigating claims that Shraddha knew political leaders and senior bureaucrats in Uttar Pradesh, as well as members of the Indian cricket team. Shiva’s mother alleged that Shraddha used these connections to intimidate him. On August 30, Shiva was named as an accused in a firing incident at Tinkle Pink Club in Gomti Nagar. The Special Task Force arrested him in Patna, Bihar, and he was sent to jail. A reward of ₹50,000 had also been announced for information leading to his arrest. Ranjana alleged that Shiva had become afraid of going to jail and that Shraddha took advantage of this fear to pressure him. Police are also investigating the roles of Shraddha and Shiva’s associates in the firing incident, including whether the shooting was arranged to implicate him. This remains under investigation. Audi with secretariat pass reaches apartment after incident A white Audi arrived at the apartment around 15 minutes after the incident, according to the report. A secretariat pass was displayed on the front of the vehicle. Police are gathering details about the car to establish who arrived in it or left in it. Residents who were present at the time reportedly said Shiva was wearing only underwear and had lipstick on his face. His mother said he had left home in a BMW two days before the incident and had been staying away since then. No arrests two days after incident Police have registered a case following the family’s complaint, but no accused had been arrested in the two days after the incident, according to the report. ACP Hazratganj Rajneesh Verma said the accused would be arrested and sent to jail. Police are continuing their investigation.

stories.title: Varanasi bans meat and fish sales for 16 days:Shops remain shut until October 26 after Navratri, ahead of Air Force show
stories.summary: The sale of meat and fish has been banned in Varanasi in two phases during the festive season and ahead of the Indian Air Force's upcoming air show. The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has issued the restrictions, citing religious sentiments and the safety of fighter jets participating in the event. The first phase covers the period of Sharadiya Navratri, when meat, fish and poultry shops across the city will remain closed. In the second phase, restrictions on meat cutting and sales will be enforced around Namo Ghat to reduce the risk of bird strikes involving fighter jets. The civic body has warned that violations will invite fines and legal action. All meat, fish and poultry shops to remain closed until October 19 Dr Vijay Amritraj, Varanasi's veterinary and animal welfare officer, said Sharadiya Navratri begins on October 11. To respect devotees' religious sentiments, all meat, fish and poultry shops across the city have been ordered to remain closed from October 11 to 19. Officials and staff across all municipal zones have been directed to conduct inspections and ensure compliance. Employees found negligent in enforcing the order and shopkeepers violating the restrictions could face fines and legal action. Meat sales banned within 2 km of Kashi Vishwanath Dham Dr Amritraj said restrictions would also remain in force in designated religious areas beyond the Navratri period, citing government orders and a resolution passed by the municipal corporation. Meat sales and animal slaughter are prohibited within 500 metres of religious sites and temples across the city. In addition, the sale, storage and consumption of meat, along with animal slaughter, are prohibited within a 2-km radius of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham. Restrictions within 20–30 km of Namo Ghat until October 26 The upcoming Indian Air Force air show has prompted additional restrictions to reduce the risk of bird strikes involving fighter jets. The administration has prohibited meat cutting and sales within a radius of 20–30 km of Namo Ghat from October 19 to 26. Officials say open-air meat cutting can attract large numbers of birds, including eagles and crows, which could pose a risk to fast-moving fighter aircraft. The main air show is scheduled for October 22, 23 and 25, while October 26 has been kept as a reserve day.

stories.title: Election boycott posters appear on BHU walls:Bhagat Singh Students Morcha demands Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and withdrawal of SIR
stories.summary: The ongoing agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is now being felt at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) as well. While various parties are organising programmes such as burning Gyanesh Kumar's effigy and immersing his ashes, posters calling for an election boycott have also been put up on the walls of BHU. The posters carry slogans in English such as ‘Boycott Elections’, ‘Rollback SIR’ and ‘Rollback CAA-NRC’. The posters were put up by the Bhagat Singh Students Morcha (BSM). The organisation has demanded Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls. See the pictures These slogans are written on the posters The posters pasted on the walls called for a boycott of the elections, the withdrawal of the SIR, and the repeal of the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and the National Register of Citizens (NRC). Appeal to boycott the electoral system According to information released by the organisation, the front is calling for a boycott of the electoral system and urging people to join the revolutionary movement to bring about a New Democratic Revolution in India. The organisation has launched a poster campaign in support of the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and the cancellation of the SIR. Movement against Gyanesh Kumar under way across the country Protests and sit-ins are being held across the country, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

stories.title: Youth dies after kite string slices neck in Gorakhpur:Wife screams for help; raids at 374 shops, 9 arrested
stories.summary: After a young man died in Gorakhpur on Saturday because of Chinese kite string, intensive raids were conducted across the district. During the operation, 374 shops were inspected in all police station areas. Banned kite string was found at nine shops. Police arrested the nine shopkeepers and are taking legal action against them. Police recovered 77 bundles of Chinese kite string from these shops. Raids continued throughout the night in the city's Tiwari­pur, Kotwali and Rajghat police station areas. Funeral held after post-mortem Ramesh Kannaujia, 35, who died after being caught in the banned Chinese kite string, succumbed to excessive blood loss. The post-mortem report confirmed that his windpipe and the main arteries in his neck had been damaged. According to the doctor who conducted the post-mortem, the kite string caused serious injuries to Ramesh's neck, cutting through his windpipe and the main arteries. This led to excessive blood loss and Ramesh's death. After the post-mortem process was completed, the body was handed over to his family. Late The last rites were performed at Rajghat on Saturday evening in a sombre atmosphere in the presence of police. The family was inconsolable throughout. Police officers present at the spot consoled the family and assured them of a fair investigation and legal action against those responsible. Here are the full details of the case A 35-year-old man died in Gorakhpur after Chinese kite string slit his neck. He writhed in agony and died on the road. At 1 p.m. on Saturday, he was riding a moped to a shop when the Chinese kite string became entangled around his neck. He applied the brakes, but by then half his neck had been cut. The man fell onto the road along with his moped. Blood began pouring rapidly from his neck. Passers-by picked him up and took him to the district hospital. Doctors there declared Ramesh Kannaujia dead. As soon as she received the information, the wife reached the district hospital in tears. She insisted on seeing her husband's face. The police initially refused, but later showed it to her. The SP suspended the outpost in-charge. The incident took place in the Tiwariapur police station area of the city. It may be noted that Chinese manjha has been banned in Uttar Pradesh for the past 10 years, but it is still being sold. In February this year, the government had said, If a person dies because of Chinese manjha, it will not be treated as an accident. An FIR for murder will be registered. Young man was the family's sole breadwinner Ramesh Kannaujiya was the only earning member of his household. He worked at a cosmetics shop and earned ₹10,000 to ₹12,000 a month. His family comprised his wife, Punna; nine-year-old daughter Aparna; five-year-old son Aryan; and elderly father, Fakire. Ramesh was also responsible for taking care of his father. His father said that Ramesh had left for the shop on his scooter. Half an hour later, a man arrived and informed them about the accident. The family then reached the hospital, but by then, his son had died. Dr R.D. Raman of the district hospital said, The young man had died before reaching the hospital. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Only after that will it be known how badly his neck had been cut or whether he died from a head injury sustained in the fall. People said - Chinese manjha being sold despite ban Local residents allege that Chinese manjha is being sold covertly at 10 shops despite the ban. They asked who would bear Ramesh's family's expenses and take responsibility for his children. The administration should crack down on the sale of manjha. City SP said - strict action will be taken against those found selling manjha City SP Nimish Patil said, An FIR has been registered in the case. Domingarh outpost in-charge Alok Singh has been suspended. A campaign will be conducted over the next 48 hours to stop the sale and use of Chinese kite string. Strict action will be taken against anyone found selling it. Six major incidents involving Chinese kite string Since when has Chinese kite string been banned in Uttar Pradesh, and why is it dangerous? In 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) banned the purchase, sale, storage and use of nylon or Chinese manjha across the country. Chinese manjha has been banned in Uttar Pradesh ever since. Despite this, many people continue to buy and sell it. This often leads to accidents. It is several times sharper than ordinary manjha and does not break easily. It is many times more abrasive than ordinary manjha. As a result, kite flyers' kites are easily cut. However, it can cause serious injuries if it comes into contact with the hands or feet of people or animals. How is Chinese manjha made, and what is the punishment for making or selling it? Chinese manjha does not come from China. It is also known as plastic manjha. Unlike ordinary manjha, Chinese manjha is not made solely from thread. It is prepared using nylon and metallic powder. The manjha is then sharpened using glass or iron filings. Making or selling manjha, or flying kites with it, can attract a prison sentence of up to five years and a fine of up to ₹1 lakh under Section 15 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. In many cases, bail is not granted either. The shop is also sealed. If the manjha causes someone's death, the punishment can be more severe. Which states have banned Chinese manjha? The sale, storage and use of Chinese manjha have been banned in several states and Union territories across India. The ban has primarily been enforced with human and animal safety, environmental protection, and public health in mind. Chinese manjha has also been banned in Delhi since 2017. Despite this, it continues to be sold openly. State governments in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Assam have also, from time to time, imposed bans on the sale and use of this dangerous manjha.

stories.title: 1,800 unclaimed bodies cremated:Gorakhpur’s ‘Amma’ buried 450 Muslims; caring for abandoned elderly showed her the way
stories.summary: Pushpalata Singh, fondly known as Amma in Gorakhpur, has performed the last rites of more than 1,800 unclaimed bodies so far. Among them, around 450 belonged to the Muslim community, whose bodies she buried in accordance with their religious customs. The 55-year-old has been dedicated to this humanitarian work for the past four years. She initially carried out the service on her own, but the municipal corporation and police administration now assist her. Recently, she also performed the last rites of an identified person whose family could not afford the funeral expenses. The family also had no male member to light the funeral pyre. An incident that changed her life Pushpalata's journey of service began around four years ago when she came across a seriously ill and helpless elderly man lying by the roadside. While others stood by and watched, she took him to her home, arranged medical treatment and cared for him. The elderly man died nearly a year later, but his family could not be traced. Pushpalata then decided to perform his last rites herself. The experience changed her outlook on life and inspired her to ensure that every abandoned person received a dignified farewell, regardless of their circumstances. Challenging conventions, she respects every religion Challenging social conventions, Pushpalata Singh has taken on responsibilities that women are often discouraged from undertaking. She says women visiting cremation grounds or lighting funeral pyres are still viewed as unusual in many parts of society. Defying these conventions, she began carrying bodies on her shoulders and performing the last rites herself. Her service goes beyond barriers of caste and religion. For Hindu deceased, she ensures cremation is carried out according to religious rituals, while Muslim bodies are buried with dignity and respect. Her commitment does not end with the last rites. The following day, she returns to the cremation ground to collect the ashes and immerse them in sacred rivers. ‘Matri Aanchal Seva Sansthan’ offers support to the living Alongside ensuring dignified last rites for the deceased, Pushpalata Singh continues to help vulnerable people who have no one to turn to. She has established an ashram called ‘Matri Aanchal Seva Sansthan’, through which she runs ‘Amma Thali’, a service that provides free meals to poor and hungry people living on the streets. Providing medical assistance to people injured in road accidents and rescuing abandoned animals for treatment have also become part of her daily routine. Extending her commitment to humanity beyond her lifetime, Pushpalata has signed an affidavit pledging to donate her organs and body after death, hoping to help others even when she is no longer alive. Administrative support and Karmaveer Award recognition Pushpalata Singh initially began her humanitarian work alone, without seeking publicity or recognition. When the district administration learnt about her courage and commitment, it joined hands with her to launch the ‘Antim Mamta Abhiyan’. Today, the police and hospital authorities contact her directly whenever they receive information about an unclaimed body. In recognition of her selfless service, Pushpalata was recently honoured with the prestigious Karmaveer Award at a ceremony in Mumbai. She has also received several honours at the local level for her humanitarian efforts.

Gandhi for Gen Z: The Mahatma is suddenly cool again | A documentary by The Hindu
stories.summary: Is Gandhi still relevant to Gen Z? In the summer of 2026, a generation that never studied Mahatma Gandhi sat down at Jantar Mantar, refused to fight back, and unexpectedly rediscovered the power of non-violent resistance. What began as a protest against the NEET paper leak soon raised larger questions about dissent, democracy and the language of political action. As students organised sit-ins, fasts and peaceful demonstrations, echoes of satyagraha surfaced in places where few were consciously looking for Gandhi. From the Cockroach Janata Party’s unconventional movement to grassroots community work led by SEWA, this documentary follows the many ways Gandhian ideas continue to appear in contemporary India. Along the way, it explores the intersections and tensions between Gandhi and Ambedkar, the meaning of civil disobedience in the digital age, and the challenge of practising non-violence in an increasingly polarised society. Featuring Gopalkrishna Gandhi, Ramachandra Guha, Tushar Arun Gandhi, Saurav Das and Mirai Chatterjee, the film brings together historians, activists and organisers to examine Gandhi not as a monument of the past, but as a proposition for the present. This is not a film about what Gandhi said. It is a film about what happens when a new generation unknowingly begins asking the same questions.

stories.title: Yogi targets SP over MLC elections:Says party sold jobs for money and is an 'enemy of education'
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said in Lucknow on Saturday, "Under the previous government, candidates who took the examinations were not selected, while some people joined government jobs after securing appointment letters without even appearing for the examinations. Jobs were obtained by paying money. In one recruitment conducted by the commission, candidates from a single caste were selected for 56 of the 86 SDM posts." The Chief Minister advised BJP office-bearers and workers to remain vigilant during the Legislative Council election. He said, "You are working hard, but you must not become overconfident. Thieves and robbers commit robberies and break-ins only in the dark of night. The opposition will also try to break in. They have accepted defeat, but they will attempt to break in." Yogi said, "A pernicious tendency to put constitutional institutions in the dock has begun. This election should also be a response to it. He said that the election is being held through ballot papers, not EVMs. Voters must deliver the result in favour of justice." The Chief Minister was speaking at the BJP's teacher-graduate voters' conference at the Defence Expo ground in Lucknow. Yogi sought votes for the BJP's graduate candidate, engineer Avanish Kumar Singh, and teacher candidate, Umesh Dwivedi. Polling for 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) seats will be held on 23 October. The main contest for these seats across five graduate and six teacher constituencies is between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party. Before the 2027 Assembly elections, the contest is being seen as a major prestige battle for both parties and an opportunity to test their political strength. Key points from Yogi's speech- 1-People used to get joining letters without taking examinations Under the previous government, candidates who appeared for examinations were not selected, while some people joined jobs with appointment letters without even taking the examinations. Jobs were obtained by paying money. In one recruitment drive conducted by the commission, candidates from the same caste were selected for 56 of the 86 SDM posts. 2- SP gave One District, One Mafia Yogi alleged that the mafia held sway during the Samajwadi Party government and that land was illegally occupied. He said, "The Samajwadi Party gave One District, One Mafia; we gave One District, One Product and One District, One Medical College." The Chief Minister claimed that the BJP government had worked to improve law and order, along with development, the expansion of medical colleges and increasing employment opportunities. 3- Also targeted dynastic and family-based politics The Chief Minister appealed to teacher and graduate voters to reject the politics of family rule and dynastic succession. He said a representative should have the commitment and ability to raise people's problems. Referring to the MLC elections being held through ballot papers, Yogi said voters had the responsibility to ensure that the result favoured justice. He appealed to people to vote cautiously. 4- Cashless treatment for teachers up to ₹5 lakh Yogi said teachers from various categories and their families had been provided cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh annually. He also mentioned insurance cover for Shikshamitras, instructors and cooks. He said facilities such as classrooms, toilets, drinking water, smart classes and digital libraries in schools had been improved under Operation Kayakalp and the NIPUN Bharat campaign. The Chief Minister claimed that the dropout rate in basic education had fallen from 20% to 3%. 5- Claim of 9.5 lakh government jobs in nine and a half years The Chief Minister said the state government had provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh young people over the past nine and a half years. He also mentioned preparations to appoint another one lakh young people. He further claimed that employment opportunities had increased through investment in the private sector and startups.

stories.title: PM Modi to visit Gorakhpur region in November:To inaugurate agriculture university in Kushinagar, address rally
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Gorakhpur region in November. He will inaugurate the agricultural university established in Kushinagar district and address a public meeting held there. The administration and BJP leadership have received information about the Prime Minister's programme, and preparations are being made accordingly. The administration is looking for a venue for the public meeting. Along with the agricultural university, Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for several other development projects. Modi's visit is being considered important in view of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. In a way, it will also mark the beginning of the BJP's election rallies. Work has begun on a strategy to make the Prime Minister's programme a success. There had been considerable discussion for several days about the prime minister inaugurating the agricultural university. His programme in November is almost finalised. An atmosphere will be created in Purvanchal The Prime Minister's visit will create a favourable atmosphere for the BJP in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The public meeting will have a direct impact on Kushinagar, Gorakhpur, Maharajganj and Deoria. Held two months before the notification for the Assembly elections is issued, the event is being considered highly significant from the BJP's perspective. It will have an impact on all 62 Assembly seats in the Gorakhpur region. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath may be joined on the stage by Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party national president Om Prakash Rajbhar and Nishad Party national president Dr Sanjay Nishad. The venue for the public meeting will be finalised soon. Preparations under way to draw a historic crowd Preparations are under way to draw a historic crowd for the Prime Minister's visit. All key office bearers in the Gorakhpur region will be given responsibilities for this. However, from the BJP state president to the regional president, everyone is currently engaged in preparations for the teachers' MLC election. Voting for this election will take place on 23 October. After that, the party's focus will shift to the Prime Minister's programme.

stories.title: Tailor's son tops UP Police exam:Mother stopped father from sending him to work as a labourer; 2 sisters are also in police
stories.summary: Sarang, a resident of Baghpat who topped the UP Police constable examination with 276 out of 300 marks, said his father had asked him to work as a labourer at the age of 13 due to the family’s poverty, but he was allowed to continue his studies after his mother intervened. He said he studied with dedication and scored good marks in high school and intermediate before deciding to join the police after Class 12; although he was also selected for the CISF, he did not join, and he added, “My hard work paid off, and I will now serve while staying in my home state.” The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Sarang’s home to meet him and learn more about his journey. His father stitches clothes at home Sarang's home is in Doghat town, around 42 km from the district headquarters. His mother, Babli Prajapati, is a homemaker, while his father, Lokendra, is a tailor. He stitches clothes at home. He has two elder sisters, Asha and Abha. Asha is with the Uttar Pradesh Police and is posted in Unnao, while his younger sister Abha is with the CISF. She is posted in Kerala. Twenty-year-old Sarang has excelled in his studies from the beginning. Despite the family's weak financial position, he worked hard to pursue his education. Father says-if his wife had not understood, his son would have become a labourer Father Lokendra says, "We were very poor. When my son was 13, I had decided to send him to work at a grocery shop in our neighbourhood. However, after his mother and both sisters persuaded me, I did not stop his education. Sarang subsequently scored 81.5% in high school and 78% in intermediate." Mother says, ‘There was milk at home, but we could not give it to the children’ Sarang's mother, Babli, says they made their children successful by educating them after working hard. She had kept animals at home ever since she got married. However, she could not give her children milk to drink or even tea. The family was raised by selling all the milk. Arranging vegetables for the children's meals was also a major challenge. But she had faith in God. The children's hard work helped the family move forward. May God bless everyone with children like mine. Sarang says he fell in love with the uniform in childhood Sarang says, "I had decided to join the police service. Whenever I saw policemen visiting our village during my childhood, I fell in love with the uniform. I was selected for the ITBP about six months ago. However, I did not join it because I wanted to join the Uttar Pradesh Police. I even left that job because I wanted to be recruited into the police force. My dream has finally come true. Only the medical examination remains now." Stayed away from social media for a year Sarang says, “I stayed away from social media while preparing for the police recruitment examination. That was when I achieved success. I had been away from social media for the past year. Watching social media reels made me feel distracted. I did not want any obstacles in my way. I relied on online courses for my studies. I devoted around 12 hours every day to preparing for the examination. Whenever necessary, I also helped my father with his work.”

stories.title: Truck runs over motorcyclists, killing three:Two nursing students die in Lakhimpur; driver flees, abandoning truck
stories.summary: A truck collided with a motorbike in Lakhimpur Kheri on Saturday afternoon, killing three people, including two nursing students, on the spot. The incident took place on the Bheera-Palia National Highway under Bheera police station. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was so severe that the motorbike became trapped beneath the truck. After the accident, the driver abandoned the truck and fled the scene. On receiving the information, Bheera station house officer Amit Pandey reached the spot with police personnel. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examinations. The deceased included Priyanka (24) and Kranti (18), residents of Botan Purwa in Nighasan. Both were nursing students at Van Beat College of Medical Science in Santgarh, Bheera. The third victim was aged around 32, but his identity could not be established. stories.title: Youth sets himself on fire after pouring petrol:Upset over a road being forcibly built on his land in Jaunpur
stories.summary: In Jaunpur, a young man set himself on fire after pouring petrol over himself in protest against a road being forcibly built on his private land. He ran around with his body on fire. When people saw him, they began filling buckets and tubs with water and throwing it over him. They then used clothes and sacks to put out the fire. He was taken to hospital, where his condition remains critical. The incident took place in Pariyawa village under Line Bazar police station, 12 km from the district headquarters. The young man has been identified as Dinesh Kumar Maurya. A video of him has also surfaced. In it, he alleged that the village head was having a road forcibly built on his land. He said he was beaten when he opposed it. Following the incident, the police stopped the road construction. See the pictures... Here is the full story, in sequence Dinesh Kumar Maurya (35) is a farmer. He lives in the Laukri Maurya settlement in Pariyawa village with his wife, Savita Maurya (32), two daughters, Happy (15) and Lucky (13), his father, Tribhuvan Maurya (55), and his brother's wife, Shivdevi. He owns a total of four biswa of land. A dispute has been ongoing for four years over the construction of a road measuring around 300 metres through this land. According to the video that has emerged, a village council meeting was held on 14 October over the dispute. It was agreed that a 300-metre road would be built. He had also agreed to give half the passage from his share of the land. However, he alleges that on 15 October, the village head forcibly began having a passage built on his land. He claims that no official passage is recorded there in the revenue records or map, although villagers have been using this route for a long time. Dinesh had gone to BHU with his ill sister He had gone to BHU in Varanasi with his ill sister on 15-16 October. During this time, his relatives Gulab Chand Maurya, Dharmraj Maurya, Subedar Maurya and Chandrabhan Maurya called the police and began having a cart track built through the middle of his house. It is alleged that the opposing parties called the police again on Friday. His wife and family members were then subjected to obscene abuse. The mobile phone of children who were recording the incident was snatched and thrown away. According to Dinesh, he left BHU at around 11 pm on Friday and reached home at around 2 am on Saturday. He then complained to the police, but his grievance was not heard. He alleged that, distressed by this, he decided to attempt self-immolation. Poured petrol over himself and set himself on fire Dinesh poured petrol over himself and set himself on fire at around 10 a.m. on Saturday morning. When his family members saw him burning, they poured water over him. They put out the fire using clothes and sacks. He was then taken to hospital, where he is undergoing treatment and remains in critical condition. Police said construction had been stopped on Friday itself Line Bazar police station in-charge Vipin Rai said, "The police are aware of the dispute over the road. Police went to the spot on Friday and stopped the construction work. It is not yet known why the farmer attempted self-immolation. The youth is undergoing treatment at the district hospital." SP City Anant Chandrashekhar said, A person in Pariyawan village attempted to set himself on fire by pouring petrol on himself. The injured man was sent to hospital. He suffered burns over 40 per cent of his body. Police are investigating the matter. Necessary legal action will be taken.

stories.title: SP’s slap controversy puts BJP on edge:Nishads and Thakurs clash, why the party could face challenges in eastern UP
stories.summary: The slap row between two Samajwadi Party leaders in Gorakhpur has heightened the BJP's concerns. The leader who slapped the other belongs to the Thakur community, while the victim is a Nishad. Before the 2027 election, the BJP does not want to risk upsetting either of these communities. Mobilisation along Nishad-versus-Thakur lines has begun in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Both communities are important to the BJP. The incident took place at the Gorakhpur Journalists' Press Club on 3 October. The dispute began over sitting in the front row. Kamlesh Singh, son of ticket aspirant Anshuman Singh, slapped former SP district president Nageena Prasad Sahani. A video of the incident also went viral. Nishad Party president and Cabinet minister in the Yogi government, Dr Sanjay Nishad, linked the incident to an insult to the Nishad community. In response, members of the Kshatriya community began holding meetings. Amid protests and counterattacks, the dispute appears to be spreading from Gorakhpur to other districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. The question now is: how much could the BJP's difficulties increase as the Thakur and Nishad communities come face to face in Purvanchal? If the two communities vote against each other in the Assembly election, who will suffer the most? Read the full report... Sanjay Nishad said, "The hand will be cut off" Ram Nageena Sahani belongs to the Nishad community. Therefore, Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad came out in his support. Addressing a gathering, he told his supporters, "Put up the Nishad Party flag and wield its stick. If anyone threatens us, we will gouge out their eyes. If anyone raises a hand, their hand will be cut off." Thakur community says, ‘A neck for a hand’ Following Sanjay Nishad's statements, meetings began being held in Gorakhpur by members of the Kshatriya community in support of Anshuman Singh. Bansgaon Nagar Panchayat chairperson Vijay Singh, alias Bablu, also responded. During this, objectionable language such as "cutting off the neck instead of the hand" was used. Some members of the Kshatriya community demanded that an FIR be registered against Sanjay Nishad. Samajwadi Party's Rambhual Nishad takes up the fight In response to the Thakur community's meeting on 9 October, Samajwadi Party leader and Sultanpur MP Rambhuaal Nishad took up the cause. He called a mahapanchayat of the Nishad community at the Nishadraaj Temple premises in Rustampur, Gorakhpur district. People from the Nishad community gathered at the mahapanchayat from several districts of Purvanchal. Rambhuaal said that if any candidate from the community of the person who slapped Nagina Prasad Sahni contested an election on behalf of any party, the Nishad community would not vote for that candidate. Why Thakur and Nishad votes matter to the BJP The Thakur community has long wielded political and social influence in Purvanchal. At the same time, the Nishad community has played a key role in the BJP's strategy of bringing non-Yadav OBC communities into its fold. After 2017, the BJP focused on aligning smaller backward communities with itself. The alliance with the Nishad Party further strengthened this equation. The Nishad community's political significance is not limited to Gorakhpur. Its presence in several districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Sant Kabir Nagar, Basti, Deoria, Kushinagar, Mau, Ballia, Ghazipur, Jaunpur and Varanasi, could influence electoral outcomes. According to senior journalist Anand Rai, the challenge before the BJP is to take both the Thakur and Nishad communities along. If the dispute escalates, resentment in one community could unite the other. This could affect not only the BJP but also the strategies of the Samajwadi Party and the Nishad Party. Whenever the Nishad community in Purvanchal has moved away from the BJP, the party has suffered losses. The Nishad community also played a crucial role in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election. In that election, Samajwadi Party candidate Praveen Kumar Nishad, backed by the Nishad Party, defeated the BJP. A no-win situation for the BJP Upper castes, particularly the Thakur community, and non-Yadav OBC communities have played an important role in the BJP's electoral strategy in Purvanchal. The demand to include the Nishad community among the Scheduled Castes has been raised for a long time. This issue has also remained central to Sanjay Nishad's politics. Despite the alliance with the BJP, the demand has not been fulfilled. In such a situation, the dissatisfaction among a section of the Nishad community cannot be viewed solely in connection with the current controversy. If the slap incident and the statements made afterwards are repeatedly raised as an issue of the Nishad community's honour, it could fuel the discontent that already exists. It will now be important to see to what extent Sanjay Nishad turns the issue into a political campaign and what stand the BJP leadership takes on it. With the two communities now facing each other, the BJP finds itself caught between a rock and a hard place. Speaking in support of either side carries the direct risk of angering the other community, which is why the BJP's top leadership is currently maintaining silence on the entire episode. Nishad voters decisive on 42 seats in Purvanchal According to political analysts, the Nishad community plays a decisive role in around 42 of Purvanchal's 124 Assembly seats, where its population ranges from 50,000 to 80,000. 2022 Assembly Elections: The BJP won all 9 seats in Gorakhpur. These included the Nishad-dominated Gorakhpur Rural, Pipraich, Campierganj, Sahjanwa, Chauri Chaura and Bansgaon seats. Lessons from the 2018 by-election: When the Nishad community turned against the BJP in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election, the BJP lost its traditional seat. Sanjay Nishad's son, Praveen Nishad, won the election. Despite the BJP's major victory in 2017, it lost the Chillupar seat. At the time, the Nishad Party was opposed to the BJP. Similarly, the Nishad Party won the Shahganj seat in Jaunpur district in 2022. The party fielded a Thakur candidate there and wrested the seat from the Samajwadi Party. The Nishad Party also won the Gyanpur seat in Bhadohi and the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj, both considered strongholds of the Samajwadi Party. The alliance with the Nishad Party also helped the BJP win several seats in the districts of Deoria, Kushinagar and Sant Kabir Nagar. If the Thakur and Nishad communities mobilise against each other's candidates in the upcoming elections, the BJP may have to completely change its strategy in seats such as Gorakhpur Sadar, Campierganj and Gorakhpur Rural, where the sitting MLAs are currently Thakurs. What is the challenge for the SP? This dispute could also add to the SP's difficulties. The incident took place at the party's own programme, raising questions about organisational discipline. The party expelled Anshuman Singh, sending a message that action would be taken. In addition, the Gorakhpur district and metropolitan units were also dissolved. If resentment over the incident persists among the Nishad community, the BJP and Nishad Party may try to turn it into a political issue. They may allege that the Nishad community is not respected in the Samajwadi Party. The SP will face the challenge of addressing the Nishad community's resentment. The space the party gives to the Nishad and other OBC communities in the selection of candidates could also prove important. However, it is difficult to say at present whether the SP will make any changes to ticket distribution to minimise the impact of the controversy.

stories.title: ₹37 lakh stolen from Lucknow flat in 17 minutes:Thieves break lock and flee with 250g gold, 1.5kg silver and ₹1.5 lakh cash
stories.summary: A flat in Silver Line Apartment near Crown Mall, in Lucknow's BBD police station area, was burgled. After breaking the lock, the thief took jewellery worth lakhs of rupees and cash. At the time of the incident, the flat owner had gone to pick up his son from school, while his wife had gone to the hospital to collect medicine. The thief broke open the lock of an iron cupboard and stole around 250 grams of gold jewellery, 1.5 kilograms of silver jewellery and utensils, along with approximately ₹1.50 lakh in cash. The entire incident was captured on the CCTV camera installed in the flat. Had gone to pick up son from school Siddharth Pandey, originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, lives in the Silver Line Apartment on rent with his wife and three-and-a-half-year-old son. In his complaint to the police, he said that at around 12:15 p.m. on 16 October, he had gone to pick up his son from school. His wife had gone to see a doctor at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital at 11:30 a.m. During this time, no one was at the flat. When Siddharth returned home at around 12:45 p.m., he found the lock on the door broken. On entering, he saw that the door of the iron cupboard had been bent and its locker was open. The belongings were scattered. On checking, he found that gold and silver jewellery and cash were missing. Thief stayed in the house for 17 minutes According to the victim, CCTV footage shows a suspect breaking the lock of the house and entering at 12:24 p.m. He bent the cupboard door, broke its lock, stuffed the belongings into a bag and left at 12:41 p.m. The suspect was wearing a red half-sleeved shirt and black half trousers. He was also carrying a black bag on his shoulder. Suspected the guard and domestic help The victim said that after the incident, he called the guard and neighbours by shouting and informed his wife over the phone. In his complaint, he expressed suspicion that the guard and domestic help were involved in the theft. He said the guard and domestic help knew that the family would be away from home. Police said they were identifying the accused with the help of CCTV footage.

stories.title: Government doctor beaten up for inappropriate touching:Woman raises alarm during ultrasound in Siddharthnagar, draws crowd
stories.summary: People assaulted a government doctor in Siddharthnagar on allegations of inappropriate touching. The doctor is accused of touching a young woman's private parts during an ultrasound examination. When the doctor did not stop despite her protest, the woman raised an alarm and called people over. They then beat up the doctor. The incident took place at Diamond Diagnostic Centre, near the Bansi Kotwali intersection, around 22 kilometres from the district headquarters. The doctor was identified as Dr L.S. Singh, posted at the government hospital in Bansi. A video of the assault surfaced on Friday evening. The incident is reportedly from 13 October. According to police, the two sides have reached a settlement in the matter. First, here is what the video shows In the two-minute-and-six-second video, the doctor is seen sitting on a chair. Several people are slapping him. During this, the young woman continued crying and accusing the doctor of molesting her. Police officers are also seen at the scene in the video, but they were unable to stop the people beating the doctor. Now read the full matter... Dr L.S. Singh is posted as a radiologist at the 50-bed government hospital in Bansi. On 13 October, he went to conduct examinations at a private ultrasound centre named Diamond Diagnostic Centre. Meanwhile, a 20-year-old woman from the area arrived at the centre for an ultrasound examination. At around 2 p.m., it was her turn. She was taken into the ultrasound room. The young woman alleged that during the examination, the doctor began touching her private parts inappropriately. He did not stop even when she protested against his actions. Frightened, the woman began screaming loudly. Hearing the commotion, people standing outside the room came inside. After learning what had happened, they caught the accused doctor and began beating him. Police brokered a compromise between both sides Bansi Kotwali in-charge Mahendra Pratap Chaturvedi said The matter was brought to the police station. Both sides were called in and questioned. After this, they reached a compromise. No one has filed a written complaint. Chief Medical Officer Sanjay Kumar Dohre said- He was not aware of the matter. It is against the rules for a government doctor to practise at a private ultrasound centre. The matter will be investigated. Information will also be sought about the allegations of molestation, and action will be taken.

stories.title: Engineer and father killed in Purvanchal Expressway crash:Family was travelling to Mau for a wedding; wife, daughter and one other injured, CCTV captures accident
stories.summary: An engineer and his father were killed in a road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Azamgarh. His mother, sister and brother were seriously injured. The speeding car suddenly hit the divider, crossed the entire lane and fell by the roadside on the other side. CCTV footage of the accident, which took place at 10 am on Friday, emerged on Saturday. The car was reportedly travelling at 110–120 kmph. The accident occurred near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area, 18 km from the district headquarters. Police reached the spot and took the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab (52) and his father, Khurshid Ahmed (83), dead. Shadab’s wife, Asma Bano (45), daughter Myra (15) and son Adnan Ahmed (9) were injured. Shadab originally belonged to Sultanpur village in the Ghosi police station area of Mau district. He worked as a civil engineer in Delhi and lived with his family in Haji Colony, Jamia Nagar. The accident is suspected to have occurred after the driver briefly dozed off. Family was travelling to attend a relative’s wedding Shadab’s family was travelling by car from Delhi to their native village, Sultanpur, to attend a relative’s wedding. Due to the high speed, the car first hit the divider on the right side, then veered left in the same lane and overturned. Car overturns after hitting divider At around 10 am on Friday, the family’s red car reached the Purvanchal Expressway near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area of Azamgarh district. Near stone marker 216.2 on the expressway, the driver reportedly dozed off. The car lost control within moments due to the driver’s drowsiness. Travelling at high speed, it first hit the divider on the right and then overturned towards the left in the same lane. The impact was so severe that the car was badly damaged. The CCTV footage shows pieces of the car flying through the air. Father and son declared dead at hospital Following the accident, a rescue team from the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) reached the spot and took all the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab and his father, Khurshid Ahmed, dead. Meanwhile, Asma Bano, Mayra and Adnan Ahmed were admitted to a private hospital for treatment. Adnan Ahmed, one of the children, is reported to be in stable condition. The police are investigating the case. Wedding celebrations turn into mourning News of the deaths of Shadab and his father, who were returning to their village from Delhi with their family, sent shockwaves through their relatives. The family was travelling home to attend a wedding, but the accident turned the celebrations into mourning. The village is grieving following the incident.

stories.title: Yogi tells law students, ‘Rule of mafia’ prevailed earlier:Even judges were stopped to let mafia convoys pass
stories.summary: CM Yogi said, without naming Atiq Ahmed, that there had been a mafia figure in Prayagraj against whom no law applied. Whether it was the Chief Minister, the Governor or a judge, nothing mattered. Whenever his convoy went out, it was given passage first. Any land he set foot on became his. Before 2017, there was the 'rule of the mafia', but we removed it from the law book and honestly implemented the 'rule of law'. On Saturday, CM Yogi attended the fifth convocation ceremony of Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University in Lucknow. Justice Vikram Nath, the next Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Arun Bhansali, Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court, and Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay were also present. Justice Vikram Nath said in a light-hearted manner, "CM Yogi had asked me to deliver a speech without reading it, but the Vice-Chancellor has asked me to read the written speech. This time, I will follow the Vice-Chancellor's instructions. The next time I come, I will follow the Chief Minister's instructions and deliver the speech without looking at the paper." Degrees were awarded to 260 students and research scholars at the ceremony. Twenty medals were presented to 17 meritorious students. These included 11 gold, five silver and four bronze medals. The gold medal recipients comprised eight female students and three male students. See the pictures... Now read CM Yogi's key points at the convocation... 1- Every lawyer must speak the truth and follow dharma Yogi said that it was essential for every lawyer to speak the truth, follow dharma and study continuously. He explained the meaning of 'Speak the truth. Practise righteousness. Do not neglect self-study,' which was quoted at the beginning of the vice-chancellor's convocation address. He said this was an important message for lawyers. 2- History will never forget Justice Khanna's dissent Referring to Supreme Court Justice H.R. Khanna's dissent during the Emergency, the Chief Minister said that history had not forgotten his dissent despite the price he paid for it. He said the incident explained the difference between the rule of law and the ruler's law, which operates according to the will of the ruler. 3- Students should embrace Ram, Krishna and Shiva Yogi referred to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia's views on Ram, Krishna and Shiva. He said Lohia had described a mind like Shiva's, a heart like Krishna's and words like Ram's as India's three great ideals. One should learn from Shiva to make decisions in difficult circumstances, from Krishna to show compassion towards the poor, and from Ram to observe propriety. He urged students to adopt these ideals in their lives. 4- A single party secured a full majority in 2014 after 30 years The Chief Minister said the rule of law and the justice system have an important role in building a developed India. Just as winning a case is important, winning the people's trust is also important for the country and the government. He said that on 16 May 2014, a single party secured a full majority after 30 years and Narendra Modi became Prime Minister. After this, the government accelerated the process of reforms. 5- More than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws were repealed Yogi said that more than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws had been repealed. Under the Jan Vishwas Act, minor errors in 183 provisions of 42 laws were decriminalised. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was introduced, and GST was implemented under the "One Nation, One Tax" framework. Article 370 was abrogated in Jammu and Kashmir, and the Nari Shakti Vandan Act was passed. He said reform did not mean merely enacting new laws, but also removing laws that were no longer useful.

stories.title: Five family members found dead at home:Parents and three children found clinging to one another in bed, property dispute reported
stories.summary: Five members of a family a husband, wife and their three children were found dead inside a house in Nangla Shripadham village in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday. The neighbours grew suspicious when the family did not wake up until late in the morning. The door was locked from inside. When they looked through a window, they saw all five lying on the beds. Foam was coming from one person’s mouth. When the police entered the house, the father was found dead on a cot, clinging to his son. On another bed, the mother was found dead, clinging to her younger son and daughter. The deceased have been identified as Mahesh (37), his wife Lalita (35), their sons Laddu (11) and Sakshat (3), and daughter Mishti (7). DCP Shravan Kumar Singh said the exact cause of death would be known after the post-mortem reports. Meanwhile, neighbours alleged that Mahesh frequently quarrelled with his mother over property. They claimed she would say that she would transfer everything in her daughter and son-in-law’s names. The neighbours also alleged that poison had been mixed into the noodles given to the family. The house is 6 km from Jewar Airport and 30 km from the district headquarters. Ate dinner and went to sleep, but never woke up Mahesh’s mother said, “Mahesh and the others ate noodles at around 10 pm on Friday night. Then everyone went to sleep. I was not feeling well, so I did not eat the noodles. Mahesh usually woke up early every morning. When he did not wake up for a long time on Saturday, I became suspicious.” Mahesh’s sister-in-law said, “After my husband died, I was thrown out of the house. I have a 14-year-old daughter, but they did not let her stay with them either. I live in a rented house with her. Mahesh had told me, ‘Sister-in-law, just hang in there for a while. It is only a matter of a few days.’ “My brother-in-law used to say, ‘My brother is gone, but I will not deprive you of your share. I will give you your rightful share in everything.’ My mother-in-law is always fighting for her daughters. My brother-in-law and his wife were very good people. My sisters-in-law should be punished. We should get our rightful share.” See some pictures… Mahesh’s brother-in-law says everything was fine at his sister’s house Based on questioning neighbours, the police said there was a property dispute within the family. Mahesh worked at a company to support his family, which included his mother, wife and children. His three sisters are married. His elder brother died by suicide after jumping in front of a train four years ago. His sister-in-law has since been living separately with her children. Mahesh’s brother-in-law, Sonu, said his mother-in-law’s parental home was in Rabupura. Besides property inherited from her husband, she also received considerable property from her parental family. She had transferred all the property in Delhi, the house in Rabupura and agricultural land into the names of her three daughters. Meanwhile, compensation was received for the agricultural land due to government work. After Mahesh’s marriage in 2017, a house was built in Rabupura using this compensation money. Mahesh began living there with his wife. A year ago, his mother also moved in and subsequently transferred this house to her daughters’ names as well. Sonu said this might have caused stress between his brother-in-law and sister, or someone might have been trying to harm them. Sonu said Mahesh had visited their home with his family 10 days ago, and everything had seemed normal at the time. They had also spoken over the phone two days earlier, but Mahesh had not mentioned any problems or stress. Police are investigating the case from these three angles 1. Food poisoning: The police are pursuing the investigation on the suspicion of food poisoning. However, Food Safety Officer OP Singh said it usually takes five to six hours for the effects of food poisoning to appear. Symptoms such as vomiting and diarrhoea are generally seen, but no such symptoms were observed in this case. 2. Suicide or murder: After it emerged that all the property was in the names of Mahesh’s sisters, the police are also investigating the possibility of suicide. They are trying to determine whether the family was under stress and whether Mahesh poisoned the others before taking his own life. 3. Property dispute: The police are also investigating the property dispute. They are trying to establish whether Mahesh had objected to the property being transferred to others instead of him, and whether someone plotted his murder out of resentment over the dispute. Lalita’s sister Pooja alleges her sister-in-law and her husband orchestrated the murders Lalita’s sister Pooja said, “This is not food poisoning. It is murder. My sister’s sister-in-law and her husband got them killed over a property dispute. They had transferred the properties in Delhi and Bilaspur into their own names.” DCP Shravan Kumar said, Five members of a family died in Rabupura. They had dinner between 10 pm and 10.30 pm. The incident came to light in the morning when a child went to wake them up for an exam. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. We are taking action based on the food they had consumed and other evidence.

stories.title: Delhi-Varanasi special train to run from today:Stops at Lucknow, departs Delhi on October 17 and returns from Varanasi on October 18
stories.summary: In view of the growing rush of passengers during the festive season, Northern Railway will operate a special train between Delhi and Varanasi. The train will depart from Delhi on the night of 17 October and reach Lucknow on the morning of 18 October. On its return journey, it will leave Varanasi on the night of 18 October and reach Lucknow late on the night of 19 October. The train will make one trip in each direction. This will make it easier for passengers from Lucknow to travel between Delhi and Varanasi. Train will reach Lucknow from Delhi at 6:30 am According to Northern Railway Senior DCM Samarth Gupta, train number 04032 Delhi-Varanasi Special Express will depart from Delhi at 9:10 pm on 17 October. The train will reach Lucknow at 6:30 am on 18 October via Ghaziabad, Hapur, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Hardoi. After a halt here, the train will reach Varanasi Junction at 3 pm via Ayodhya Cantt and Jaunpur Junction. Return journey from Varanasi at 8:15 pm On the return journey, train number 04031 Varanasi-Delhi Special Express will depart from Varanasi at 8:15 p.m. on 18 October. Passing through the scheduled stations, the train will reach Lucknow at 2:10 a.m. on 19 October and Delhi at 11:45 a.m. General, sleeper and AC coaches available The special train will have general, sleeper and AC coaches. The train is being operated in view of the additional rush of passengers during the festival, and is expected to provide relief to passengers travelling from Lucknow and other stations along the route.
