stories.summary: Floods continue to wreak havoc in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, the water level of the Gomti river has been rising for the 12th consecutive day. Roads in VIP areas have been submerged, while water has reached neck level in the lanes of Faizullaganj. More than 40,000 houses are over half submerged. Boats are operating on roads, and over 3 lakh people have been affected. The Riverfront has been closed until further orders. The Ghaghara river is in spate in Gonda, with floodwater entering eight villages. More than 7,000 people are stranded in the floods. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda river is eroding its banks. So far, 13 houses and four temples have been washed away into the river. A rain alert has been issued for 30 districts today. Over the past 24 hours, eight cities, including Meerut and Bareilly, witnessed heavy rain accompanied by hailstorms. Atul Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said a western disturbance is active over Uttar Pradesh, leading to the change in weather.

stories.title: Several trains from Lucknow cancelled amid Delhi protest:AC Express, Tejas among services suspended; 7,000 passengers affected
stories.summary: Rail traffic between Lucknow and Delhi has been affected by the proposed demonstration by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday. The Railways has cancelled several trains due to operational reasons and the traffic situation around Delhi's major railway stations. Five trains, including the Lucknow Mail, AC Express and Tejas Express, did not operate on Friday. This caused inconvenience to around 7,000 passengers. Several trains arriving in and departing from Delhi will also remain cancelled on Saturday. Samarth Gupta, Senior DCM of the Northern Railway's Lucknow division, said that 12229 Lucknow Mail, 12429 AC Express and 82501 Tejas Express, which run from Lucknow to New Delhi, remained cancelled on Friday. According to Sumit Kumar, Chief Public Relations Officer of the North Eastern Railway, 12559 Banaras-New Delhi Express and 12581 Banaras-New Delhi Express also did not operate on Friday. These trains will not operate on Saturday Trains cancelled, roadways buses to provide relief Amid train cancellations, roadways buses will remain an option for passengers travelling to Delhi. The Transport Corporation has neither changed the operation of buses running on the Delhi route nor cancelled any bus. Additional buses have been arranged in Noida and Ghaziabad in case the number of passengers increases. Anil Kumar, the Transport Corporation's general manager (operations), said officials in Lucknow, Noida and Ghaziabad had been instructed to ensure proper bus operations and passenger facilities. The number of passengers at the bus stations in all three cities remained normal on Friday. Buses continued to operate every hour on the Delhi route from the Alambagh bus terminal. Additional buses will also be arranged as needed.

stories.title: Lucknow University student detained before leaving for Delhi protest:Picked up from Tagore Lawn, was to join Jantar Mantar demonstration
stories.summary: A video has emerged showing a student of Lucknow University being detained late on Friday evening. Police detained Shubham Kharwar at Tagore Lawn as he was leaving to take part in a protest at Jantar Mantar. He was preparing to travel to Delhi. According to Shubham Kharwar, he was scheduled to travel to Delhi to take part in the protest at Jantar Mantar. Police took him away from Tagore Lawn before he could leave. Meanwhile, several other students of Lucknow University are also under police watch. In view of the protest in Delhi, police in Lucknow also appear to be on alert. Police accused of detaining him before he could leave for Delhi Shubham alleged that police detained him before he could leave for Delhi. He said he was going to take part in the protest. Following the incident, the matter was also discussed among students on the university campus.

stories.title: 18 more trains to stop at Maihar station during Navratri:Temporary halt from October 10 to 22; check train names
stories.summary: Railway has decided to provide 18 trains with temporary five-minute halts at Maihar station to facilitate pilgrims, in view of the fair held in Maihar during Navratri. The rail administration has taken this decision to assist devotees travelling to the fair. These include the Gorakhpur-Pune Express and Gorakhpur-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express originating from Gorakhpur, as well as trains originating from Chhapra, Raxaul, Nautanwa and Ayodhya Cantt. The trains will be halted at Maihar station on different dates between 10 and 22 October. The trains will reach Maihar at their scheduled times and depart after a five-minute halt. This will make it easier for devotees travelling to the Maihar fair to offer prayers. In particular, passengers travelling on long-distance trains will get additional time to board and alight at Maihar station. Trains originating from Gorakhpur will also halt Two trains departing from Gorakhpur have also been given a five-minute temporary halt at Maihar station. The 11056 Express from Gorakhpur to Lokmanya Tilak Terminus will arrive at Maihar station at 8:25 p.m. and depart at 8:30 p.m. from 11 to 21 October. Meanwhile, the 11038 Express from Gorakhpur to Pune will arrive at Maihar station at 4:20 a.m. and depart at 4:25 a.m. from 10 to 17 October. In addition, the 11055 Express from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus to Gorakhpur has been scheduled to arrive at Maihar station at 3:10 a.m. and depart at 3:15 a.m. from 11 to 21 October. The 11037 Express from Pune to Gorakhpur will be given a halt at Maihar station from 11:05 a.m. to 11:10 a.m. on 15 October. Trains travelling towards Chhapra and Bihar will also get the facility Railways has also included trains bound for Chhapra, Muzaffarpur and Raxaul in this arrangement. The 11059 Express from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus to Chhapra will arrive at Maihar station at 3:10 a.m. and depart at 3:15 a.m. from 10 to 20 October. The 12669 Express from Chennai to Chhapra will arrive at Maihar at 8:50 p.m. and depart at 8:55 p.m. from 10 to 19 October. The 15268 Express from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus to Raxaul will arrive at Maihar at 10:40 a.m. from 12 to 19 October. Meanwhile, the 15267 Express from Raxaul to Lokmanya Tilak Terminus will arrive at 11:25 a.m. from 10 to 17 October. The departure of both trains has been scheduled five minutes after their arrival. The 19052 Express from Muzaffarpur to Valsad will arrive at Maihar at 11:40 a.m. and depart at 11:45 a.m. from 12 to 19 October. Similarly, the 19051 Express from Valsad to Muzaffarpur will arrive at 3:05 p.m. and depart at 3:10 p.m. from 10 to 17 October. Trains to Durg, Nautanwa and Ayodhya Cantt will also have a halt The 18201 Express from Durg to Nautanwa will arrive at Maihar at 5:35 a.m. and depart at 5:40 a.m. from 14 to 21 October. The 18202 Express from Nautanwa to Durg will arrive at 1:55 a.m. and depart at 2 a.m. from 11 to 18 October. The 22103 Express from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus to Ayodhya Cantt will arrive at Maihar at 6:45 a.m. and depart at 6:50 a.m. from 12 to 19 October. Meanwhile, the 22104 Express from Ayodhya Cantt to Lokmanya Tilak Terminus will arrive at 8:50 a.m. and depart at 8:55 a.m. from 13 to 20 October. The 19045 Express from Surat to Chhapra will be halted at Maihar station from 2 a.m. to 2:05 a.m. from 11 to 21 October, while the 19040 Express from Chhapra to Surat will be halted there from 10:40 p.m. to 10:45 p.m. during the same period. The 11060 Express from Chhapra to Lokmanya Tilak Terminus will have a scheduled halt from 8:25 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. from 12 to 22 October. Meanwhile, the 12670 Express from Chhapra to Chennai will arrive at 7:25 a.m. and depart at 7:30 a.m. from 12 to 21 October. Railway authorities have appealed to passengers to check their train's scheduled date and time before setting out on their journey.

stories.title: Verdict in Meerut blue drum murder case on October 14:Muskan-Sahil face SC appeal if death penalty denied; Saurabh’s mother begins prayers for justice
stories.summary: A court will deliver its verdict in the sensational Meerut blue-drum murder case on 14 October. Muskan and Sahil will be sentenced by the Meerut district judge's court for the brutal murder of Merchant Navy officer Saurabh Rajput. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra will announce the punishment for Saurabh's wife, Muskan, and her boyfriend, Sahil, who have been convicted of his murder. The sentence could be either the death penalty or life imprisonment. Saurabh's mother has been praying day and night, hoping that her son's killers will be hanged. She has begun a special nine-day religious ritual dedicated to the goddess. Saurabh's mother and brother, Rahul, say they will approach the Supreme Court if Muskan and Sahil are not sentenced to death. They say their fight for justice will end only when both are hanged. Only then, they believe, will Saurabh's soul find peace. A day before the sentencing of Muskan and Sahil, Saurabh's family spoke to Dainik Bhaskar and shared their views. Read what they said… ‘Muskan must be sentenced to death’ Saurabh's mother, Renu Devi, has been making repeated trips to court for the past 15 months. She has personally attended every hearing, following the entire legal process in the hope that her deceased son, Saurabh, would get justice. Renu Devi says both Muskan and Sahil should be sentenced to death because the crime they committed was horrific. It shook society as a whole. She claims that seeing this case has emboldened other women, who have also started killing their husbands in new ways. In such circumstances, the court should set an example by awarding the death penalty to Muskan and Sahil. ‘Only then will Saurabh's soul find peace’ Renu Devi further says that her deceased son, Saurabh, remains restless even today. His soul will find peace only when Muskan, the wife who killed him, is hanged. She also demands that Sahil be sent to the gallows. ‘We will continue our fight for justice’ Renu says she has complete faith in the court and believes the law will support her family. The guilty must not be spared. If Muskan and Sahil are not sentenced to death, the family will approach higher courts. She says they will not remain silent and will continue to seek justice. They will fight their case in the High Court and then the Supreme Court to ensure that Muskan and Sahil are hanged. The family will repeatedly appeal to the courts to award the killers the strictest possible punishment. ‘The family will not keep Muskan's daughter’ Saurabh's elder brother, Rahul alias Bablu, spoke about Muskan's daughters. He said the elder daughter, Pihu, lives with her maternal grandparents, who have looked after her since the beginning. They do not even allow Saurabh's family to meet her. The younger child was born while Muskan was in jail. Rahul claims that she is Sahil's daughter, not Saurabh's. He asks why the family should take responsibility for a child who is not Saurabh's daughter. He says they are not concerned about what happens to the child. If Muskan is sentenced to death, they cannot do anything about where her daughter lives. Now, read what Muskan's family has to say… ‘Muskan should be punished for what she did’ Muskan's father, Pramod Rastogi, told Dainik Bhaskar over the phone that the family did not want to make any statement on camera. He said they had nothing to do with Muskan and that she had died for them the day she murdered Saurabh. The family is trying to put its life back on track. He said they had not visited Muskan even once and would never visit her in jail or meet her outside. They were also not concerned about the child staying with her in jail. He said the child was Sahil's daughter and that Muskan could keep her or do whatever she wanted. Pramod Rastogi said the elder daughter, Pihu, would continue to live with them because she was Saurabh's daughter. She had lived with them since birth, and they would always keep her with them. However, he said the family would never fight a legal battle on Muskan's behalf. Read how Saurabh Rajput was murdered - Former Merchant Navy officer Saurabh Kumar Rajput, who had returned to Meerut from London, was murdered by his wife, Muskan Rastogi, on March 3, 2025. Her boyfriend, Sahil Shukla alias Mohit, helped her commit the crime. They first mixed medicine into Saurabh's food to render him unconscious. While he was asleep in the bedroom, Muskan herself stabbed him in the chest for the first time. - After his death, they took the body to the bathroom, where Sahil severed both hands and the head from the torso. They put the body parts into a plastic drum to dispose of them and filled it with a cement mixture. To mislead family members and neighbours, Muskan went to Shimla and Manali. - For 13 days, she continued uploading photos and videos on Instagram to make people believe that they were travelling together. The murder came to light on March 18, when Saurabh's younger brother, Rahul, reached his brother's house. He saw Muskan with a man, Sahil. When he asked about his brother, Muskan could not give a convincing answer. A foul smell was also coming from inside the house. Rahul raised an alarm, and neighbours gathered. When the police arrived, they discovered the murder. During police custody, Muskan and Sahil reportedly narrated the entire sequence of events.

stories.title: No law against Chinese manjha despite govt promise:Why police cannot charge murder, and how to save lives
stories.summary: October 10, 2026: Ramesh Kanojia, 35, died in Gorakhpur after Chinese manjha slit his throat. The next day, Sunil Gujarati died in a similar incident in Varanasi. In both cases, police registered cases of culpable homicide against unidentified persons. Now, let’s go back eight months… February 2026: Mohammed Shoaib, 33, died in Lucknow after Chinese manjha got caught around his neck. Less than 24 hours later, retired soldier Brijesh Rai suffered a 10-inch-long wound on his face caused by manjha in Lucknow itself. He received 30 stitches. Fortunately, he survived. Following these accidents, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath lashed out at officials. He asked how Chinese manjha was still being sold despite the ban. He directed officials to treat deaths caused by Chinese manjha as murder. Even after this, people continue to die from Chinese manjha regularly. The Uttar Pradesh government has already promised the Allahabad High Court that it will enact a separate law on Chinese manjha, but this has not happened yet. The question now is: Why has the sale of Chinese manjha not stopped? Why are murder cases not being registered in such incidents? Read on in UP Explainer… Question 1: Why is Chinese manjha deadly? Answer: Chinese manjha is actually synthetic manjha. Its name has led people to believe that it is manufactured in China. However, it is made in India using monofilament nylon, the same material used to make fishing nets. This is what makes it extremely dangerous. Traditional Indian manjha uses cotton thread, which breaks when subjected to a sudden jerk. Nylon thread, however, stretches instead of breaking. If someone gets caught in it, it can cut deep into their body. To make Chinese manjha sharper, powdered glass, aluminium or iron filings are mixed with adhesive and applied to the thread. The glass coating makes the manjha almost invisible in the air. It acts like a surgical blade against motorcyclists and birds. If it gets caught in electrical wires, the metal powder can cause it to conduct electricity. Question 2: How is Chinese manjha sold while evading the police? Answer: To avoid detection by the police, Chinese manjha is hidden in grocery shops, bangle shops and scrap warehouses instead of kite shops. Wholesalers sell it only to trusted customers or people they know. Retailers use code words such as Monokite, Cobra and Tangs for it. Some suppliers upload short videos on Instagram or Facebook showing the manjha cutting apples and vegetables. These videos also include WhatsApp numbers for placing orders. Chinese manjha is completely blocked on online shopping sites such as Amazon and Flipkart. Sellers get around this by listing it as nylon thread, fishing-net wire or strong sewing thread. Buyers recognise it from the photographs and place orders. In major cities, sellers use quick-delivery apps that deliver products within 8–10 minutes, as well as local courier services, to deliver the manjha directly to customers’ homes. Question 3: Why are shopkeepers selling it and kite flyers buying it? Answer: The cost of producing Chinese manjha is much lower than that of ordinary manjha. However, because it is banned, it sells at high prices. People take the risk because of the prospect of hefty profits. It is secretly transported from one state to another through courier services and large transport consignments. In cities such as Lucknow, Bareilly and Meerut, people compete in kite-flying contests involving bets. Instead of being held openly in large grounds, these contests often take place on rooftops in residential neighbourhoods. Kite flyers use Chinese manjha to improve their chances of winning by making it harder for their kites to be cut. Question 4: Why are cases of culpable homicide being registered after deaths caused by manjha? Answer: There are several legal aspects behind this: Under Indian criminal law (BNS/IPC), establishing murder requires proving the accused’s intention to kill. A shopkeeper selling Chinese manjha or a person flying a kite generally has no direct intention to kill an unknown motorcyclist. Nor is any personal enmity established. In such circumstances, a court may reject a murder charge. Those selling or flying kites with Chinese manjha know that it is banned. Yet they continue to sell and use it. The law provides that knowingly engaging in a dangerous act that is likely to cause death may fall under culpable homicide (Section 105 of the BNS/Section 304 of the IPC), rather than murder (Section 103 of the BNS/Section 302 of the IPC). Courts across the country have taken a clear position on this technical legal issue. Several courts, including the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Jabalpur, have directed that deaths caused by Chinese manjha should be prosecuted under Section 106(1) of the BNS (causing death by negligence) or Section 105 (culpable homicide). In such cases, the police and government may register a murder FIR to send a strong message. However, if there is insufficient evidence when the chargesheet is filed or during the trial, the case may be converted to culpable homicide. This is why murder charges are not generally included in the FIR. Question 5: What can the government do to ensure that such deaths are treated as murder? Answer: A separate law would need to be enacted for this. In July 2026, the Uttar Pradesh government told the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court that it would frame a separate law on Chinese manjha. The process is under way. Since proving murder without specific intent is difficult, the law should include provisions such as these: The law should explicitly state that anyone who sells, manufactures or uses Chinese manjha is presumed to be fully aware of its potentially fatal consequences and to have intended to cause serious harm to human life. This would mean the police would not have to separately establish a clear motive for murder in court. The offence should be placed in the category of strict liability. This means the accused could not simply argue, “I did not intentionally kill anyone” or “It was just an accident”. Once it is established that the accused possessed or sold Chinese manjha, they would be held legally responsible for deaths caused by it. A sub-section should be added to the law stating that any death caused by Chinese manjha will be treated as equivalent to murder under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), with punishment under the same section. This would prevent courts from treating such deaths as a less serious offence, such as death caused by negligence, and imposing lighter sentences. Accountability must also be enforced strictly. Manufacturers and wholesalers of Chinese manjha should be treated as the principal conspirators. If someone dies because of the manjha they supplied, there should be a provision to prosecute them as co-accused in a murder case and impose a life sentence. Question 6: How many people have been convicted in such cases in UP so far? Answer: In November 2015, while hearing a public interest litigation, the Allahabad High Court directed the state government to ban Chinese manjha. The Uttar Pradesh government subsequently imposed a complete ban in 2016. In July 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) imposed a nationwide ban on Chinese manjha, citing the damage it causes to the environment and birds. Cases for selling or using Chinese manjha are registered under Section 15 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The provision allows for imprisonment of up to five years, a fine of up to ₹1 lakh, or both. In most deaths caused by Chinese manjha, cases of culpable homicide are registered against unidentified persons because the source of the manjha is unknown. If a suspect is subsequently identified and convicted of culpable homicide, they may face a sentence of up to 10 years. As far as convictions are concerned, there are no verified official government figures showing that a trial has been completed and a sentence handed down in any such case so far. In most cases, proceedings remain pending in court or action is limited to the police level. Three days ago, following the death of a young man in Gorakhpur, police recovered 77 bundles of manjha and arrested nine shopkeepers. Alok Singh, the officer in charge of the Domingarh police outpost, was suspended. These are instances of arrests and suspension, not convictions. After Mohammed Shoaib’s death in February 2026, Lucknow Police raided kite and manjha shops and arrested two men for possessing the banned thread. However, the police could not establish whose manjha had caused the incident among those flying kites in an open area. Identifying the accused and gathering solid evidence against them remain major challenges in prosecuting such cases as murder. Cases against sellers of Chinese manjha are ongoing. Question 7: How can ordinary people protect themselves on the road? Answer: Chinese manjha is so thin and transparent that it is difficult to see while riding a motorcycle. Ordinary road users, especially two-wheeler riders, should take the following precautions: Wrap a thick muffler, scarf or towel around your neck. If possible, wear a leather or thick-fabric neck guard. This will prevent the manjha from coming into direct contact with the skin. Always wear a helmet that also covers the upper part of the neck. Keep the helmet visor down while riding to prevent the manjha from striking your eyes or face. Install a metal wire or guard at the front of the motorcycle, fitted near the handlebars. It deflects any thread coming towards the bike upwards, preventing it from reaching the rider’s neck directly. Some time ago, Hyderabad Traffic Police ran a campaign in the city to have such guards installed.

stories.title: Modi to launch campaign from Chaudhary Charan Singh’s village:Focus on farmers; can it influence 126 West UP seats?
stories.summary: The BJP and the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) are set to sound the poll bugle for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections from Hapur. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Purpur Madhiya village in Hapur, the native village of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, on December 23. Jayant Chaudhary will also be present. The BJP and RLD will hold a major public meeting on Chaudhary Charan Singh’s birth anniversary. The NDA alliance will attempt to bring together farmers, the Jat-Gujjar equations and Chaudhary Charan Singh’s legacy on one platform. The political message is clear: All communities in western UP are with the BJP-RLD alliance, while Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA equation has failed. In the previous Assembly elections, the RLD was not in an alliance with the BJP. It contested the elections in alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) and won eight seats. Just before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the RLD became part of the NDA alliance. The BJP is now preparing to build a saffron wave in Jat- and Gujjar-dominated constituencies in western UP. Read the full report… BJP-RLD to consolidate the Jat-Gujjar equation across 126 seats Around 126 Assembly seats in western UP are considered important for the BJP-RLD alliance. The Jat and Gujjar communities influence electoral outcomes in several constituencies in this region. Prime Minister Modi’s public meeting alongside the RLD is expected to be a major show of strength. According to RLD state general secretary Atir Rizvi, the Prime Minister’s Office has given its approval for the December 23 programme. Jayant Chaudhary has also invited Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, BJP president Nitin Nabin, state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary and leaders from western UP. The organisation is deciding the venue for the public meeting. An estimated 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh people are expected to attend the event. The question being raised is why Prime Minister Modi is beginning the election campaign from western UP. Political observers say SP president Akhilesh Yadav has recently been trying to expand his reach among the Gujjar community. Events in Dadri related to Gujjar emperor Mihir Bhoj, along with the issue surrounding his statue, are considered part of this political effort. Against this backdrop, the event on Chaudhary Charan Singh’s birth anniversary will be an attempt by the BJP-RLD alliance to keep its core voters united in western UP. Jayant to showcase NDA unity against SP’s PDA Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says the BJP-RLD alliance’s first major public meeting by Modi for the UP elections will be significant. He identifies three key aspects of the alliance’s strategy. First: To reach farmers by invoking Chaudhary Charan Singh’s legacy and convey that only the BJP can resolve farmers’ problems. Second: To maintain the acceptance of the BJP-RLD alliance among Jats and Gujjars in western UP, as these communities influence around 108 to 120 seats. Third: To showcase NDA unity against the SP’s PDA equation. However, the NDA alliance will also face challenges related to seat-sharing, claims by local leaders and candidate selection. How the RLD strengthened its position in western UP over two elections 2017 Assembly elections: The BJP won 312 seats in Uttar Pradesh, including 100 of the 126 seats in western UP. This accounted for around 79% of the seats in the region. The RLD won only one seat, Chhaprauli. Sahendra Singh Ramala became the MLA from this Jat-dominated constituency. However, he later joined the BJP, leaving the RLD with no representation in the Assembly. 2022 Assembly elections: To challenge the BJP’s stronghold, the SP formed an alliance with RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary. The RLD fielded candidates in 33 of western UP’s 126 seats. The SP-RLD alliance won 41 seats, with eight MLAs elected from the RLD. The BJP’s tally fell from 100 to 85 seats, and its success rate dropped from 79% to 67%. By-elections were held in the Khatauli Assembly constituency in Muzaffarnagar on December 5, 2022, with the results announced on December 8. RLD candidate Madan Bhaiya, backed by the SP, defeated BJP candidate Rajkumari Saini by more than 22,000 votes. With this victory, the number of RLD MLAs in the Assembly rose to nine in 2022. The Khatauli by-election was necessitated after BJP MLA Vikram Singh Saini was disqualified. In October 2022, a special MP/MLA court in Muzaffarnagar sentenced him to two years in prison in a case related to the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots. RLD left the SP after not getting the seats it wanted Just before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the RLD parted ways with the SP. There were two main reasons behind the breakdown of the alliance. First: There was a deadlock over the number of seats the SP would give the RLD and the selection of candidates. Second: The Union government decided to confer the Bharat Ratna posthumously on former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh. After this historic decision, Jayant Chaudhary said the government had not only honoured his grandfather but had also honoured crores of farmers. Following this, he could not refuse the alliance. After joining the NDA, the RLD won both the Baghpat and Bijnor seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Who stands to benefit from Akhilesh’s ‘chavanni’ remark in western UP? The controversy in western UP politics began after a remark made by Akhilesh Yadav around a month ago, in which he took a dig at Jayant Chaudhary, saying, “We turned a 25-paise coin into a rupee, yet he still left us.” The RLD is using the remark against Jayant as an issue of political and social respect in western UP. Jayant Chaudhary has also responded to Akhilesh Yadav. Jayant said he always tries to ensure that no one becomes his enemy. He added that he had not provoked Akhilesh, yet the SP chief continued making statements against him. At a Swabhiman rally in Saharanpur around a month ago, Jayant played videos of SP leaders on stage. Taking a political dig, he said, “Leave ABCD politics aside. We will trap you in G for sugarcane and J for Jat, and then the SP will not return to power.” His wife, Charu Chaudhary, also addressed the rally. Responding to Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks, she said no one had the right to insult, lecture or tell others what to do. Taking a dig at Akhilesh Yadav, she said such remarks reflected the mindset and arrogance of the person making them. In a democracy, it is the people who decide which party forms the government and who comes to or leaves power. If the RLD succeeds in building an anti-SP sentiment among farmers, the BJP-RLD alliance could benefit in terms of seats.

stories.title: Leopard carries away 7-year-old girl in Lakhimpur:Father chases it screaming; daughter’s torn clothes found 200 metres away
stories.summary: A leopard carried away a seven-year-old girl in Lakhimpur Kheri on Monday night. The girl was playing in the courtyard of her home when the leopard attacked her. After hearing his daughter's screams, the father chased the leopard for around 200 metres, but it entered a sugarcane field in the darkness. Villagers searched for the girl, but she could not be found. Her clothes were found in the field. Villagers are angry that the Forest Department team had not arrived even four hours after the incident. The incident took place at 8 p.m. in Bojhiya village in the Dhaurahara forest range, 75 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures... Now read the full case in sequence... Sampat Giri (50), a resident of Bhojiya village, works in agriculture. His family includes two children, Saniya and her twin brother Vikas. Their mother died around seven years ago. Sampat said he returned home from Gajiyapur market at around 7 p.m. on Monday evening. He had brought a banana for his daughter Saniya. After reaching home, he began doing some work. Meanwhile, Saniya was playing in the courtyard, while her twin brother Vikas was inside the house. Suddenly, a leopard entered the house and began carrying Saniya away in its jaws. Father returned with his daughter's clothes Hearing his daughter's screams, Sampat ran after her. He chased the leopard for around 200 metres and tried to rescue his daughter, but the leopard entered a sugarcane field. After Sampat raised the alarm, family members and villagers reached the spot. A search for the girl was then launched. After receiving information about the incident, police from Padhua police station reached the spot. With the help of villagers, the police launched a search operation in the sugarcane field and surrounding area. The girl's clothes were found in the field, but there was no trace of her. Station House Officer Mohit Pundir said the girl was being searched for. Villagers angry over forest department team's failure to arrive According to the villagers, the forest department team had not reached the spot even nearly four hours after the incident. This angered the people. The incident of the leopard entering the village and carrying away the girl spread panic throughout the area. The villagers continued searching for the girl until late at night.

stories.title: 24-year-old woman dies after falling from Lucknow hotel's 10th floor:Man who stayed with her for 6 hours flees
stories.summary: A 24-year-old woman died after falling from the 10th floor of Hotel Celestial Manor in Lucknow on Monday evening. She had checked into the hotel with a man who allegedly fled shortly after she fell. The incident took place at around 6 pm in the Sushant Golf City police station area. The woman was identified as Samreen, a resident of Chhapatia in Lucknow. The man who was staying with her was identified as Avneesh Jaiswal, a resident of Dostpur in Sultanpur district. According to the report, the two had spent around six hours together in the hotel room before the incident. Woman checked in with man at 11.46 am According to the police, Avneesh Jaiswal had booked room number 1037 at the hotel. He and Samreen checked in at around 11.46 am on Monday. At around 6 pm, Samreen fell from the balcony. After seeing her fall, Avneesh reportedly rushed into a lift and left the hotel from the ground floor. He then took his motorcycle from the parking area and fled. Police arrived at the scene shortly afterwards. A field unit was called in to photograph and videograph the site, and evidence was collected. The woman's body was sent for a post-mortem examination. Woman's father unaware of hotel visit Samreen's father, Mohammad Tajju, lives in Hata Surat Singh in Chhapatia and works in the private sector. He said Samreen worked at a hotel and had left for work on Monday morning. He later received information about her death. Her father said he did not know how she had reached the hotel and was also unaware of the man who had accompanied her.

stories.title: Divya Mittal says, 'I chose UP, not Mirzapur':Will reveal future plans during Navratri; dismisses speculation
stories.summary: Divya Mittal, who left her IAS job to enter politics, said on Monday, "I have chosen Uttar Pradesh, not Mirzapur. I will announce what I plan to do, and when, how and where I will do it, during this Navratri." Divya Mittal arrived in Mirzapur on the first day of Navratri. She has begun a nine-day ritual at the Maa Vindhyavasini Dham. She will stay there for the nine days. A crowd continued to gather to meet Divya Mittal on Monday. At 2 pm, members of the Jaiswal Club welcomed her and raised slogans of "Long live Divya Didi". Divya Mittal responded, "That is a good slogan-Divya Didi." Divya Mittal, an IAS officer of the 2013 batch, resigned on 30 August. She made it clear on 29 September that she would enter politics. Divya Mittal will not join any political party After a photograph of Divya Mittal with Raja Bhaiya went viral on social media, speculation began that she might join a political party. She made it clear that she was not going to join any party. She said, "I had explained my position very clearly and in detail in the previous video as well. I am making it clear before you today too that I am not going to join anyone's party." She did not give a direct answer on contesting the election from Mirzapur Divya Mittal was asked whether she would contest the Mirzapur Nagar Assembly seat. She did not give a direct answer. She said she had already announced her decision to enter politics and would soon provide information about the steps she would take next. Denied meeting Rahul Gandhi Divya Mittal was also questioned about a meeting with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Denying that any such meeting had taken place, she said she had already made it clear in her video that she had not met Rahul Gandhi. People said in the Bhaskar poll: Divya Mittal should contest the election for the Samajwadi Party and prepare to contest from Mirzapur Which party should former IAS officer Divya Mittal contest the election for, and from where? On 2 October, Dainik Bhaskar asked its readers two questions on this. The first question was: Which party could give Divya Mittal the greatest success in politics? There were four options: the BJP, the Samajwadi Party, Raja Bhaiya's party and an independent candidacy. The Samajwadi Party was chosen by the highest share of readers, 30%. In other words, nearly three out of every 10 readers believed that Divya Mittal should enter politics with the Samajwadi Party. The BJP came second, securing 28% of the vote. The option of contesting the election as an independent was also chosen by 28% of respondents. Meanwhile, 14% of readers chose the option of joining Raja Bhaiya's party. This means the vote difference between the SP and the BJP was just 2%. The independent option received as many votes as the BJP. Interestingly, Divya Mittal has said that instead of joining any party, she would enter politics as the "voice of the people". She has said that she will decide her political path in consultation with the people. Served as Mirzapur DM and brought water to Lahuriadih Divya became Mirzapur's DM in September 2022. She came into the limelight there for her work involving public meetings in rural areas and drinking water. The initiative to supply water through pipelines to Lahuriadih village was also undertaken during her tenure. Even after her transfer from Mirzapur, her farewell remained a topic of discussion. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Her tenure in Deoria also attracted attention. A dispute over powers between elected representatives and the administration there once again brought her into the spotlight. Left IAS career to enter politics Divya, an IAS officer from the 2013 batch, resigned from her post on 30 August. Her resignation was accepted on 14 September. Since then, there had been speculation about her future plans. After completing a BTech from IIT Delhi and an MBA from IIM Bengaluru, Divya had taken up a job in London with a package worth lakhs. Divya joined the civil services after leaving her job in London Divya's husband is from Punjab and cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt

stories.title: Class 5 girl cannot read a Hindi newspaper:Allahabad High Court questions UP’s education system; says she should study until Class 12
stories.summary: A girl who had studied only up to class five told the Allahabad High Court that she could not read a Hindi newspaper. Apart from writing her name, she could not write anything in Hindi. The court subsequently expressed serious concern over Uttar Pradesh's education system. A division bench of Justice Atul Sridharan and Justice Achal Sachdeva said: "The question naturally arises as to why the victim studied in school only up to class five. Why was the state unable to ensure that her education continued? Or why was she not compelled to remain in school to complete her education up to class twelve?" The court was hearing a habeas corpus petition. It was related to a case under the POCSO Act. The petitioner, Rakesh Yadav alias Pappu, had sought the girl's production before the court. He had eloped from home with the girl in 2025. The girl later gave birth to a child. The matter dates to 5 October and came to light on Monday. Court Asked About Girl's Educational Background During the hearing, the judges asked the girl questions about her educational background. The court asked whether she could read a Hindi newspaper. The girl replied, "No." When asked whether she could write her name, she said, "Yes." The court expressed surprise, saying that according to the records and the state's lawyer, the girl had studied up to Class five. Despite this, she could not read a newspaper in her mother tongue. The girl could only sign her name. She could not write anything more than that in Hindi. Court Asked UP Government Questions and Offered Suggestions The court also spoke to the girl's father During the hearing, the court also spoke to the girl's father. He said that he was illiterate and had never attended school. He earned ₹10,000 to ₹12,000 a month through daily-wage labour. He is the family's only earning member. He also has to take responsibility for his four children and elderly parents. None of the four children earns yet. The court said, "A large section of the population does not have adequate knowledge of the rights granted by law and the Constitution. Such people are also unaware of their legal duties and obligations, and the consequences of violating them." Suggestions sought on amendments to POCSO Act The High Court requested the Law Commission to suggest amendments to provisions of the POCSO Act that apply to cases involving relationships between minors. The court said the issue should be reviewed. It said that in some circumstances, strictly enforcing the law could promote injustice rather than advance justice, particularly when a child has already been born from such a relationship. The court suggested that the Law Commission could consider whether a special judge should be given sufficient discretion to take the circumstances of the case into account while deciding the sentence. Girl Allowed to Leave with Young Man The petitioners said that the girl and the young man had both run away from home. They subsequently had an affidavit prepared on 1 September 2025, in which they described themselves as husband and wife. However, the state government and the girl's father stated that her date of birth was 25 July 2010. This meant that the girl was only 15 years old. Therefore, after she was recovered, she was sent to a juvenile home. She later gave birth to a child there. On Monday, while hearing the habeas corpus petition, the High Court found that the record did not contain a birth-date certificate issued by the girl's school. Nor was there a birth certificate from the municipal body or panchayat. However, based on a bone examination, the girl's age was estimated to be around 18. The court subsequently treated the girl as an adult. The girl expressed her wish to live with the young man. The court therefore allowed her to leave with him.

stories.title: UP Board exam 2027 timetable released:Class 10 and 12 exams to be held from February 5 to 24
stories.summary: The UP Board announced the timetable for the Class 10 and Class 12 examinations on Monday evening. The exams will begin on February 5, 2027, and continue until February 24, 2027. The Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections will be held after the examinations. Bhagwati Singh, secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad (UPMSP), said the Class 10 and Class 12 examinations would be held simultaneously in two shifts. The first shift will run from 8:30 am to 11:45 am, while the second shift will be held from 2 pm to 5:15 pm. On February 5, both Class 10 and Class 12 students will take their Hindi examinations in the first shift. Sanskrit and Agriculture papers will be held on the final day, February 24. This time, the board examinations will be completed within 20 days. The Class 10 and Class 12 exams are scheduled to be conducted over 15 days within this period. A total of 27.75 lakh students are registered for the Class 10 examination and 24.80 lakh for Class 12, taking the combined total to 52.55 lakh students. In 2026, 53.37 lakh students appeared for the examinations, which means the number of candidates has decreased by 82,000 compared with last year. Administrative instructions and wide publicity In accordance with the directions of the Uttar Pradesh government, the Board of Secondary Education has instructed the Additional Secretaries of all regional offices (Meerut, Bareilly, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur) and all District Inspectors of Schools (DIOS) in the state to ensure wide publicity for this examination schedule in their respective districts through principals, so that candidates can complete their board examination preparations on time. stories.title: Jayant Chaudhary hits back at Akhilesh's 'chavanni' jibe:Says 'Your taunts missed the mark; if you keep mocking others, who will stand by you?'
stories.summary: Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) chief Jayant Chaudhary on Monday targeted Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav. He said, "The issue was about value. Those who do not consider me worth even a quarter of a rupee and say, 'Spit on the quarter,' I want to tell them that I am not even a quarter. I do not consider myself equal even to the dust of Braj." Jayant said, "These are the days of social media. From there, he (Akhilesh) floated a jibe and launched some attacks, but his arrow could not reach me. The arrow did not hit its mark." He further said, "Now he is angry about why this was said. Perhaps I should not have said it. From the stage, he asked, 'Are you angry or not? Do you accept what I am saying or not?' But that is how verbal arrows work. If you speak without thinking, make sarcastic remarks for 24 hours, do not take things seriously and do not learn to maintain relationships, then who will stand by you?" Jayant was speaking in Agra. He held a Swabhiman Sabha at 1 p.m. in Jaingara village in the Fatehpur Sikri Assembly constituency. Around 5,000 people had gathered. The RLD is preparing to expand its political strength in the Braj region. Akhilesh had said, "We turned a four-anna coin into a rupee, yet they left us and went away."

stories.title: Young man dies suddenly while performing ablution in Saharanpur:He went to the mosque to pray, fell backwards and could not get up
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man suddenly died inside a mosque in Saharanpur before prayers. He was performing ablution when he fell backwards. The people present initially could not understand what had happened. Later, a young man lifted him and tried to give him water, but his condition did not improve. His family took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. A heart attack is suspected. The deceased was a labourer. He was identified as Sharafat, a resident of Buddahkheda village. The incident took place on Sunday afternoon. CCTV footage of the incident emerged on Monday. Understand the incident through 3 pictures... Now read what is visible in the video... Buddhakheda village in the Gangoh police station area has a Muslim majority. There is a mosque in the village. At around 12 noon on Sunday, Sharafat went to the mosque to offer prayers. The footage shows Sharafat performing wuzu before the prayers, washing his hands and feet. He suddenly fell backwards. A short while later, a young man wearing a red shirt and black trousers approached Sharafat. He was seen trying to support and lift him. He continued trying to help. Around 41 seconds later, some other people also began arriving at the spot. Preparations for Zuhr prayers were under way At the time of the incident, preparations for Zuhr prayers were underway at the mosque. Those attending the prayers were in their places. Sharafat was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Village head Harish Chaudhary said Sharafat was the eldest of his six brothers. He supported his family by working as a labourer. He is survived by a daughter and a son. Sharafat, who was responsible for supporting the family, died suddenly, plunging his relatives into deep grief. Sharafat was buried in the village cemetery. The family did not have a post-mortem examination conducted. Also learn about some other sudden deaths in Uttar Pradesh Class 2 student dies suddenly while sitting in Balrampur A Class Two student died while sitting in class in Balrampur on 22 September. The girl suddenly stood up from her seat and then fell. She regained consciousness after a while, but then fainted and fell again. She did not get up after that. The teachers took her to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. The school management said that a Ganesh immersion procession was passing near the school when the incident occurred. A DJ was playing at full volume during the procession. It said the girl's condition deteriorated and she died because of the loud sound. Teacher dies while marking attendance at UP Board examination In Bulandshahr, 55-year-old private teacher Surendra Pal died of a heart attack in February while performing board examination duty. He was assigned duty in the first shift of the examination and was marking the attendance of high school candidates. During this, he suddenly felt chest pain and collapsed within moments. Seeing this, the students in the classroom called the college staff. Fellow teachers lifted him and rushed him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Devotee dies while sitting on a boat at the Sangam A 38-year-old devotee, Vishnu Thakur, died of a heart attack while taking a boat ride at the Sangam in Prayagraj. A video of the incident, which took place on 15 July, also emerged. It showed the devotee sitting on a boat wearing a life jacket and using his mobile phone. A child was sitting in front of him. The devotee suddenly collapsed and did not get up again. He had come from Mathura with his family to visit the Sangam. His cousin, Ranveer Thakur, is a BJP district minister in Mathura. Railway employee collapses at tea stall, does not get up again In Jhansi, 29-year-old railway employee Ajay Kushwaha came to a hotel from his office to get tea. He then fell face-first onto a tray of pakoras and samosas kept on the shop counter. He subsequently fell to the ground. People present at the spot mistook it for an epileptic seizure. Some began making him smell their shoes and socks, while others kept rubbing his chest. Meanwhile, the railway employee lay on the ground, writhing for around 3 minutes. His body then stopped moving. He was taken to hospital immediately, where doctors declared him dead. CCTV footage of the entire incident has also emerged. 13-year-old student dies while bowling A 13-year-old student died while playing cricket in Mainpuri in February. Virat Chauhan was bowling when he suddenly began experiencing severe pain in his hand. After some time, he fell to the ground, began writhing, and lost consciousness. His family took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Virat was a sixth-grade student. Doctors suspected a heart attack. Contractor staggered and fell while playing badminton, never got up again In Mahoba, 58-year-old contractor Sudhir Gupta died of a heart attack while playing badminton in March. He suddenly staggered while playing on the court and placed a hand on his chest. He walked towards a bench four steps away but fell to the ground. The people playing with him rushed to his side and tried to administer CPR, but by then he had stopped breathing. The entire incident took place within five seconds. Doctors described it as a silent heart attack. Teacher dies while sitting in car in Sitapur Government teacher Radheshyam Patel (50) died while sitting in his car in Sitapur on 14 August. His body was found at around 10 a.m. on the roadside, in the driver's seat beside the car's front passenger seat. The car door was lying open. Shopkeepers nearby became suspicious after seeing the car parked there for a long time. They went over and called out to him. They shook his body, but there was no response. Doctors suspected that he had died of a heart attack.

stories.title: SP MP Dhanraj Nathwani flies to Lucknow on chartered plane:Collects Rajya Sabha victory certificate, returns to Gujarat in 3 hours
stories.summary: SP’s billionaire Rajya Sabha MP Dhanraj Nathwani arrived in Lucknow by chartered plane on Monday. He went straight from the airport to Vidhan Bhavan and collected his certificate of victory in the Rajya Sabha elections from the returning officer. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav was not present on the occasion. He had suddenly planned to leave for Delhi, where he was to join the Opposition’s march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Therefore, Nathwani was accompanied by Leader of Opposition in the UP Assembly Mata Prasad Pandey and Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Council Jasim Ansari. After collecting the certificate, Nathwani visited Akhilesh’s residence and met him. Earlier, Nathwani’s private chartered plane was scheduled to land at Amausi Airport at 8.45 am, but it landed at 11.10 am. Nathwani stayed in Lucknow for around three hours and left for Ahmedabad at 2.10 pm. Results announced on 9 October, elections held for 10 seats All candidates in the election for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh have been elected unopposed. They include eight BJP candidates and two from the Samajwadi Party. As soon as the results were announced on 9 October, all eight newly elected BJP MPs reached the venue and collected their certificates of victory. Neither of the Samajwadi Party's two candidates was present at the time. Dhanraj Nathwani had already shared on social media that he would collect his certificate on 12 October on the auspicious occasion of Sharadiya Navratri. Nathwani said, 'The goal is to take Akhilesh's vision forward' Speaking to journalists after collecting his certificate at the Vidhan Bhavan, Dhanraj Nathwani praised Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav's tenure. He said, "Akhilesh Yadav's vision for the development of Uttar Pradesh has been very clear. During his tenure, historic work was carried out in the state in the fields of infrastructure, education and development. A network of expressways was laid across the state, the metro network was launched and world-class stadiums were built." Had come under fire from opponents after praising PM Modi Dhanraj Nathwani recently came into the spotlight over a social media post in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the completion of 25 years of his public life. He shared a video praising PM Modi's leadership, nation-building and dedication, which read: "25 years of leadership, 25 years of commitment, 25 years of resolve to serve." The post mentioned his journey from becoming the Chief Minister of Gujarat to becoming the Prime Minister of the country. Questions had begun to arise among opposition parties and the internal factions of the Samajwadi Party as soon as this post surfaced. However, Akhilesh Yadav dismissed all speculation and, by sending him to the Rajya Sabha, signalled his commitment to industry- and development-focused politics. What will the Samajwadi Party gain by giving Nathwani a ticket? Through Nathwani, the Samajwadi Party could expand its reach among major business groups and the industrial sector. Ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, this could create a new political connection for the Samajwadi Party. Political experts are linking this decision to Akhilesh's strategy of building ties with big business leaders. It is also being compared with 2004. At the time, Anil Ambani entered the Rajya Sabha with the support of Mulayam Singh Yadav. There was also political discussion then over Reliance being awarded major power projects in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Akhilesh says Vikas Yadav got 10 votes in Azamgarh:Vows to stop BJP’s ‘fraud’; pays tribute to Lohia with uncle
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Monday, "The SIR that was conducted in Uttar Pradesh has been nullified. You did not even realise it, and a new SIR was launched. We will not allow this 420 fraud by the BJP to operate across all 403 Assembly seats." He said, "In one Assembly constituency in Azamgarh, there are 10 voters named Vikas Yadav. One vote will be cast by Vikas Yadav, while the BJP will cast the remaining nine. Millions of fake votes have been created in Uttar Pradesh. This means there is wrongdoing in the SIR. ₹crores were spent and time was wasted, but nothing happened. We are Gandhians. We will protest, but will not break any law." Before this, Akhilesh paid tribute to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia in Lucknow with his uncle Shivpal Singh Yadav. He said the BJP was a crisis for the country. When the election comes, a government of socialists will be formed. The PDA is completely alert. Whoever is oppressed is a socialist. That is the PDA. Together, we will complete the work of Lohia ji and Netaji. Akhilesh Yadav's key points- 1. What action was taken against the BLO, SDM and DM? Akhilesh alleged that more than 100 forms had been filled out by a person named Dashrath in Lucknow's Sarojini Nagar Assembly constituency. In Sultanpur, votes were deleted after forging signatures in the name of Nandlal Nishad. He questioned what action had been taken against the BLO, SDM, DM or Election Commission officials in these cases. 2. If stopped by police, the SP will protest within the law Akhilesh said that the Samajwadi Party would stage the proposed protest in Delhi in a peaceful and Gandhian manner over Chief Minister Yogi's allegations that the Opposition was spreading anarchy. Even if the police stopped it, the party would register its protest while remaining within the bounds of the law. 3. People linked to the BJP are working as fake journalists Akhilesh expressed his displeasure over the misbehaviour with journalists in Delhi and the arrest of a woman journalist. He said that such treatment of journalists was not appropriate for democracy. Some people linked to the BJP are working as fake journalists. 4. Compared the BJP's working style with Hitler's On allegations that RSS members took part in the protest wearing police uniforms, Akhilesh compared the BJP with Hitler. He claimed that political workers were being made to wear police-like uniforms and used against the Opposition. 5. Faizullaganj not declared disaster-affected Akhilesh claimed that around five lakh people in Lucknow's Faizullaganj had been affected by floods, but the area had not yet been declared disaster-affected. Several families have been forced to leave their homes. Questioning the decisions to open and close the barrage gates, he accused the authorities of negligence in flood management. 6. stories.title: Yogi takes 'chameleon' jibe at SP in Gorakhpur:Says party and education are like two riverbanks that can never meet
stories.summary: CM Yogi, targeting the Samajwadi Party (SP), said that the SP and education were like the two banks of a river that could never meet. The SP was a staunch opponent of education. Anyone opposed to education could not be a well-wisher of teachers. Yogi said that before the Rajya Sabha elections, the SP had been repeatedly shouting about PDA. There were 10 Rajya Sabha seats, and the SP fielded two candidates. One was its 'Chacha Jaan', that is, a part of the Family Development Authority. The other was a wealthy industrialist from Mumbai, meaning, 'Make someone else's money your own'. The chameleon must have been happy, thinking that it had found a companion in the SP who would work as its competitor. The CM said that if the SP preached that there would be security and peace if it came to power, it would be like a crocodile coming to the riverbank and preaching that it had stopped hunting. The Chief Minister was interacting with teachers in Gorakhpur on Monday to appeal for votes in favour of BJP candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi in the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers' MLC election. Around 12,000 teachers attended the programme.

stories.title: History-sheeter posed as Baba for 22 years in Jhansi:Held divine courts, claimed to cure illnesses; minor complaint exposes identity
stories.summary: Pradeep Shukla, alias Natroj, who is famous in Jhansi as 'Kaali Sarkar Baba', had been living in hiding for 22 years. A minor complaint exposed the fact that he was a history-sheeter. Some local residents had complained that he had abused and threatened them, and the complaint reached the SSP. The matter was then investigated. Around four days ago, he was summoned to the Mauranipur police station, where he was questioned. People knew him as Satyanand Shukla, alias Kaali Sarkar. However, the police discovered his real name and address. His use of a different name raised the police's suspicions. The Hardoi police were then contacted. Hardoi police records showed that Pradeep Shukla was a history-sheeter. It was also discovered that he was an accused in a 33-year-old robbery case. SSP Vikas Kumar then spoke to police officials in Hardoi. The Hardoi police reached Jhansi with the warrants issued against the accused. He was subsequently arrested on Sunday. See 3 pictures of Kaali Sarkar Baba He had been holding the divine court for two years The accused, Pradeep Shukla alias Natroj, is a resident of Chauhan Thok in the city Kotwali area of Hardoi district. With several cases registered against him, he is listed as a history-sheeter in police records. He fled to Jhansi 22 years ago. He first lived in Lahchura village and later rented a place in Mauranipur. He had been living in Kuraincha village in Mauranipur for around two years. There, he built a temple dedicated to Kali Mata as well as an ashram. He changed his name to Satyanand Shukla alias Kali Sarkar. He also began holding a divine court while posing as a holy man. He claimed to cure people's illnesses and resolve their other problems. The site where he built the temple had previously contained a raised platform. He initially installed an idol in a room and held the divine court there. He later had a temple built. Between 2,500 and 3,000 people visited the place every day. Minister lobbied to secure his release The accused initially held his Divya Darbar only on Fridays. As the crowds grew, he began holding it on Saturdays and Sundays as well. He held the Darbar on Wednesdays for local people. Within two years, he had acquired devotees not only in Jhansi but in different parts of the country. People from abroad had also begun arriving here. At these gatherings, he claimed to cure every illness and resolve other problems. Not only that, some ministers from Madhya Pradesh had even become his disciples. According to sources, after receiving information about his arrest, some Madhya Pradesh ministers remained engaged in lobbying for his release. Hardoi Police Had Been Searching for Baba for 12 Years Mau Ranipur CO Ratneshwar Singh said, 'Several cases have been registered against Pradeep Shukla. In 1993, the police arrested him in a robbery case and sent him to jail. Another case of assault was registered against him in 1998. He was not appearing in court in either case.' The court subsequently issued permanent warrants against him. Hardoi Police had been searching for him for around 12 years. On Sunday, a joint team of Hardoi and Mau Ranipur police raided the temple and arrested Kali Sarkar Baba, alias Pradeep Shukla. More than one lakh followers on Instagram Baba created an Instagram page called 'Kali Sarkar' about a year ago. It has more than one lakh followers. In view of Navratri, Kali Sarkar issued a notice on social media informing people that the darbar would remain closed for nine days. However, the police arrested him on the first day of Navratri.

stories.title: Lucknow’s wanted model flees to Delhi, 3 associates detained:Accused Shraddha Dubey divorced from husband, has a son; wanted in businessman’s murder case
stories.summary: Police have intensified the search for model Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the murder of 28-year-old businessman Shiva Sharma in Lucknow. Her location was traced to Delhi, and a police team has been sent there. On Sunday, Hazratganj police detained two or three of Shraddha's associates for questioning. Their names have not yet been disclosed. Police questioned them about Shiva's relationship with Shraddha. The police investigation revealed that Shraddha Dubey is a native of Rae Bareli. She was married and has a son. Shraddha divorced her husband in 2022. Her son lives with her husband. After that, she rented a flat in the Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda and began living there. Shraddha owned a black Scorpio, which she bought last year. Three days ago, on 9 October, Shiva died after falling from the fourth floor of the same Awadh Green Apartment. Shiva had been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for four months. He was wearing only underwear. There was lipstick on his face. See 2 pictures of Shraddha Murder case filed against five, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Adil Ranjana Sharma, Shiva's mother, filed a murder case against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Adil, in connection with her son's death. She alleged that Shraddha pushed her son from the fourth floor. There were marks on Shiva's body at several places from being burned with cigarettes. Connections with leaders and top bureaucrats He also claimed that Shraddha and Shiva had met at a club. Shraddha has connections with political leaders, top bureaucrats and Indian cricket team players. She used to frighten and blackmail her son by invoking their names. Shraddha spotted on the apartment's CCTV footage The police have also examined CCTV footage from Avadh Green Apartment and Lohia Hospital. It shows Shraddha with her driver, sister and some other people. It is therefore clear that Shraddha was present when Shiva fell from the fourth floor of the apartment. Why did she flee after the incident? The police said this would become clear after her arrest. Shiva was threatened for ₹1 lakh in extortion A case was registered on 12 August 2025 in the Vibhuti Khand police station area against history-sheeter Rishabh Rai and 8-10 unidentified associates for allegedly demanding ₹1 lakh in extortion from Shiva Sharma, abusing him and threatening to kill him while displaying a pistol. Shiva's mother had filed the case against them. It was alleged that at around 8 p.m. on 11 August 2025, while Shiva was sitting at the 'Abongja Café' in the Shiva Farmers' Market, Rishabh arrived there with eight to 10 associates. The accused called Shiva inside the cabin and, while abusing him, demanded that he pay goonda tax within two days. When he refused, the accused assaulted him. They pulled out a pistol and threatened to kill him. There was firing at Tinkle Pink Club in Gomtinagar on 30 August. Shiva was an accused in the case. He fled to Bihar after the incident. The STF arrested him in Patna, Bihar, on 13 October 2025 and sent him to jail. During this period, a reward of ₹50,000 had also been announced for him. The police investigation is indicating that this case, too, is linked to Shraddha Dubey and her associates. Watch four reels of model Shraddha Dubey- Shraddha made a name for herself in modelling Shraddha Dubey has made a name for herself in the modelling world. She has received the 'Best Face of Lucknow' award. She has also been the organiser of the 'India Glamorous Run-Way Week' modelling show. She was also the show topper at the 'You and I International Face of Fashion Week' in Delhi. She has received the 'Best Face of Lucknow' award as well. Bollywood professional makeup artist Vikas Srivastava honoured her at an event at the Buddhist Research Institute. Shraddha began her career in Hyderabad. Alongside pursuing an MA, she completed a PGDCA. She then began fashion blogging. In an interview as a model, Shraddha said that her parents were happy when she left her studies and began modelling. Worked in a Zee Music album Shraddha also worked in Zee Music's album 'Tujh Mein Hai Baarish'. She appeared in it as part of the star cast alongside Sanjeev and Bhavya. The song is available on Zee Music's YouTube channel. Shraddha was also seen distributing rations and food during the coronavirus pandemic.

stories.title: Boyfriend kills girlfriend’s aunt, dies by suicide:Shoots her uncle too in Chitrakoot; attacks family after release from jail
stories.summary: In Chitrakoot, a boyfriend entered his minor girlfriend's house on Sunday night and shot her aunt dead. He also opened fire on her uncle when he intervened. Fearing that he would be caught, he then shot himself in the chest with a country-made pistol and died. The incident caused panic in the village. The villagers immediately informed the police. The three were rushed to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared the accused, Shyamdhar Mishra (25), and the girl's aunt dead. The uncle sustained a gunshot wound to his hand and was referred to Prayagraj. The incident took place in Jorwara village in Mau tehsil, around 50 kilometres from the district headquarters. Police said the Dalit girl's family had filed a complaint against Shyamdhar a few days earlier. He was subsequently sent to jail by the police. He carried out the attack after being released from jail recently. Girl's family objected to the affair Dinesh Chand is a PRD personnel in Jorwara village, under the Mau police station area. He has three sons - Ram Aadhar, Shiv Aadhar and Shyamdhar Mishra. Shyamdhar was having an affair with a 17-year-old Dalit girl who lived 150 metres from his house. When the girl's family learnt about it, they objected. The minor's family consists of her parents, four brothers and four sisters. She is the youngest. Her father works as a labourer. She lives in the same house as her brother and his wife. Her labourer brother has three sons and three daughters. The eldest son and one daughter are married. Complaint filed under molestation and SC/ST Act On Thursday night, the girl's family caught the two in an objectionable situation. The next day, Friday, the girl's family filed a complaint against Shyamdhar for molestation and under the SC/ST Act. During this time, there was a heated exchange between Shyamdhar and the girl's family. Police released him after booking him for disturbing the peace The police took action and arrested Shyamdhar the same day. He was released on Saturday after being booked for disturbing the peace. It is being said that Shyamdhar was enraged over this. At 10 p.m. on Sunday, he reached the girl's house carrying a country-made pistol. He began hurling abuses. Son recounts what happened to his mother and father: Read The deceased woman's son said that Shyamdhar arrived with a handkerchief tied over his mouth. As soon as he arrived, he began hurling abuses. When his mother objected, he shot her in the chest. When his father came to save her, Shyamdhar fired at him as well. He narrowly escaped, but the bullet hit his hand. Shyamdhar then ran towards the fields while shouting. Fled and hid in a field, then shot himself When the police reached the spot after receiving the information and began searching for the accused, they found him lying in the fields around 250 metres from his home. He had sustained a gunshot wound to the chest and was groaning in pain. Blood was coming from his mouth. The police took him to hospital, from where he was referred to Prayagraj. He died at around 2:30 a.m. at Swaroop Rani Hospital. Family members accused police of negligence SP Arun Kumar Singh, ASP Piyush Kant Rai, CO Fahad Ali and forces from several police stations reached the village. A forensic team was called to the spot to conduct an investigation. The girl's family members accused the police of negligence and opposed the body being taken for a post-mortem. The police later pacified them. SP Arun Kumar Singh said: A boy shot the girl's aunt and then committed suicide. The girl's uncle was also shot. The girl is a minor. The two were having an affair. Further action is being taken after questioning the victim's family.

stories.title: Floods in Lucknow, neck-deep water in colonies:Rain in Noida-Ghaziabad; python wraps around snake-catcher’s leg in Gonda
stories.summary: Flooding continues to cause trouble in Uttar Pradesh, with Lucknow remaining under water for the 15th consecutive day. Several colonies are submerged in neck-deep water. More than 40,000 houses are still inundated, affecting over 3 lakh people. The Chandrika Devi Temple premises are also filled with knee-deep water. The Ganga is in spate in Unnao, with boats being used in several streets and neighbourhoods. In Gonda, the Ghaghra flood has affected 10 villages. Meanwhile, in Rajgarh Aminpur village, a python wrapped itself around the leg of a snake catcher on Saturday evening. He managed to free himself after struggling for nearly half an hour. Meanwhile, rain accompanied by thunder and lightning has been lashing five cities, including Noida, Ghaziabad, Bareilly and Aligarh, since Monday morning. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 15 districts in western Uttar Pradesh and warned of possible hailstorms. Hail had already lashed Meerut and Shamli on Sunday. Strong winds also uprooted trees at several places in Bijnor.

stories.title: Gorakhpur power cut today:Supply to remain disrupted for 5 hours in several areas
stories.summary: Electricity supply will remain disrupted for five hours in several areas of Gorakhpur on Monday due to road widening and power line shifting work. According to the electricity department, supply to the 11 kV Hanumant Nagar area, served by the Durgabari power substation, will remain suspended from 10 am to 3 pm. Supply will also be disrupted during the same period in areas served by the 11 kV Rail Vihar and Karim Nagar feeders under the Raptinagar New substation, the 11 kV Shaktinagar feeder under the Rustampur substation, and areas connected to the Shahpur substation. The department has advised consumers to store water and complete other essential electricity-related tasks before 10 am to avoid inconvenience during the shutdown. Power supply will be restored once the work is completed.
