Flood victims get trapped after buying land in Lucknow:‘We fear our houses may sink’; plot prices could rise further if embankment is built
stories.summary: Lucknow’s Faizullaganj now looks like a waterlogged island. Water has almost disappeared from the roads, but 2 to 4 feet of water still remains in the narrow lanes. The flooding has caused the greatest distress to people living in single-storey houses. They are covering their rooftops with tarpaulins to protect their valuable belongings, including refrigerators, cupboards and televisions. Aman Verma, who lives on 60 Feet Road in Faizullaganj, also has a single-storey house. When water entered his home, he gathered his belongings and moved to the roof. Speaking with a choked voice, Aman says, “Many people are saying that our houses were built on the river, which is why they got submerged. I want to ask them how the water reached Palassio and Ekana.” Like Aman, thousands of people in Faizullaganj have been forced to live on their rooftops. Many of them came from other districts, bought plots of land here and built houses. Now, watching the flooding, they regret their decision. They say, “If we had known this earlier, we would never have bought land here.” The Dainik Bhaskar team has been continuously covering the flood-affected areas. This time, we spoke to people who bought land and built houses in the floodplain. Listen to what they are going through amid the flooding and what they have to say. Nagma Khatoon, who originally belongs to Biswan in Sitapur, is sitting by the roadside in the Daudnagar area. She is waiting for the water to recede and for a boat to arrive. Nagma, who moved here with her family in 2020, says, “Our entire house is submerged. The fridge, cupboard, groceries... everything is floating in the water. We could not rescue even a single item safely. My son and husband are trapped in the flood. I received news that their health had deteriorated, so I risked my life to come and see them.” Nagma continues, “Around seven to eight years ago, we invested our entire life savings in buying land here. We have been living here for six years. If we had even the slightest idea that Lucknow could also experience flooding, we would never have bought land here.” ‘We built our house with our hard-earned money, and now it is sinking’ Sushil Tiwari, who moved here from Hardoi, shares the same pain. Sushil says, “We had heard stories about the 2008 floods, but conditions remained normal for years afterwards. We bought land here in 2017 and built a house with our hard-earned money. Today, my entire house is submerged. Everything inside has been ruined. People say we must have bought the land because it was cheap, but that is absolutely not true. We bought the plot at a very high price.” ‘Land in the floodplain is being sold at the highest rates’ Faizullaganj and Daudnagar gradually began developing after 2010. After 2018, real estate activity increased sharply in these areas. Salaried people arriving from other districts invested their hard-earned money in plots here. Local resident Moinuddin says, “The price of land on Daudnagar’s 60 Feet Main Road has now reached ₹6,000 per square foot. In prime locations, people are charging as much as ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 per square foot. Even in the inner lanes, you will not find land for less than ₹2,000 to ₹3,000 per square foot. This was not an unplanned settlement where land was available for next to nothing.” When Moinuddin was asked whether land prices would fall after such severe flooding, he replied with a smile, “Absolutely not! Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has now announced that a dam will be built. Property dealers and builders will publicise this announcement and sell the land at even higher prices. The real problem is that earlier, when some water accumulated, it could be pumped out using pumping sets. But this time, that was not possible.” Expert says river’s width was reduced in the name of a riverfront, and that was wrong More than 40,000 houses in Faizullaganj have been affected by the flooding, of which around 50% are single-storey houses. More than 4 lakh people have been affected by the flooding in Lucknow. According to a 2018 report published in the research journal Environmental Sustainability, the width of the Gomti River in Lucknow was reduced from 450 metres to 240 metres during the construction of the riverfront. The river’s flow corridor was also narrowed from 250 metres to between 100 and 125 metres. Tall concrete walls were built along both banks of the river. As a result, when a heavy flow of water arrived this time, the river could not pass through the narrow concrete channel. The water backed up and began wreaking havoc in residential areas. Water level was below the danger mark, yet 40,000 houses were flooded The Gomti has flooded five times, and the threat remains Professor Dutta explains that the Gomti River originates in Pilibhit and travels around 900 kilometres before reaching Ghazipur. Along the way, 185 tributaries and streams, including 35 major rivers, flow into it. Unfortunately, several tributaries were officially classified as ‘drains’, filled in and built over. Nature never forgets its course, and Lucknow is now bearing the consequences.

stories.title: Ajay returns without meeting Rahul, may quit Congress:Political debut with Anupriya could complicate contest for Pindra seat
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai will demonstrate his strength today at Maa Nakateshwari Dham in Pindra, Varanasi. He is reportedly upset with the party. The reason is a dispute involving Mamta Chaudhary at the Congress headquarters in Lucknow on 11 October. The party's top leadership had called him to Delhi to contain the damage. He went there on 14 October but did not meet Rahul Gandhi. Questions are now being raised about whether Ajay Rai will leave the Congress. If he does, will he return to his former party or begin a new political innings with Anupriya Patel? Read the full story… Ajay Rai served as Uttar Pradesh Congress president for more than 3 years, but on 2 October, he was suddenly removed, and Aradhana Mishra, 'Mona', was appointed as the state president. Before this, Aradhana Mishra was the Congress Legislature Party leader. Ajay Rai accepted the decision and congratulated Aradhana Mishra. He also said, “I am a soldier of Rahul Gandhi.” The dispute began with the taunt, ‘Who is the president?’ On 11 October, the first day of Navratri, Aradhana Mishra had organised a programme to take charge as the state Congress president. Ajay Rai also arrived from Varanasi with his supporters to attend the event. At the state Congress office, Ajay Rai's supporters were asking the crowd to make way, saying, “The president is coming.” In response, Mamta Chaudhary, the president of the Congress Mahila Morcha for the central region, taunted them, saying, “Who is the president? I would not even like to look at such a president.” Ajay Rai's supporters objected to Mamta's remark. An argument then escalated between the two sides. The dispute became so heated that Ajay Rai's supporters even took off their shoes. Angered by the incident, Ajay Rai began leaving the party office. Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari, Aradhana Mishra's father, somehow managed to persuade him to stay. However, the incident intensified speculation that Ajay Rai was upset with the party. Sources associated with the party say Mamta Chaudhary has a good relationship with Aradhana Mishra. This has led to speculation that Mamta had Mona Mishra's backing when she made the remark. However, this claim has not been confirmed. The party has not taken any action against Mamta Chaudhary so far. Conspiracy against Ajay? He was not even given a chance to present his case Ajay Rai took charge as Uttar Pradesh Congress president on 19 August 2023. At the time, the party had suffered a crushing defeat in the 2022 Assembly elections, winning just two seats. The morale of party workers had also fallen. During his tenure of more than three years, Ajay Rai tried to boost the morale of party workers. He remained active on a range of local and state issues and worked to strengthen his connection with the public. It is reported that he also bore the entire cost of running the party office himself. The number of Congress MPs in Uttar Pradesh increased from one in 2019 to six in 2024. Ajay Rai was now working to strengthen the party ahead of the Assembly elections, but he was suddenly removed from his post. It is reported that Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, had been working to have Ajay Rai removed for the past month. He reportedly convinced senior party leaders that the Congress would not perform well in the Assembly elections under Ajay Rai's leadership. Ajay Rai's strict manner of dealing with people is also being cited as a reason for the change. Caste equations have also emerged as a factor in the discussions. According to sources, Rahul Gandhi was not in favour of the change and wanted the decision to replace the state president to be postponed until after the Assembly elections. Initially, the party considered appointing a Muslim leader as state president. However, Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi wanted the post to go to Aradhana Mishra, a Brahmin leader. Aradhana Mishra was eventually appointed state president. It is reported that Ajay Rai is also upset because he believes a conspiracy was plotted against him to remove him from the post. He was reportedly called to present his side after Rajendra Pal Gautam submitted his report. However, sources claim that his views were not heard because Priyanka Gandhi and K.C. Venugopal opposed giving him that opportunity. Leaving the Congress will not be easy for Ajay According to sources associated with the party, after Ajay Rai was removed as state president, Rahul Gandhi immediately offered to make him a member of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) and appoint him as the party's in-charge for a state. However, Ajay Rai did not accept the offer. Rahul Gandhi remains in regular contact with Ajay Rai. Therefore, deciding to leave the Congress will not be easy for him. A leader close to Ajay Rai, speaking on condition of anonymity, said he would not leave the Congress. According to the leader, Ajay Rai might consider leaving the party only if Rahul Gandhi himself mistreated him. The leader added that Ajay Rai also has limited political alternatives. Could Ajay Rai return to the BJP? Ajay Rai began his political career with the RSS and the BJP's student organisation, ABVP. He was elected MLA from the Kolasla Assembly constituency on a BJP ticket in 1996, 2002 and 2007, winning three consecutive terms. When the BJP denied him a ticket for the 2009 Lok Sabha elections, he resigned from both the party and his position as MLA. He then joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) and contested the Lok Sabha election from Varanasi, but lost. His resignation left the Kolasla Assembly seat vacant. He was elected MLA again in the by-election as an independent candidate. Before the 2012 Assembly elections, Ajay Rai joined the Congress. That year, he won the Pindra Assembly seat on a Congress ticket. He subsequently contested the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi against Prime Minister Narendra Modi but lost on all three occasions. The road ahead in Pindra will not be easy either According to senior journalist Anand Rai, Ajay Rai's return to the BJP would be difficult. Ajay Rai is preparing to contest the Pindra Assembly seat. At present, BJP MLA Awadhesh Singh represents the constituency. Like Ajay Rai, he also belongs to the Bhumihar community. In the 2022 Assembly elections, Ajay Rai finished third in Pindra, while BSP candidate Babulal came second. The result was similar in the 2017 elections. A source associated with the BJP claims that, while serving as state Congress president, Ajay Rai openly criticised the theft of offerings at the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Therefore, the chances of his returning to the BJP are low. Even if he joins Anupriya Patel, the seat-sharing issue will remain Why did he not meet Rahul Gandhi despite travelling to Delhi? On 14 October, reports emerged that Rahul Gandhi had called Ajay Rai to Delhi. Ajay Rai travelled there but did not meet Rahul Gandhi. Earlier, senior Congress leaders had been called to Delhi to participate in Rahul Gandhi's protest, but Ajay Rai did not attend that either. This led to speculation that he had avoided meeting Rahul Gandhi because he was upset with the party. However, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ajay Rai denied being upset with the party. He said: I had gone to Delhi for my child's admission. There was no programme to meet Rahul Gandhi. Does anyone get upset with their own family? The Congress is my family and my home. Why is Ajay Rai suddenly demonstrating his strength in Pindra on 17 October? Following the dispute at the Congress office on 11 October, Ajay Rai posted a message on social media on the night of 14 October. In the post, he announced a rally near Maa Nakateshwari Dham in Pindra at 12:30 pm on 17 October. He wrote, “Pindra is my family.” According to senior journalist Anand Rai, after being removed as state president, Ajay Rai's option now is to focus on preparations in his assembly constituency. By demonstrating his strength in Pindra, he will want to boost the morale of his supporters. Meanwhile, people associated with the party believe that the committee formed to investigate the 11 October dispute is also due to submit its report on 17 October. Ajay Rai therefore wants to demonstrate his strength through the rally. He also wants to send a message about how important he is to the Congress. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’, responding to a question from Dainik Bhaskar, said, “Ajay Rai is a member of our family. He is a senior leader and our elder brother.”

stories.title: UP PET centres set 500–600 km away:35 lakh candidates angry; commission chairman says centres were allotted through automated system
stories.summary: Candidates appearing for the PET examination are facing long journeys to reach their allotted centres, with Siddharth Singh from Jaunpur having to travel 520 km to Mainpuri and Mohammad Rehman from Prayagraj being assigned a centre in Ghaziabad, 650 km away. Their plight reflects the concerns of 35 lakh candidates who have been allotted examination centres 500 to 600 km from their homes and are struggling to decide whether to focus on exam preparation or spend additional time travelling, with some preparing to begin their journeys a day in advance. Dainik Bhaskar asked commission chairman Satyanarayan Sabat about the issue. He said the commission takes steps to prevent cheating in examinations. Examination centres are now allotted through automation, which is why some candidates have been assigned centres farther away this time. The PET-2026 examination will be held on 25 and 30 October and 1 November. Around 35 lakh candidates are expected to appear. Candidates must take this eligibility test for government jobs under the UPSSSC. Only those who pass can apply for Group B and Group C jobs. On 12 October, the commission announced on its website the cities where the examination would be held. This triggered anger among candidates. Students are now demanding that the government and commission change their examination centres. To understand the difficulties they are facing, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to candidates. Himanshu Pandey from Pratapgarh says, “We cannot apply for UPSSSC jobs without passing the PET examination. At present, we are studying for 18 hours every day. Now we have learnt that my examination centre has been allotted in Firozabad, 470 km away. Just think about it. I will have to travel through the night to reach the centre. I will be so exhausted that I will not be able to write my answers properly during the examination.” R.K. Maurya from Pilibhit is facing a similar problem. He says, “My examination centre has been allotted in Bijnor, 240 km away. It takes five hours to get there by train, and then I have to struggle to reach the centre. If I am even a few minutes late, they will send me back from the examination centre. The commission has not taken our convenience into account.” Only 10 days left for the examination, but confirmed seats are unavailable Only 10 to 15 days remain before the examination. Candidates complain that they are unable to get confirmed train tickets because their centres are 500 to 600 km away. There are also no direct bus or train services to several districts, forcing candidates to change buses or trains once or twice. Since the centres are far away, they will have to arrive a day in advance. Travel fares, accommodation and food could together cost each candidate up to ₹2,000. Women candidates face an additional difficulty, as they feel unsafe travelling away from home alone. Naturally, they will have to take a family member along. The combined cost of travel, accommodation and food for two people can reach ₹3,500 to ₹4,000. As a result, daughters from poor families are being forced to consider skipping the examination. ‘Why so much travelling for just a screening test?’ Since the admit cards were released, candidates have been demanding a change of examination centres on social media. They argue that the PET is only an initial screening test for Group B and Group C government jobs, such as Lekhpal, Junior Assistant and VDO. It is not an examination that directly determines final job appointments, so there is no reason to send candidates such long distances for it. Five times the population of Sikkim in PET candidates The examination will be conducted over three days, with two shifts each day. The commission has set up a total of 1,372 centres across 60 districts in the state. A record 35 lakh 41 thousand 296 candidates have applied this time. An average of 6 lakh candidates will appear in each shift, with around 12 lakh candidates taking the examination each day. The total number of PET candidates is approximately five to six times Sikkim's population of around 7 lakh. Commission chairman says, ‘Allotments were made by computer’ Commission chairman Satyanarayan Sabat says, “Uttar Pradesh is a large state, with a distance of around 1,100 kilometres from one end to the other. The most suitable arrangement has been implemented in view of the examination centres available for 35 lakh candidates. The number of candidates is high in eastern Uttar Pradesh districts such as Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia and Jaunpur. In comparison, there are fewer examination centres. Meanwhile, western Uttar Pradesh has fewer candidates and more centres. Therefore, candidates have been allotted centres according to requirements.” Understand in 3 points: Who has been allotted a centre, where and why Candidates with disabilities: Under the government's policy, they have been given examination centres in their home districts as a concession. Women candidates: Keeping their safety in mind, they have been allotted centres outside their home districts but in another city within their administrative division. Male candidates: They have been allotted examination centres in other administrative divisions.

stories.title: Ravita’s love story behind husband’s murder using a snake:Showed injuries to boyfriend on video calls; Meerut court sentences both to death
stories.summary: A Meerut court has sentenced Ravita and her lover Amardeep to death for murdering her husband, Amit Kashyap, and trying to pass off the murder as a snakebite. Additional District Judge (ADJ-12) Jayveer Singh Nagar said that giving them life imprisonment would not be enough for the crime. In his judgment, the judge wrote that Amit's murder had shaken the foundation of married life. He said Amit had trusted his wife and made her the mother of his three children, but she joined hands with her lover to kill him by strangling him. The judge described the murder as a cruel betrayal of the husband-wife relationship. He said the case fell under the “rarest of rare” category and required the harshest punishment. After the death sentence was announced on Friday evening, Ravita and Amardeep were shifted to the prisoners' barracks. Both kept crying and did not touch the food sent to them. Ravita also developed a high fever. Judge says husband-wife relationship is based on trust The judge wrote that the relationship between a husband and wife is traditionally seen as a bond of trust, sacrifice and commitment. He said Amit's murder was not just the killing of one person but also a serious blow to the values associated with marriage in Indian society. He observed that a husband expects his wife to protect him, just as she expects him to stand by her. In this case, the person Amit trusted most allegedly became involved in his murder. The judgment referred to Hindu religious beliefs that describe a wife as an “Ardhangini”, or the other half of her husband, and a partner in his duties, happiness and sorrow. Judge says Ravita went against the ideals of Savitri The judge also referred to the story of Savitri, who, according to Hindu tradition, brought her husband Satyavan back from the god of death, Yama. He said Ravita had acted against the ideals linked with Savitri. The judge noted that people traditionally pray for their spouses' long lives during festivals such as Karwa Chauth, but Ravita had allegedly joined her lover to kill her husband. He wrote that Amit had trusted Amardeep like a brother. Amardeep used to visit Amit's house and had worked with him on tile installation. The judge said this trust had also been betrayed. Judge warns against using murder to remove a partner from the way The judgment said such crimes could weaken people's faith in the marriage bond and create a wrong message that a spouse could be killed for the sake of an outside relationship. The judge also referred to the couple's three young children. He said they had lost their father and their mother would now be in prison, leaving their future uncertain. He held Ravita responsible for the situation caused by the crime. The judge said a lenient punishment in such cases could send the wrong message to society. He stressed that strict punishment was needed to prevent similar crimes. Defence lawyer did not appear for the hearing At around 11:30 am on Friday, ADJ-12 Jayveer Singh Nagar entered the courtroom. Ravita and Amardeep joined the hearing from jail through video conference. Amardeep was wearing a white shirt, while Ravita was wearing a brown suit and had covered her head with a dupatta. The two looked at each other briefly. The judge told them that they had been found guilty in the Amit Kashyap murder case and that the hearing was to decide their punishment. Additional District Government Counsel Farzana Khatoon represented the prosecution, while Balraj Singh appeared as the lawyer for Amit's family. The defence lawyer, Omkar Singh Bhati, did not attend personally and sent a junior lawyer in his place. Farzana argued that the murder was extremely cruel and could not be forgiven. She said Ravita and Amardeep had strangled Amit and attacked him several times. The postmortem report had recorded scratch marks on Amit's face, hands, and chest. She also said Ravita had allegedly planned the murder with Amardeep to marry him and then tried to hide the crime by placing a snake on Amit's bed to make it look like a snakebite. The lawyer representing Amit's family cited more than five Supreme Court rulings and requested the death penalty for both accused. The arguments lasted around 20 minutes. The defence did not present arguments. Ravita asks court to care for her three children After the arguments, the judge asked Amardeep whether he should be given the death penalty or life imprisonment. Amardeep replied that his parents were elderly and requested that someone take care of them. When Ravita was asked the same question, she said she had three young children and requested that they be looked after. Both fell silent when asked to respond further. The judge then said the verdict would be announced after lunch. Ravita and Amardeep cry as judge reads verdict At around 3:05 pm, Amit's mother, Munesh, and his brother, Sonu, were present in the courtroom. Ravita and Amardeep were again connected from the district jail through video conference. As soon as the judge began reading the verdict, both accused started crying. Their cries could be heard in the courtroom. The judge read translations of verses from the seventh chapter of the Manusmriti and the Atreya Samhita. He referred to the role of punishment in maintaining order and said justice requires punishing wrongdoers, respecting good people and treating those seeking justice fairly. Judge breaks pen after announcing death sentence While explaining his decision, the judge said that the “rarest of rare” category was not limited to cases in which a body was cut into pieces. He said a planned murder in which a wife and her lover allegedly strangled her husband and then used a snake to make the death look accidental was also an exceptionally serious crime. The judge then sentenced Ravita and Amardeep to death, saying life imprisonment would not be enough. The courtroom broke into applause, and some lawyers raised slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. Amit's mother began crying and folded her hands to thank the judge. Both Ravita and Amardeep also cried after hearing the sentence. The judge further ordered that the district magistrate would be responsible for ensuring the care, upbringing, and education of Amit and Ravita's three children. After giving the order, the judge broke his pen and left the courtroom. He delivered the verdict in around 12 minutes.

stories.title: Hindu Raksha Dal worker shot dead in Ghaziabad:Went with leader Pinky Chaudhary over plot dispute, mob beats attacker
stories.summary: A Hindu Raksha Dal worker was shot dead over a plot dispute in Ghaziabad's Sahibabad area at around 7 pm on Friday. The deceased, 22-year-old Ayush Valmiki, had accompanied Hindu leader Pinky Chaudhary to the site over the dispute. Ayush got into an argument with the accused, Rahul Sahni, over possession of the plot. Rahul then allegedly shot Ayush with his licensed pistol. After the shooting, Rahul tried to flee the scene. However, Hindu Raksha Dal workers caught him and severely beat him. After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot, rescued Rahul from the crowd and took him into custody. Read the full story below : Sahibabad ACP Amit Saxena said that in the Sahibabad area, a woman named Namita Sharma had sold a 180-square-yard plot to Poonam, the wife of Hindu Raksha Dal president Pinky Chaudhary. Pinky Chaudhary claims that he has already paid Namita Sharma several crore rupees for the plot. A 280-square-yard plot of land next to this plot is lying vacant. It is green-belt land. Namita Sharma claims it as her own, while Pinky Chaudhary also claims it. The two sides have previously disputed the land. The two sides again clashed over it on Friday evening. Gunfire followed an exchange of abuse On Friday evening, Rahul Sahni arrived at the plot with some people on behalf of Namita Sharma. Meanwhile, Pinky Chaudhary and workers of the Hindu Raksha Dal also reached the spot. The two sides first exchanged abuses, after which a physical fight broke out. Rahul Sahani fired a shot from his licensed pistol. The bullet hit Ayush Valmiki. He was immediately taken to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Ayush was a resident of Gokulpuri in Delhi. Hindu Raksha Dal workers caught Rahul Sahani and beat him. The police, who arrived after receiving the information, rescued him from the crowd and detained him. ACP Amit Saxena said that a report was being registered on the basis of the complaint. Action will be taken in the entire matter based on the evidence. Pinky Chaudhary had gone to jail for distributing swords to Hindus Pinky Chaudhary has been embroiled in controversies before. A 21-second video of him emerged on 29 December 2025. The video was from the Shalimar Garden area of Ghaziabad. It showed Pinky Chaudhary distributing swords from house to house along with his supporters. In the video, her supporters were carrying swords and battle-axes. Chanting "Victory to Mother India", they were knocking on the doors of houses. When the owner came outside, they handed him a sword. They said the sword was for protecting sisters and daughters. If a situation like the one in Bangladesh arose, they said, it should be used to protect oneself from non-believers. In this case, the police arrested Pinky Chaudhary and her son on 6 January. After being released on bail on 15 January, Pinky Chaudhary took out a 25-kilometre-long procession.

stories.title: Elderly woman breaks down on seeing Divya Mittal:Hugs her in Mirzapur and says, 'Daughter, I had longed to see you; today my wish has come true'
stories.summary: An elderly woman broke down in tears on seeing former IAS officer Divya Mittal in Mirzapur on Friday. Hugging her, Duiji Devi said, “Daughter, I had been waiting for you for a long time. Today, my wish has been fulfilled. I have seen you to my heart's content. May the goddess continue to bless you. May you progress greatly.” Divya Mittal visited Mirzapur for the first time on Friday after forming a political party. She first visited the Maa Sheetla Temple in Gadbada Dham, where she offered prayers. During her visit, supporters raised slogans such as, “Divya, keep fighting; we are with you,” and “Long live Divya Didi.” At around 4 pm, Divya Mittal reached Lahuriyadah village, where she met Duiji Devi. In 2023, when Divya Mittal was serving as the Mirzapur district magistrate, she had inaugurated a drinking water facility in the village. At that time, Duiji Devi had blessed her. The villagers also garlanded Devkali, the woman who had demanded a school in the village. Divya Mittal told the villagers that she would make every possible effort for the development of Lahuriyadah village. She spoke to the villagers for around half an hour. Check out the pictures below : Divya Mittal announced her political party on Facebook on Thursday Former IAS officer Divya Mittal began her political journey on Thursday, October 15, by launching her own party, named Janniti Bharat. At 1 pm, she posted a video on Facebook announcing that she would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election from the Mirzapur Sadar constituency. Divya Mittal said, “In Janniti Bharat, you will be in charge. Janniti Bharat will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh election. The government will run according to your wishes for five years.” Divya Mittal had said, “My aim is to change politics” On September 30, Divya Mittal had announced her decision to enter politics. She had said, “I will stay in Uttar Pradesh. I will not be afraid; I will ask questions. I will not join any party. I will walk alone. My aim is not to change politicians, but to change politics entirely. I do not need money or muscle power.” Divya Mittal, a 2013-batch IAS officer, resigned from service on August 30. At the time, she was serving as special secretary in the Revenue Department. Her resignation was accepted on September 14. After completing her BTech from IIT Delhi and MBA from IIM Bengaluru, she had worked in London in a job that offered a salary package worth lakhs of rupees. 1. First pledge of 'Janneeti Bharat' — People at the centre of policies Divya Mittal said, “I am forming my own party. There is no shortage of parties, but there is a shortage of people being heard. Like the Ganga, where every drop is equal and helps determine the way forward, I want to build a party where every person has a role. This party is called 'Janneeti Bharat'. Its first pledge is to put people at the centre of the country's policies and let them decide those policies. She recalled how Devkali Devi had asked her for a school even when her home had no water. Work began after Divya's video, but stopped when the land was found to belong to the forest department. Children are still waiting for the school. She questioned why forest land could be cleared within 80 days for roads needed by big industrialists, while files for schools, roads or factories for poor people could remain pending for 80 years. The second pledge is justice for all, where everyone is heard and people help decide how policies are made. She said policies should reflect the sacrifices of parents who eat less to feed their children and cut their own expenses to educate them. She also called for farming policies shaped with farmers, who understand problems from fields to markets and falling prices, and trade policies that consider the challenges faced by small traders from business to ports. She added that a girl looking at the moon from her rooftop today should one day be able to reach it. The pledge is: Policies from the people, and India shaped through those policies. 2. Every decision will be based on need, not identity: Janniti Bharat's second pledge- every decision will be based on need, not identity. A road was being built, raising hopes in the village, when someone pointed a finger and diverted its route. On one side, thousands of people would benefit; on the other, there was one person. The road was diverted towards the latter, where there were hundreds of houses. Courtyards were destroyed and homes were demolished. The person for whom the road was built was somebody. In public policy, everyone will be able to point to a location on the map. If there is a dark stretch or a turn where girls are afraid to pass, they will be able to flag it there. The spot will be marked through a mobile app, and once it receives 100 markings, it will have lighting, patrols and cameras. The decision will be made neither by the police nor by a politician, but by the girls themselves. Whether it is a hand pump, a road or a brick-paved path, work will begin wherever people point first. There will be no consideration of caste, religion or status; everyone will decide together. 3. Decisions based on need and equality in decision-making Janneeti Bharat's third pledge is: decisions based on need and equality in decision-making. A woman applied for a permanent house, but she did not know that her house had been approved. An intermediary came to her home and said, "Mother, I can get it done; give me ₹5,000." If the woman knew about the approval beforehand, where would the intermediary go? All the works carried out in that village, using funds from any source, should be visible on mobile phones. If you give the children notebooks to check, they will say everything is fine. Who is the first to know about a bad road? Those who travel on it. This is Janneeti Bharat's third pledge-accountability to the people and improvement based on accountability. She served as Mirzapur's district magistrate and brought water to Lahuriyadah Divya became Mirzapur's district magistrate in September 2022. She drew attention there for her work involving public meetings in rural areas and drinking water. The initiative to supply water through a pipeline to Lahuriyadah village was also launched during her tenure. Even after her transfer from Mirzapur, her farewell remained a talking point. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Her tenure in Deoria also subsequently drew attention. A dispute over powers between public representatives and the administration there put her in the spotlight once again.

stories.title: UP declares holiday on October 19 for Mahanavami:Offices to remain closed for 3 days in a row
stories.summary: The Yogi government has changed the holidays for Mahanavami and Vijayadashami in Uttar Pradesh. Now, Mahanavami will be a holiday on Monday, October 19, while Dussehra will be observed as a holiday the next day, October 20. Earlier, the government had announced a combined holiday for Mahanavami and Dussehra on October 20. Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department, SVS Rangarao, has issued an order in this regard. October 18 is a Sunday. This means government offices, schools, banks and other institutions across the state will remain closed for three consecutive days. Sandhi Puja to be held on October 19 for 48 minutes Kashi astrologer Pt. Rishi Dwivedi said the period between Maha Ashtami and Mahanavami during Navratri holds special religious importance. The last 24 minutes of Ashtami and the first 24 minutes of Navami together form the Sandhi Kaal, during which Sandhi Puja is performed. This year, Sandhi Puja will take place on October 19, from 10:27 am to 11:15 am. According to religious beliefs, Goddess Durga took the form of Chamunda during this period and killed the demons Chand and Mund. Therefore, worship during these 48 minutes is considered especially important. Devotees pray to Goddess Durga for happiness, peace and the well-being of their families. Devotees can complete their fast on October 20 or 21 Both Navami and Vijayadashami fall on October 20 this year. Devotees can perform the havan, worship and Purnahuti (the final offering in the ritual) on the morning of October 20, during Navami Tithi. However, the correct time to complete the Navratri fast depends on family traditions and religious practices. Religious scholar Vinay Pandey said Navratri begins on Pratipada of the Ashwin Shukla Paksha and continues with the worship of the nine forms of Goddess Durga until Navami. Due to changes in the timing of lunar dates, Navratri sometimes lasts eight days, nine days or even ten days. He explained that different traditions are followed for completing the fast. Some devotees break their fast on Dashami after performing the havan and Purnahuti, while others prefer to do so during a full Dashami Tithi. Therefore, devotees should follow their family traditions and religious beliefs to decide whether to complete their fast on October 20 or October 21. Goddess Durga to arrive on an elephant and leave on a rooster this Navratri Dr. Subhash Pandey of the Astrology Department at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) said that since Navratri begins on Sunday this year, Goddess Durga will arrive riding an elephant. According to religious beliefs, an elephant is a symbol of good rainfall, rich harvests and prosperity. It is also believed to bring purity to the surroundings and help devotees overcome illnesses and problems. Since Navratri will end on Tuesday, the goddess will leave riding a rooster, also known as a cock. 3 other things to know 1. Stability in India and the world According to astrological beliefs, Goddess Durga's arrival on an elephant may bring peace and stability to India and the world. The current atmosphere of global unrest may calm down, and enemy countries may begin talks and improve their relations. It may also help spread a sense of brotherhood in society. 2. Stronger financial conditions The goddess arriving on an elephant is also considered a symbol of wealth, prosperity and abundance. Therefore, people may see greater financial stability after Sharadiya Navratri. Markets such as the stock market and real estate may see growth, while new job opportunities may also emerge. 3. Political changes According to astrology, Goddess Durga's departure on a rooster may bring political changes in India and across the world. These changes are believed to be positive. The ongoing conflict between the ruling parties and the opposition may reduce, while greater stability may also be seen in global politics.

stories.title: Ravita's love story behind husband's murder:Showed injuries to boyfriend on video calls; Meerut court sentences both to death
stories.summary: In Meerut, a court has sentenced Ravita, who had her husband Amit murdered and then had a snake bite him, and her lover Amardeep to death. Ravita, a mother of three, met Amardeep six months before Amit's murder. Amit had invited his friend Amardeep home for a meal. When Ravita served Amardeep dal and rice, he fell in love with her. One day, he came to her and confessed his feelings. A few days later, he handed Ravita a slip of paper with his mobile number written on it. Ravita video-called Amardeep and showed him the injuries from beatings on her body. She said, "My husband is cruel. He beats me a lot." As the two grew closer, they decided to live together. However, they began planning Amit's murder to make it appear that no one could suspect them. That is why they planned to have him bitten by a snake. Where did Amardeep and Ravita meet for the first time? How was their affair exposed in front of Amit? When did they plan the murder? To find out, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to police officers involved in the case. Read the report... They first met over a meal, and the lover gave her his mobile number on a slip In police custody, Amardeep and Ravita told their respective stories. Interrogation in separate rooms after their arrest revealed that their love story was only six months old. The question was what had happened that led them to plan Amit's murder in such a short time. Amardeep said, "I met Amit at a site about a year ago. We became friends because we worked together. This was in October 2024. I told him that it was difficult to find good food in the market, so one day he took me to his home for a meal. That was when I first met Ravita." I returned after eating lentils and rice, but I could not forget Ravita. Then one day, when I went to Amit's house to pick him up, I met Ravita again. That day, I told Ravita how I felt. She did not say anything, but looking into her eyes, I felt that she was ready too. I was afraid, so I did not try again. A month passed in this way. Then one day, we met at the market. That day, I wrote my mobile number on a slip of paper and gave it to her. Ravita then called me, and we began talking. Ravita told me, "Amit beats me; he is heartless. He has sex with me as if I were not his wife." Hearing all this, I became emotional. She also showed me the injuries on her body over a video call. Gradually, we decided that we would get married. I also started going to her house when Amit was away. Boyfriend said: Amit beat me on 23 March and threatened to kill me In the meantime, Amit found out about our affair. In fact, he had seen us together. After that, he said a lot to Ravita. I met Amit on 23 March 2025. He assaulted me then. I needed 15 stitches in my hand. After that, Amit sent four or five boys after me. They would appear along the way, and one or two of them also came to my house to summon me. But I did not go with them. After that, whenever Amit met me, he threatened me, saying, "I will kill you." He would say, "I will kill Ravita; I will cut her up." Meanwhile, Ravita told me that Amit was harassing her. They were quarrelling every day. I first told Ravita, "You should divorce him; after that, we will get married." But Amit was not ready for this. He insisted, "No matter what happens, I will not divorce you." Ravita searched: How to evade the police after committing murder Ravita said, "I cannot leave Amit like this. He has a family too; he must be removed from the way." After this, Ravita began searching on her mobile phone for ways to commit murder. The police found the following searches in her Google search history: "How to evade the police after committing murder?" and "Easy ways to commit murder." Meanwhile, one day, a neighbour again told Amit about Ravita's affair. That day, Amit beat Ravita. On 5 April 2025, Ravita called and said, "Arrange a snake. Amit now has to be eliminated." For the next seven days, the two of them kept thinking about how to kill Amit. What happened on the night of the murder, 12 April... A snake was arranged through Nikhil So that people would not become suspicious, Ravita took Amit to Saharanpur in the morning to visit the Mata Shakambhari Devi temple. From there, she continued posting videos of herself on Instagram. Meanwhile, Amardeep was arranging the snake. He told the police that he first spoke to a boy named Rajkumar, who lived in Bahsuma. Rajkumar gave him Nikhil's number. Nikhil arranged the deal with the snake charmer. The snake charmer took ₹1,000, placed the snake in a sack and handed it over to him. He then brought the snake home. Ravita quarrelled with Amit and went to sleep in the adjoining room Meanwhile, as planned, Ravita quarrelled with Amit after returning from Saharanpur. She took the children and went to sleep in the adjoining room. Ravita called me and said, "He has beaten me again. He will kill me. We have to finish the matter today. Bring the snake." I then went to her house, which was about 600 metres away. There was complete silence in the house. The two of us went into Amit's room. Amit was fast asleep. We tried to take the snake out of the sack, but became afraid that it might bite one of us. We suddenly did not know what to do. Then we decided to hold Amit's hands and legs and strangle him. Ravita held his hands while I strangled Amardeep. He kept flailing his arms and legs, but his body became still within 3 minutes. I then placed the snake beside Amit and left the house. How did the entire case come to light? Read on Children saw a snake on their father's bed On the morning of 13 April, Ravita's son went to his father's room to wake him up. He saw a snake on the bed. The boy began screaming when he saw it. Ravita, who was sleeping in another room, also ran towards Amit's room. Once there, she pretended to cry, scream and shout. A crowd of neighbours gathered at the scene. When they saw a live snake on the bed, they panicked. Everyone thought Amit had died after being bitten by the snake. A snake charmer was called, and he somehow caught the snake. A Forest Department team also reached the scene. The neighbours and relatives became convinced that the snake had bitten Amit throughout the night. There were snake-bite marks at 10 places on his body, but Amit's uncle became suspicious. He said, "We will have a post-mortem conducted before the cremation." The police were called. The post-mortem report revealed that Amit had died from strangulation. The presence of poison in his body was not established. The police then began questioning Ravita. After five hours of questioning, Ravita revealed the truth. After Amardeep's name emerged, he too was arrested. Ravita had said: Amit beats me and says he will make me a prostitute Ravita had told the police, "Amit beats me. After finding out about my affair, he used to threaten me, saying, 'I will make you engage in prostitution.' What could I do? Amit himself had arranged for me to speak to Amardeep." “Amit used to beat me badly. He had said that he would kill me. He wanted to turn me into a prostitute. So I planned to kill him with Amardeep. He brought the snake. I held Amit's hands and covered his mouth, while Amardeep strangled him. After that, we placed the snake under his body. Amardeep then went home.”

stories.summary: Om Prakash Rajbhar: उत्तर प्रदेश की राजनीति में बयानों और सियासी हमलों का दौर लगातार जारी है। इसी बीच समाजवादी पार्टी के प्रवक्ता आशुतोष वर्मा ने मंत्री ओम प्रकाश राजभर के बयान पर तीखी प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए उन पर निशाना साधा है। आशुतोष वर्मा ने राजभर की राजनीतिक स्थिति, उनकी पार्टी के भविष्य और भारतीय जनता पार्टी के साथ उनके संबंधों को लेकर तंज कसा। उन्होंने कहा कि ओपी राजभर की पार्टी में अब उनके बच्चों के अलावा कोई साथ नहीं रह गया है और उनके विधायक भी उनके साथ नहीं हैं। सपा प्रवक्ता ने दावा किया कि राजभर अब अपनी राजनीतिक पारी के अंतिम दौर में हैं और राजभर समाज भी उनसे आगे बढ़ चुका है। उन्होंने तंज भरे लहजे में कहा कि भाजपा में विलय करने से पहले उन्हें अपने बच्चों को सेट कर लेना चाहिए, वरना यह मौका भी हाथ से निकल सकता है। उनके इस बयान ने प्रदेश की सियासत में जुबानी जंग को और तेज कर दिया है।

stories.title: Mayawati fields Akash to boost BSP campaign:To hold rallies in 5 UP seats, Punjab and Uttarakhand
stories.summary: After making his fourth comeback in the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), Akash Anand is set to step up his political activities once again. Party chief Mayawati has assigned him the responsibility of addressing public meetings in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand. Seven public meetings are planned for Akash over the next two months. Candidates from several Assembly constituencies have also requested him to address rallies in their areas. His increased activity signals that Akash Anand is likely to play a more active role as the BSP prepares for the 2027 Assembly elections. Akash Anand to hold 7 public meetings across UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand The BSP central office has released the schedule of public meetings by party national coordinator Akash Anand. He will address five meetings in Uttar Pradesh, along with one each in Punjab and Uttarakhand, over the next two months. According to the schedule, meetings will be held in Anupshahr, Bulandshahr, on October 28; Nakur, Saharanpur, on November 2; Bikapur, Ayodhya, on November 20; Agra on November 22; and Bilhaur, Kanpur, on November 29. Meetings are also planned in Punjab on November 26 and Haridwar, Uttarakhand, on December 6. The venue for the Punjab meeting has not yet been finalised. Mayawati again expresses confidence in Akash After taking Akash Anand back into the party, BSP chief Mayawati appointed him national coordinator. He had earlier been expelled from the party. Following his return, Akash was also seen alongside Mayawati at the event marking Kanshi Ram's death anniversary on October 9, where he expressed his respect for her. With a series of public meetings now being planned, Mayawati appears to be preparing to give Akash an important role ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The programme is being seen as significant amid the ongoing discussions within the party between his supporters and opponents. He has addressed election rallies before Before his latest expulsion from the party, Akash Anand had addressed public meetings in Sadabad in Hathras and in Noida. The Sadabad meeting attracted attention across the country. Following his return to the BSP, preparations are now underway to send him to different regions once again. BSP candidates have also been requesting that Akash address rallies in their constituencies. Through these meetings, the party aims to increase activity among its workers and strengthen public outreach ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Eye on other communities alongside the Dalit vote Before the 2027 election, the BSP faces the challenge of retaining its traditional Dalit support base while increasing its support among other social groups. The proposed rallies in Anupshahr, Nakur, Bikapur, Agra and Bilhaur are significant in this regard. Through these programmes, the party may seek to strengthen its presence in different regions. Reaching Saini community voters and other backward classes in western Uttar Pradesh may also be part of the BSP's strategy. Meanwhile, by holding meetings in Punjab and Uttarakhand, the party is trying to activate its organisation in other states as well. 6 December rally also has political significance Akash Anand's last proposed rally will be held in Haridwar on 6 December. The day is observed as Dr B. R. Ambedkar's Mahaparinirvan Diwas. The date is ideologically and organisationally important for the BSP. In this context, Ambedkarite ideology, social justice and strengthening the organisation are likely to be the key issues at the Haridwar rally. Meanwhile, the Azad Samaj Party, led by its president Chandrashekhar Azad, has also proposed an event at the Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan in Lucknow on Constitution Day, 26 November. The programmes organised by the BSP will also be watched amid the growing activity of various parties in Dalit politics. When did Mayawati assign Akash responsibilities and when did she remove him? Find out 10 December 2023- Mayawati called a meeting of leaders from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. At the meeting, she declared Akash, the son of her youngest brother Anand Kumar, her successor. On 7 May 2024, Mayawati stripped Akash of all responsibilities over his inappropriate remarks. She removed him as national coordinator as well as from the post of successor. Mayawati said Akash was still immature. Mayawati reversed her decision 47 days later. 23 June 2024 She reinstated him as her successor and assigned him the responsibility of national coordinator, but on 2 March 2025, she again stripped him of all responsibilities. 3 March 2025- Mayawati expelled Akash from the party. She said Akash should have shown his maturity by expressing remorse. Instead, under the influence of his father-in-law, he became selfish and arrogant. 13 April- Mayawati forgave Akash. She had said, "I will not make Akash my successor." Three months later, that is, on 18 May, Mayawati once again appointed Akash chief national coordinator. She said Akash was being given a second chance. 29 August A new post of national convenor was created in the party, and Akash was given responsibility as national convenor. 3 September- Mayawati removed Akash from the post of national convenor. She said he still needed to become more mature. 9 September- Mayawati set a condition for handing responsibilities back to Akash: his father-in-law had to retire from political life. 10 September- Mayawati expelled him from the party. A few hours later, Akash's father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, announced his retirement from politics. Akash Anand married Pragya, daughter of Ashok Siddharth, on 26 March 2023. Mayawati also attended the wedding. -File photo Now read about Mayawati's recent decisions 6 September: After removing Akash, Mayawati assigned her nephew Ishan the responsibility of reviewing the organisation in 19 states. 13 September: Mayawati announced that not only Akash but Ishan, too, would not be given any position in the party. She indicated that her niece, Deepika Anand, would be promoted within the party. Akash Entered Politics in 2017​​ Akash Anand was seen with Mayawati at a public rally in Saharanpur in 2017. He then continued working for the party. He was appointed national coordinator in 2019. After this, the BSP-SP alliance broke up. At the time, it emerged that Mayawati had ended the alliance at Akash's behest. Akash Anand's name appeared on the list of star campaigners for the first time during the 2022 Himachal Pradesh Assembly election. Akash pursued a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in London.

stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused the Samajwadi Party (SP) of giving away its Rajya Sabha tickets to wealthy people in exchange for money. Speaking at a public meeting in Ghaziabad on Friday, he claimed that the party could have contested two or three seats but chose to give its tickets to others. Without naming SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, Yogi said, “You have seen how the Samajwadi Party has worked to sell tickets in the Rajya Sabha election. They could have contested two or three seats. But I have been saying from the beginning that the SP's PDA means ‘Parivar Development Authority’.” He added, “They gave their first ticket to their uncle. The BJP had said that PDA means ‘Paraya Dhan Apna’ — making someone else's wealth one's own. In this situation, they mortgaged their second ticket to a wealthy man from Mumbai. This is their true character.” Yogi addresses MLC election meeting in Ghaziabad Yogi was speaking at a public meeting for the MLC graduates' and teachers' constituency elections at Sunderdeep Deemed University in Dasna, Ghaziabad. Dinesh Kumar Goyal and Shrichand Sharma are contesting the election. Goyal is from Ghaziabad, while Sharma is from Gautam Buddh Nagar. Voters from the Meerut and Saharanpur divisions will cast their votes in the election. Before the meeting, the Chief Minister was scheduled to inspect the sewage treatment plant (STP) in Indirapuram. However, the inspection programme was cancelled. Know Yogi's 8 key points 1- 'Durga Puja pandals could not be set up under the SP government' Yogi said that during the Samajwadi Party's rule, Kanwar yatras, Ramleela performances and Durga Puja pandals faced restrictions. He claimed that if the SP were in power today, there would be riots and curfews. He said grand Ramleela performances are now being held at several places during Sharadiya Navratri, with no unrest during Kanwar yatras. 2- ‘Development was a distant prospect under the SP government’ Yogi accused the SP of neglecting development, education and employment. He said that during its four terms in power, the state faced crises related to security, development, identity and jobs. He claimed that riots, curfews, loot, damaged roads and power shortages had become the state's identity under the SP government. 3- ‘SP followed different rules for education’ Yogi alleged that the SP government followed different standards for educational institutions. Referring to Azam Khan's university, he claimed that it received different treatment, while other institutions seeking recognition faced difficulties. He said the BJP government had introduced the same rules for everyone and followed the principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”. 4- ‘Religious sites are being developed under the BJP government’ Yogi said grand corridors had been built at the Kashi Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini temples, while a grand Ram temple had been built in Ayodhya. He also referred to development in Mathura-Vrindavan and the ongoing corridor project at the Maa Shakumbhari Devi temple in Saharanpur. He said an elevated road near the temple would be completed after this year to make visits easier for devotees. 5- ‘Most districts in UP now have a medical college’ Yogi said universities had been established in Aligarh, Moradabad, Azamgarh, Balrampur, Mirzapur and Saharanpur. He also cited the sports university in Meerut, the Ayush university in Gorakhpur, the agricultural university in Kushinagar and a university for persons with disabilities in Bundelkhand. He claimed that most districts in Uttar Pradesh now had a medical college. 6- ‘Those who play with youth employment will go to jail’ Yogi said Uttar Pradesh was now known for “One District, One Product” rather than “One District, One Mafia”. He said travel between Meerut and Prayagraj now takes around six hours and pointed to metro services in Meerut, Ghaziabad, Noida, Kanpur and Lucknow as signs of development. He added that the BJP government had provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh people in nine years. He warned that anyone who interfered with young people's employment would face jail and action against their property. 7- ‘SP cannot be trusted on education’ Yogi accused the SP of playing with the future of young people and opposing education. Comparing the party to a crocodile that promises to help people cross a river but instead drowns them, he said the SP could not be trusted to fulfil its promises on education. 8- ‘Yogi appeals to voters to elect BJP candidates’ Yogi appealed to teachers and graduate voters in the Meerut division to ensure the victory of BJP candidates in both the teachers' and graduates' constituency elections. He said voters in the division had supported the party earlier and expressed confidence that they would do so again. The Election Commission has declared October 23 a holiday in connection with the elections.

stories.title: Accused opens fire at police during Rajkot robbery-murder panchnama:PSI shoots him in leg in retaliation; former employee plotted crime after being fired
stories.summary: In the sensational robbery-cum-murder case at Tanvi Gold Refinery in Rajkot, the main shooter, Anurag Singh Rajput, who allegedly opened fire during the robbery, attacked the police team when he was taken to the scene to prepare a panchnama and collect evidence. Anurag suddenly fired two rounds at police personnel using another concealed weapon that he had hidden at the spot, triggering panic and chaos. Following the sudden attack on the police team, Crime Branch PSI Vanrajsinh Dodiya showed presence of mind and exceptional courage, immediately returning fire in self-defence. The bullet fired by the PSI struck Anurag in the leg, causing him to collapse to the ground in a pool of blood. The police immediately took him into custody. Anurag, who sustained serious injuries after being shot in the leg, was rushed to Rajkot Civil Hospital for treatment under tight police security. Following the attack on the police, senior police officers also rushed to the scene and the hospital. Property worth more than ₹1.52 crore recovered The police have solved the case involving the murder of Laljibhai Sardhara and the robbery of 1 kg of gold and 3 kg of silver outside Tanvi Gold Refinery in Rajkot's Aji GIDC area on 14 October, when he was shot at three times. Teams from Rajkot City Police carried out the operation in coordination with police from three to four districts and two states. They arrested all 10 accused belonging to a notorious Uttar Pradesh gang within just 9 hours. The police successfully recovered 100% of the stolen property, including the gold and silver, worth more than ₹1.52 crore in total. Gold hidden in shoes and car seat covers Joint Police Commissioner Chaitanya Mandlik said that after carrying out the robbery, the accused had cleverly concealed the gold and silver bars inside their shoes and car seat covers to evade the police investigation. However, with the help of AI technology, the CCTV network and human intelligence, the police traced the links between the accused and arrested all 10 of them along with the stolen property. The Home Minister has also praised the Rajkot Police for this swift success. Former employee emerged as mastermind, current staff member provided a tip-off The police investigation has revealed that the robbery was not a sudden incident but a planned conspiracy. Ashwinikumar, aka Lankesh Singh, who had previously worked at Tanvi Gold Refinery for 5-6 months, was the alleged mastermind behind the crime. Meanwhile, Shaileshkumar Kherwa aka Shailendra Singh, who currently works at the refinery, provided all the inside information. Shailesh kept Lankesh informed about every development, including exactly when the manager would leave with the refined gold and silver. Lankesh had given clear instructions to his associates to shoot anyone who came in their way during the robbery. Fired three rounds and sped away in the car at 120 km/h On 14 October, when the manager was travelling to the showroom on an Activa carrying gold bars and silver dust powder from the refinery, people in a maroon Tata Tigor tried to snatch the bag. When Laljibhai Sardhara and the security guard resisted, accused Anurag Singh Rajput fired three precise rounds at Laljibhai, causing serious injuries that proved fatal. After the robbery, the accused sped towards Chotila at 120 km/h, where they changed vehicles and fled towards Rajasthan and Morbi in a Kia Sonet and an Eicher. Arrests made in a joint operation across Rajasthan, Morbi and Rajkot By imposing roadblocks and tracing vehicle routes, the police obtained assistance from the Rajasthan Police. A total of 10 accused have been arrested – six from Pindwara and Udaipur in Rajasthan, three from Morbi and one from Rajkot. All the accused are residents of Chandauli, Ghazipur and Mau districts in Uttar Pradesh. Among those arrested, cases of attempted murder had previously been registered in Uttar Pradesh against Ashwini, aka Lankesh, and Ajit Kumar Pandey, a case of culpable homicide against Anurag Singh, and criminal cases in Haryana against Shailesh Kherwa. 'E-beat system' to be implemented in Rajkot for security To enhance the security of traders and citizens during the festive season, the police department has prepared a special action plan. The city will be divided into different beats and round-the-clock patrolling will be launched. In addition, a digital 'e-beat system' will be implemented in the coming days, ensuring online tracking of all police patrolling and checking activities.

stories.title: Girl who abused Chandrashekhar says, 'We are staunch Brahmins':Claims rapes happened under Akhilesh’s government, arrested by Gonda police
stories.summary: Pallavi Shukla, a woman from Gonda who had abused Chandrashekhar Azad, has made objectionable remarks against Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav. The social media creator posted a video on Facebook in which she said, “We are staunch Brahmins. No matter what happens, we will never support Yadavs.” Pallavi said that the bicycle, the SP's election symbol, would always remain rusty, while the lotus would continue to bloom. She also said that anyone could file as many cases against her as they wanted. Following a complaint by Gonda SP leader Waqar Khan, Kaudiya police arrested Pallavi from her home at around 4:15 pm. Posted a 1-minute, 46-second video In the video, Pallavi said that the person who had created a video of Akhilesh Yadav using AI should delete it. She then abused the Yadav community and said that she did not support Yadavs because she belonged to the Brahmin community. She also said that her father was a staunch Hindu. Pallavi said that people could be angry or happy with her, but she would continue to speak the truth. She claimed that girls were raped and were not safe under the SP government. She added that the lotus would continue to bloom. Making further objectionable remarks against Akhilesh Yadav, she said that the bicycle had become rusty when the SP came to power. She also made comments about people who eat meat and chicken, saying they try to present themselves as a brand. She further said that the bicycle could not be trusted because it could get punctured anywhere on the road. Throughout the video, Pallavi abused Akhilesh Yadav four times and used abusive language against the Yadav community an equal number of times. She also made offensive comments about the Muslim community. Lives in a village in Gonda, has over 42,000 Facebook followers Pallavi Shukla is a resident of Baunapur village under the Kaudiya police station area in Gonda. She has more than 42,000 followers on Facebook. Her father, Panchanan Shukla, is a farmer, and she has studied up to Class 12. Her brother went missing seven years ago and has not been found yet. Pallavi makes reels on Bhojpuri songs and posts them on Facebook. According to the report, her family has distanced itself from her. Case registered earlier for abusing Chandrashekhar After the video went viral, SP leader Waqar Khan, the party's in-charge for the Katra Bazar Assembly constituency, filed a complaint at the Kaudiya police station. Station House Officer Shashi Kumar Rana said police took note of the viral video, registered a case against Pallavi Shukla and arrested her. Earlier, Pallavi had also abused Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad and members of the Scheduled Caste community. On July 3 this year, a case was registered against her at the Kaudiya police station based on a complaint by sub-inspector Sheshmani Pandey. She was accused of abusing Chandrashekhar and threatening to beat him with shoes and slippers.

stories.title: 2 die after oxygen cylinder-loaded pickup hits divider:Both were trapped in the cabin after the collision in Lucknow; third person critical
stories.summary: Two people died and a third person is in critical condition after an oxygen cylinder-loaded pickup truck collided with a divider in Lucknow on Friday evening. The accident took place near the Sheikhpura toll plaza in the Nigohan area. The impact badly damaged the front of the pickup, trapping two people inside the cabin. The collision was so powerful that the oxygen cylinders loaded in the vehicle scattered across the road. Nigohan police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. With the help of local residents, they rescued the trapped people and rushed the injured to the Mohanlalganj Community Health Centre (CHC). The identities of the injured people have not yet been established. Police got the cylinders scattered across the road removed and restored normal traffic. See 2 pictures... Two people trapped inside the cabin At around 4:30 p.m. on Friday, Nigohan police received information that a pickup loaded with oxygen cylinders had collided with a divider near the Sheikhpura toll plaza. As soon as the information was received, the Nigohan station house officer reached the spot with a police team. The front of the pickup had been crushed in the collision, trapping two people, including the driver, inside the cabin. Efforts under way to identify the injured With the help of local residents, the police pulled both people out and sent them to the Mohanlalganj Community Health Centre for treatment. The oxygen cylinders loaded in the pickup had scattered across the road during the accident. The police and local residents collected the cylinders and had them placed in a safe location. The obstruction was then cleared from the road and traffic was restored to normal. Efforts are under way to identify the injured.

stories.title: Akhilesh says he opposes BJP's conspiracy, not SIR or SSR:Submits data on voter list irregularities in 100 seats to EC
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav once again accused the BJP of conspiring to manipulate the voter list. He said his party was not opposed to SIR or SSR, but to the alleged conspiracy and irregularities involved in the process. He demanded that the voter list should be revised only once. There should be no repeated revisions. The process of adding or deleting names should be completed during that revision. The former chief minister held a press conference at the party office on Friday. During the event, former BJP MP Rajpal and state executive member Harbir Malik joined the party. Akhilesh Yadav claimed that the BJP's core voters were moving away from it. Sanatanis, women, the middle class and young people were also angry with the party. This was why a conspiracy was now being carried out in collusion with the Election Commission to manipulate the voter list, he said. He said the Samajwadi Party had submitted data from 100 Assembly constituencies to the Election Commission, showing irregularities carried out or orchestrated by the BJP. Key points from Akhilesh Yadav's press conference... 1- Claim that one young man is registered to vote in several places Giving an example of alleged irregularities in the voter lists, Akhilesh Yadav said his party had submitted data from 100 assembly constituencies to the Election Commission. He referred to a young man who is set to vote for the first time, but whose name is alleged to be registered in several places. Akhilesh said the young man is educated and honest. He will cast his vote at only one place, but other people could vote in his name elsewhere. He sought a response from the Election Commission on the matter and targeted the BJP. He said the issue of 20 booth-level officers (BLOs) losing their lives during the SIR had also come to light. Akhilesh alleged that when evidence of irregularities in the voter list emerges, attempts are made to brush them aside by calling them minor errors. He also questioned the role of the Election Commission. 2- Workers were present at booths on 17 and 24 Akhilesh appealed to party workers to get voters' names added during the campaigns to be held at polling booths on 17 and 24 October. He said the process of adding and deleting names from the electoral roll should be transparent. 3-There should be no second revision after SSR The Samajwadi Party chief demanded that there should be no second revision after SSR. He alleged that the BJP starts responding whenever questions are raised with the Election Commission. He also questioned the role of companies such as TCS. 4-BJP voters are moving away from it Akhilesh Yadav said that voters from several sections who traditionally support the BJP were angry with the party. According to him, Sanatani voters were upset by allegations of theft involving donations and religious offerings. Women were also angry. He alleged that a mother had been insulted after the fire incident in Lucknow. He said the middle class was troubled by inflation and corruption. Young people were angry over alleged irregularities in examinations such as NEET. Akhilesh claimed that Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha, as well as beneficiaries of government schemes, were also moving away from the BJP. Taking a jibe at the BJP, he said the party spoke of "One Nation, One Election", but its intention was more like "One Corruption, One Election". 5- y for the panchayat elections Asked about the panchayat elections, Akhilesh Yadav said he was ready for every election. He alleged that the financial burden on village heads had increased and that the position of panchayat representatives had weakened. Alleging irregularities in the Kundarki and Meerapur by-elections, he said that after this, the Election Commission changed the rules related to providing CCTV footage. Akhilesh also claimed that no action had been taken on Nandlal Nishad's complaint. Former BJP MP Rajpal Saini joins the Samajwadi Party Akhilesh Yadav welcomed BJP leader and former MP Rajpal Saini, BJP state executive committee member Harbir Malik and other leaders who joined the party. He said that strengthening mutual love, compassion and a sense of belonging would make the PDA family stronger. A large number of people from the Kashyap, Dalit and other communities have joined the Samajwadi Party. This will increase the party's strength and public support. Akhilesh said, "This is only the beginning. Legislators have not yet been welcomed. There are many of them as well. There are also several parties that are bargaining. Once they have worked out their calculations, we will turn our attention to them as well." SP national general secretary Shivpal Singh Yadav said that the SP's caravan was moving ahead rapidly. Several influential people from the state are joining the party under Akhilesh Yadav's leadership. He claimed that in the 2027 Assembly election, the people of the state, including farmers, the poor and the youth, would work to form an SP government. -------------------- Read this news too... Minister Rajbhar says a dozen SP MLAs are in touch, all eager to join Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar took a swipe at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, saying that the election is to be held in Uttar Pradesh, but Akhilesh is staging protests in Delhi. He said Akhilesh would have gained even 10 votes if he had visited a village in Uttar Pradesh, but instead he was going to Delhi and telling lies. Rajbhar claimed that around a dozen SP MLAs were in touch with him. Read the full story...

stories.title: Rajbhar says government is ready for panchayat polls:Awaiting OBC Commission report, clarity expected in a month
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said the government was ready to hold the panchayat elections and was only waiting for the OBC Commission's report. The government would announce the election dates immediately after receiving it. According to Rajbhar, the state government set up the OBC Commission on the Supreme Court's orders. The commission is working to determine OBC reservation for the panchayat elections and will submit its report within a month. Speaking at a membership enrolment ceremony held at the SBSP headquarters, he said: "The Allahabad High Court has ordered the government to hold the panchayat elections within three months. The government welcomes this decision. We are ready to comply with the High Court's order. The election process will be taken forward as soon as the commission's report arrives. After that, there will be no need to approach the Supreme Court. Ballot papers have already reached the districts. We will not back out of the elections." 'In SP, P stands for dynastic politics and D stands for the wealthy' Rajbhar also targeted Akhilesh Yadav and the Samajwadi Party. He said it was the Samajwadi Party's leaders who had approached the High Court over the panchayat elections. During his tenure, Akhilesh Yadav promoted only certain castes. If his intentions had been honest, young people from the Nai, Rajbhar and Banjara communities would also have been given the opportunity to become police constables. Taking a jibe at the Samajwadi Party's PDA (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) slogan, Rajbhar said its truth was exposed in the Rajya Sabha elections. He alleged that the "P" in the Samajwadi Party stood for dynastic politics, which was why Ram Gopal Yadav was sent to the Rajya Sabha. The "D", meanwhile, stood for wealth. He questioned the decision to give Parimal Nathwani an opportunity. Instead of giving leaders from other castes a chance, the Samajwadi Party prioritised wealthy people. 76 leaders from the SP, LJP and VHP join the SBSP Leaders and workers from several parties joined the SBSP at the membership ceremony. All of them joined the party in the presence of Om Prakash Rajbhar.

stories.title: Five family members killed in Bulandshahr car crash:Vehicle hits tree at 100 kmph, three critically injured
stories.summary: Five people from the same family were killed and three others were seriously injured after a speeding Maruti Eeco van crashed into a roadside tree in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, on Friday. Eight people were travelling in the van when the accident took place. The family was on its way from Sidhpura in Kasganj district to the historic Belon temple in Dibai to offer prayers. The accident took place in the Narora police station area of Dibai tehsil, around 40 km from the district headquarters. The impact was so severe that the van was badly damaged, leaving the occupants trapped inside. Cries for help were heard at the spot. Eyewitnesses said the van appeared to be travelling at more than 100 kmph. The collision was so powerful that it sounded like an explosion. Two women, three men and three children were in the van A total of eight family members were travelling in the van. They included two women, three men, an 11-year-old girl, a five-year-old child and a one-year-old girl. Five people died in the accident. The deceased included a one-year-old girl, a woman aged around 35 and three men aged approximately 40 to 45 years. Police rescued the injured and sent them to hospital After receiving information about the accident, local police reached the spot and began rescue work. Police and local residents helped pull the injured and the deceased out of the damaged van. The three injured people were taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital for initial treatment. Due to their serious condition, doctors referred them to a higher medical centre. Five deaths leave family and village in mourning Administrative officials reached the spot to assess the situation. The bodies were taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examinations. The deaths of five members of the same family have left their native village, Sidhpura in Kasganj district, in mourning. Their relatives are devastated by the sudden loss. See the pictures- The story is being continuously updated...
