Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh has argued that this change jeopardizes the integrity of the census.

stories.title: Brad Paisley and wife pledged $1 million for a free grocery store in 2024; it opened in 2026
stories.summary: Brad Paisley and Kimberly Williams-Paisley have expanded their philanthropic efforts by launching a second location of The Store, a nonprofit grocery aimed at combating food insecurity in Nashville. Following their first store's success in 2020, which garnered over 3,100 dedicated volunteers, the couple has invested $1 million into this new initiative to ensure families receive dignified access to food choices and additional resources.

stories.title: Retirement Fuels Bushland Restoration: Ken and Jill revive 970ha bush; older Australians follow
stories.summary: In their eighties, Ken and Jill Hooper have become dedicated stewards of bushland in Australia, showcasing an inspiring commitment to conservation post-retirement. Over the last twenty years, after acquiring properties in Victoria and New South Wales, they focus on enhancing biodiversity and curbing invasive species to safeguard native wildlife. Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV to be discharged from hospital after successful lung cancer surgery today
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to leave the hospital after a successful lung cancer surgery, demonstrating commendable recovery progress. He engaged positively with his senior aides, expressing heartfelt gratitude towards the medical team for their dedicated care. As doctors await crucial test results to plan further treatment, the pontiff's upcoming trip to Latin America from November 6 to 17 highlights his determination to fulfill his commitments.

stories.title: ‘JD wanted to chat with us real quick’: How Trump’s press secretary was fired mid-interview
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia's brief tenure as White House press secretary ended abruptly after just five days due to a rocky start marked by an underwhelming briefing and questions regarding her qualifications. Despite Donald Trump's warning to reconsider the role, she was determined to fulfill her duties to the president and the nation. Her departure leaves the press office in limbo, especially with midterm elections approaching.

stories.title: Islandwide Power Outage: Sri Lanka hit by multi-hour blackout; hydropower failure probed
stories.summary: Sri Lanka faced a significant power outage that affected the entire island for over three hours. Essential services such as water supply, internet, and mobile connectivity were disrupted during this time. Authorities are investigating the cause, with a potential failure at a hydropower station being considered. Citizens were warned to conserve water due to the impact on supplies from power cuts.

stories.title: Stalin turns fire on Congress over SIR; serves up Bihar, Soren exit reminder
stories.summary: MK Stalin endorsed protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and criticized Congress for its inconsistent positions. During a DMK Parliamentary Party meeting, four resolutions were adopted, including the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The DMK emphasized its early opposition to the SIR process and questioned Congress's credibility on the issue. Resolutions included support for student protests and criticism of local party leaders’ silence.

stories.title: CJI flags ‘external forces’ that threatened to disrupt NLSIU convocation in his address
stories.summary: At the NLSIU convocation ceremony in Bengaluru, Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged external challenges that threatened the event, inspiring graduates to champion legal principles with unwavering integrity. Deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar reinforced the notion of law as a civic duty, sharing plans to bolster the state's legal system. Students were proudly awarded their degrees, marking the start of their professional journeys in the legal field.

stories.title: US ranchers win pipeline compensation fight but face $300,000 legal bill, Supreme Court to hear case
stories.summary: A group of North Dakota ranchers who spent nearly $300,000 fighting a pipeline company over land compensation have taken their dispute over legal expenses to the US Supreme Court. Although they reached a settlement, an appeals court ruled that the company need not cover their legal costs. The Supreme Court will hear the case on November 9.

stories.title: 10 charred to death in fire at seaside resort in Bangladesh
stories.summary: At least 10 people were killed and nine injured after a fire gutted a three-storey seaside resort in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar district early Saturday, The Express Tribune reported. The blaze broke out around 6.30am at TUPTUP Resto and Resort, built mainly of bamboo and wood. The cause remains unknown, while several people’s whereabouts were unclear. Injured victims were taken to hospital.

stories.title: Stephen King’s $3 million pledge helped transform hometown library into a $9.6 million project
stories.summary: Stephen and Tabitha King have committed $3 million to the Bangor Public Library renovation, provided that $6 million is raised through community efforts. Thanks to local support and a municipal bond, the library hit its $9 million target, kickstarting essential upgrades like roof repairs and improved community spaces, honoring both its historical significance and modern audience requirements.

stories.title: Forgotten John Constable Painting: $37 buy authenticated at $315,000; other 2024 finds hidden in plain sight
stories.summary: Hidden away in a cupboard for years, a painting believed to be by John Constable was recently found and has skyrocketed in value from its auction price of $37 to an astounding $315,000. This extraordinary revelation joins the ranks of remarkable discoveries, like a rare Lego mask and a Victorian brooch, which emphasize that ordinary objects can possess extraordinary worth.

stories.title: Snakes Found Inside Airport: Venomous western browns spotted in terminal; experts explain heat-driven visits
stories.summary: As summer approaches, Alice Springs Airport is preparing for an influx of snake sightings, with multiple reports emerging from terminal areas. In response, the airport management has put in place monitoring systems and hired professionals for safe snake removal. Travelers are encouraged to remain alert and immediately report any sightings to airport personnel, emphasizing safety first in this reptilian season.

stories.title: ‘Law and order does not exist’: SAD chief Badal holds CM Mann responsible for Punjab anti-drug activist’s murder
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal has held Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann accountable for the breakdown of law and order following the tragic murder of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh, also known as Jhota. The incident occurred during an altercation over drug sales at a pharmacy. CM Mann expressed his regret over the incident and assured citizens of a comprehensive investigation.

stories.title: ‘Nepalese nationals added to Goa voter rolls’: GFP chief claims SIR irregularities, seeks probe
‘Agenda to set country on fire’: BJP retorts to opposition’s ‘regime change’ call
In 2013, Tope Awotona emptied about $200,000 of his savings to build Calendly; eight years later investors valued the company at $3 billion
stories.summary: In 2013, Tope Awotona launched Calendly to tackle the difficulties professionals face in scheduling meetings. His journey began with personal funds, retirement savings, and loans, slowly gathering momentum. By 2021, Calendly had soared to a valuation exceeding $3 billion, driven by a booming user base and the demand for streamlined online scheduling.

stories.title: Sanjay Raut submits explanation in SC contempt case, says ‘we expect justice’
DMK seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, rules out joint protests with Congress
stories.summary: DMK has called a parliamentary party meeting emphasizing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They are demanding the immediate dismissal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and urge for an inquiry into his conduct. The party criticized Congress for perceived hypocrisy in its stance on the revisions while denouncing police actions against protests at Jantar Mantar. Furthermore, DMK MPs are set to discuss their grievances with President Droupadi Murmu.

stories.title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
New York’s Plaza Hotel to close for four years to restore its historic facade
stories.summary: Starting in January 2027, New York City's iconic Plaza Hotel will embark on a significant facade restoration that is projected to last a minimum of four years. This closure will impact not only guests but also local residents. With previous renovations totaling $450 million between 2005 and 2008, and a pandemic-related shutdown in 2020, this restoration seeks to uphold the hotel's renowned architectural significance for generations to come.

stories.title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has declared that internet access is a fundamental right applicable to all, including children. This decision reinforces the significance of achieving a balance between safety and individual freedoms online for minors. Moreover, the court advocates for enhancements in identifying harmful content. This landmark ruling builds upon earlier verdicts that recognized digital access as a constitutional entitlement.

stories.title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee faces court warrants over 2018 video targeting BJP IT cell
‘He spoke to Putin to buy diesel’: Ex-diplomat Fabian after Trump waives sanctions over Russian oil
McClellan base closed in 2001; 25 years later, its 3,000-acre site boasts $600m in investment
stories.summary: Following its shutdown in 2001, McClellan Air Force Base prompted worries about economic decline. However, the area has been revitalized with McClellan Park, which boasts a $600 million investment and encompasses 10 million square feet of facilities. The site now functions as a public-use regional hub, enhancing local transportation and offering significant employment opportunities, while also emphasizing environmental restoration initiatives since the base's closure.

stories.title: Indian woman jailed over son’s fatal stabbing faces possible deportation from UK
stories.summary: Kiran Kaur, convicted for aiding her son’s murder, has been sentenced to three years. Her son, Vickrum Digwa, is serving life for fatally stabbing an 18-year-old student. Kaur may face deportation back to India if released early under a government initiative. This case highlights concerns over religious symbols linked to violence. Appeals from both Kaur and Digwa are set to be heard in November.

stories.title: ‘Foreign-inspired terrorism no longer visible’: Home Secy Govind Mohan on changing internal security landscape
‘Why is govt scared?’ Congress’s Vijay Wadettiwar slams Centre over delimitation, delay in all-party meet
Encounter breaks out between security forces, terrorists in J&K’s Kupwara
BJP veteran LK Advani in ICU under medical observation after chest infection
'Verify before she vilifies': India rejects UN rapporteur's claims on youth protests
Iran broke? $25bn oil loss, $350m crypto frozen as militias send money back to IRGC
‘Opposition’s duty is to oppose, expose, depose’: Congress defends ‘regime change’ remark
PM Modi to visit Canada on December 11-12, Mark Carney confirms after phone call
Zelenskyy terms Russian peace moves a ‘parody’, slams Trump deal
Order to limit satellite system used by Ukraine came from White House: Report
'Women ought to be released after sunset': Neha Bora questions night-long detentions over anti-SIR stir
Delhi protest: Dipke held under preventive detention, to face magistrate; AISA's Neha Bora released
Congress: Never hid aim of toppling govt through democratic means
SPO missing with his rifle found dead in J&K’s Kishtwar
Centre deviating from assurances, say Ladakh groups
J&K outcry & probe after senior IAS ‘abuses’ woman junior
Higher duties at lower pay amount to workplace exploitation, says J&K HC
'Been more than 10 hours': CJP claims Abhijeet Dipke 'kidnapped' by Delhi Police
Kharge writes to PM Modi: Call all-party meet on delimitation bill
Govt ropes in aided, private teachers, PSU staff for Census work
FSSAI notice to Radisson Blu, BigBasket over safety lapses
PM Modi, Trump to meet in Manila next month?
Entrepreneur lists Aston Martin-designed home for $19.5m
stories.summary: Selling for $19.5 million, David Ingram's architecturally magnificent Hudson Valley home, designed by Aston Martin, is now available. The residence includes broad living spaces and striking details, reflecting five years of enhancements since he bought it in 2020. Noteworthy features include a swimming pool and an underground automotive gallery. Now focused on his wellness endeavors, Ingram rarely visits, prompting this sale of his exquisite property.

stories.title: Ahead of polls, Amit Shah attacks Mann govt for drug menace
stories.summary: State CM Counters Shah With Drug Seizure In Gujarat

stories.title: Amid empty seats, govt slashes dental PG cut-off
Government rebuts opposition's charge, defends Jaishankar-Rubio Mumbai meet
stories.summary: Cites Earlier Instances Of Foreign Leaders Being Hosted Outside Delhi

stories.title: Historic Ojai Tudor once home to composer Leo Robin sells for $4.6 million
stories.summary: Ojai's prestigious Estelle Clark Estate, emblematic of Tudor Revival architecture, has fetched $4.6 million after its initial listing at $6.495 million. This estate, built for the glamorous silent-film star Estelle Clark, also boasts a legacy linked to acclaimed composer Leo Robin. The appeal of historically rich and restored homes continues to thrive among buyers in the Ojai area.

stories.title: Indianapolis Dam Removal Project: City dismantles Emrichsville Dam; wildlife passage restored
stories.summary: The city of Indianapolis is set to dismantle the Emrichsville Dam as part of an initiative to revitalize the White River's natural flow. This endeavor is designed to improve aquatic habitats and ensure the safety of river goers. Funding has been obtained from a variety of federal and state organizations to assist with this project.

stories.title: California land trust sues to block roads across a 402-acre preserve saved from housing development
stories.summary: In a bid to protect the Clover Valley nature preserve, Placer Land Trust has initiated a lawsuit to block infrastructure development attempts. Established four years ago, this cherished area has faced housing pressures in the past. It comprises ancient oak forests, wetlands, and vital archaeological sites. The conservation easement was created to enforce permanent protection, and the legal proceedings will reinforce this against any existing development rights.

stories.title: Five women in Trump’s world who made headlines in last 15 days: Katie Zacharia overtakes Anthony Scaramucci in record of shortest tenure
‘For 5 hrs, no one knew where she was’: AISA says Neha Bora detained at RK Puram police station
Don't tinker with any documents, never alter or backdate: Immigration expert's warnings to H-1B applicants in India
Submerged Archaeological Sites Study: Researchers map two underwater Aboriginal sites; stone moved 23 km
stories.summary: Archaeologists collaborated with Indigenous rangers to explore submerged sites off Murujuga in Western Australia. They uncovered artefacts and evidence of past human activity before rising sea levels altered the landscape. Two key locations highlighted interactions with freshwater resources and elevated terrains. The research involved several universities and emphasized the importance of Indigenous expertise in cultural heritage.

stories.title: Miami teen becomes ‘Spider-Man of Brickell’ after brave chase
stories.summary: Harry Cossyphas, a Miami high school senior, became a local hero after chasing a theft suspect. He witnessed a robbery and immediately pursued the man into an alley, despite being pepper-sprayed. Cossyphas managed to tackle the suspect and hold him until the police arrived. The Miami Police honored him with a hero award and acknowledged his bravery and prompt response. The suspect, Yagiz Dogan, was charged with third-degree grand theft.

stories.title: Edinburgh's historic Palm Houses reopen after a £23.5m restoration replaced 5,750 panes of glass
stories.summary: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's Palm Houses have undergone extensive restorations costing £23.5 million over the past five years. Researchers carefully replaced all 5,750 glass panes to ensure they withstand harsh weather conditions. Following this work, nearly 600 rare plant specimens have been replanted in the glasshouses. The restoration enables continued conservation, education, and scientific discovery efforts related to endangered flora.

stories.title: Texas courthouse vacant since 1977 faces demolition after $120 million repair estimates
stories.summary: In a decisive move, Nueces County officials have voted unanimously to proceed with the demolition of the aged 1914 courthouse, which has seen a decline over the decades and thwarted multiple redevelopment attempts. Expected to last around 130 days, the demolition aims to create opportunities for future development while eliminating continuous security expenses for taxpayers. While some historical artifacts will be saved, extensive asbestos contamination complicates the safe removal process.

stories.title: Doe House Listed At $27 Million: 1908 Pacific Heights mansion hits market; bay views meet modern luxury
stories.summary: Built in 1908 for timber magnate Frank P. Doe, Doe House merges historic charm with modern amenities. Spanning 8,175 square feet, it boasts seven spacious bedrooms and ample outdoor spaces. Nestled in Pacific Heights, the mansion offers breathtaking views of Lafayette Park and San Francisco Bay. With its recent renovations that preserve the original Edwardsian style, this $27 million estate is a remarkable find for discerning buyers.

stories.title: Historic Inn Becomes Commons: Community restores 1901 landmark; raised to cut flooding risk
stories.summary: The former Island Inn on Ocracoke Island has been reborn as a vibrant community and cultural hub, thanks to the passionate efforts of local residents and the Ocracoke Preservation Society. Faced with the threat of redevelopment, they successfully restored the historic building, which now hosts a variety of educational programs and community gatherings. Key renovations improved its safety and flood resilience.

stories.title: Natalie Harp printed out Susie Wiles' ouster speculation report; Trump 'blew up' leading to White House 'freakout'
Two vessels carrying 24 Indian seafarers hit by projectiles, drone in separate incidents; all safe
stories.summary: Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two vessels carrying Indian seafarers were attacked in October. The MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, while the YARA J was hit by a drone off Romania. Fortunately, all 24 Indian nationals aboard both vessels are reported safe and unharmed. India has condemned attacks on commercial vessels, citing concerns for the safety of seafarers.

stories.title: 'American workers should come first in their own country': Republicans bring new bill to make H-1B visa salary threshold $140,000
‘Don’t have to do this’: Trump tells new press secy Zacharia she can quit if she wants
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia has faced significant scrutiny after her brief tenure as White House press secretary. Donald Trump expressed concerns about the job's challenges and suggested she reconsider her position. The media has provided harsh coverage of her professional background and recent press briefing. Despite his doubts, Trump emphasized that the decision about her future is ultimately up to her.

stories.title: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as new report shows spike in civilian casualties
stories.summary: Russia's recent strikes have plunged Ukraine into darkness, impacting electricity for hundreds of thousands and resulting in civilian injuries. Amidst this turmoil, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced his worries over diminishing US support during a summit in Brussels. Civilian casualties surged by 85% in September compared to last year, as Ukraine urgently calls for more military aid while the EU seeks to enhance its support for the beleaguered nation.

stories.title: US tells election officials to guard against AI-powered cyber threats ahead of midterm elections
Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages, torch cars and trees during olive harvest
stories.summary: Residents and human rights organisations say Israeli authorities have done little to stop settler attacks. They allege that soldiers have sometimes helped settlers, protected them or stood by while Palestinian villages came under assault. The violence has prompted accusations of “ethnic cleansing”, including from the British government, which accused Israel of turning a “blind eye” to the campaign.

stories.title: Indian-origin Met Police officer charged with attempted rape, sexual assault in London
Off-duty US soldier saves gunshot victim, earns Army Commendation Medal for quick first aid
stories.summary: When gunfire erupted near his residence, Private First Class Stephen Bradley sprang into action, showcasing his military training to help a gunshot victim. His quick thinking involved applying a tourniquet and pressure dressing, stabilizing the civilian's injuries until emergency responders arrived. Local authorities are actively investigating the shooting, while Bradley's bravery earned him the Army Commendation Medal for his commendable response during this critical situation.

stories.title: 'No vessel in sight': At least 16 people rescued from Pacific Ocean off Mexico’s coast
Indian national charged in US over false citizenship claim to vote in 2024 election; faces up to 10 years in prison
Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.

stories.title: Putin, Trump to announce several joint projects as Russian diesel returns to market
stories.summary: Russia and the United States are set to announce new initiatives beyond their recent diesel agreement. Discussions reportedly include collaborative data centre projects powered by Russian nuclear energy. Supplies of diesel have begun reaching international markets following the deal with the United States. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the arrangement, expressing concerns about its implications for energy revenue.

stories.title: Dolly Parton donated $100,000 for a healing garden at a hospital tied to her family roots
stories.summary: A new $55 million medical facility has opened in South Carolina, featuring an outdoor healing garden. This garden was funded by a $100,000 donation from country music star Dolly Parton, honoring her family's local roots. The garden aims to provide patients and their families a peaceful retreat during difficult times. Parton expressed her support for the hospital staff and future patients during the opening ceremony.

stories.title: Mailchimp’s founders turned a side project into a $12 billion business without outside funding
stories.summary: Originating from humble beginnings, Mailchimp evolved within two decades from a small business tool to a powerhouse in the marketing industry. Launched by The Rocket Science Group's Ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius, it caught the attention of Intuit, who acquired it for around $12 billion in 2021. With a sharp focus on customer-centric innovation and maintaining independence, Mailchimp solidified its status as a leader in global digital marketing.

stories.title: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target
stories.summary: A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.

stories.title: NCW steps in after video shows senior J&K IAS officer 'abusing' woman subordinate
California wildfires spread amid strong winds; over 150,000 customers without power
stories.summary: Southern California is currently grappling with wildfires, prompting evacuation orders in several communities and causing widespread power outages. The combination of heat and dryness has amplified fire risks, with strong winds anticipated. Firefighters are actively battling flames in areas like Malibu and Azusa, urging locals to stay alert. In an effort to mitigate fire hazards, precautionary power outages have been instituted across numerous regions.

stories.title: 'OH'IO No: Vivek Ramaswamy's Catch-22 problem with MAGA
stories.summary: Ramaswamy is running to become Ohio governor, a position he perhaps sees as a stepping stone to something bigger in the party. Yet Ramaswamy’s association with Trump is increasingly becoming a liability among neutral voters, while his faith and skin colour are proving a deterrent among parts of the MAGA base.

stories.title: US midterms 2026: DOJ sues California, claims 20,000 suspected ‘noncitizen voters’; seeks to block mail ballots
India diversified crude oil sources from 27 to 41 amid disruptions in Hormuz, Red Sea: Hardeep Puri
stories.summary: India has expanded its crude oil supply sources from 27 to 41 countries to improve energy security. The government is also increasing its refining capacity and exploring new oil sources in response to geopolitical concerns. Minister Hardeep Singh Puri emphasized the impact of global shipping disruptions on domestic industries and households. He outlined plans to enhance domestic energy production through initiatives like the Samudra Manthan scheme.

stories.title: 'While with Nitish, I got 9 people murdered': Anant Singh's shocking claim, then clarification
stories.summary: Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Anant Snigh claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said. However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates.

stories.title: Renner’s $7M mansion makeover sells for $24M three years later
'We'll knock it out fast': Trump may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility
stories.summary: Donald Trump indicated that the US may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility to deter nuclear weapon development. He stated that nuclear weapons would not be necessary for achieving US objectives in the situation. The remarks followed ongoing US-Israeli strikes against Iran since February, amid rising tensions. Iran's foreign ministry denied any nuclear activity at the site, labeling US threats as baseless.

stories.title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
stories.summary: Opposition parties in India are gradually uniting to support protests against the Chief Election Commissioner. Following arrests of CJP leaders, Rahul Gandhi showed solidarity, signaling a possible shift in strategy. Previously, Congress and CJP had organized separate protests over electoral issues, but they now seem to be collaborating more closely.

stories.title: HM Shah slams Punjab govt on murders of anti-drugs crusaders, MHA seeks report on 3 recent cases
Oprah Winfrey donated $12 million to a Smithsonian museum in 2013; it still celebrates Black history
stories.summary: With a remarkable contribution of $13 million, Oprah Winfrey has solidified her legacy at the National Museum of African American History and Culture. Her financial support was instrumental in the museum's fundraising efforts, culminating in the naming of the Oprah Winfrey Theater. This theater serves as a vital space for public events, fostering discussions surrounding African American history and cultural narratives.

stories.title: 'Steady improvement': Vatican releases first pictures of Pope Leo XIV after lung surgery
Car registered to teen who planned mass shooting at Auora was at the parking lot of Hindu temple; Balaji temple issues statement
Marine experts call for satellite-based decision support system for sustainabler fisheries amid climate crisis
Pennsylvania court blocked a $250,000 farm sale after siblings challenged a 99-year lease deal
stories.summary: Siblings are embroiled in a legal conflict over the fate of their family-owned 60-acre farm in Pennsylvania. A sister residing on the land sought to sell it despite having a long-term tenancy. In response, her siblings filed an urgent petition to block the sale, citing property rights. The Pennsylvania Superior Court supported the injunction, illustrating the complicated nature of co-ownership and informal familial arrangements in property disputes.

stories.title: Russian officer helped Ukraine kill over 300 troops by leaking military secrets
stories.summary: Russian army lieutenant Lev Stupnikov took a perilous stand against his own military by secretly supplying Ukrainian forces with critical intelligence. His actions led to the targeted elimination of more than 300 Russian soldiers and deliberate sabotage of weapons systems, culminating in his flight to the Russian Volunteer Corps as a direct challenge to Putin's leadership. Stupnikov’s bravery reshaped the landscape of the ongoing Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: 'Interfering in electoral practices': India pulls up US lawmaker for claims on voter roll deletions
stories.summary: India has dismissed Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's remarks regarding its electoral process as unwarranted and uninformed. The Ministry of External Affairs warned that her comments interfere with India’s democratic practices. India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, also rejected these allegations as unacceptable interference. The Election Commission of India is currently conducting a nationwide revision of electoral rolls in various phases.

stories.title: Iowa couple restore 40 acres choked with invasive plants; rare habitats draw sandhill cranes
PM-SETU clears Rs 1,195 crore for five ITI clusters in 3 states, J&K
stories.summary: Total investment approved under scheme rises to Rs 3,687 crore; five industry partners to help upgrade training infrastructure and courses

stories.title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by police
stories.summary: AISA chief Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police while heading to a protest, and was taken to an unknown location. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke was also detained at his residence shortly before the protest. Police stated the situation remained peaceful despite the detentions and heightened security in the capital. Hundreds of protesters gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House, waving national flags.

stories.title: Judge upholds solar deal on 562.8 acres, keeping $330M project in play
UN warns Russian attacks and winter hardship could displace more Ukrainians
stories.summary: As winter approaches, Ukraine faces dire challenges with essential services declining due to ongoing conflict. Millions of internally displaced individuals struggle to reunite with their homes, often in ruins. With falling temperatures, access to heating, electricity, and safe drinking water becomes precarious. Funding shortages jeopardize relief initiatives, leaving countless families at risk. Humanitarian organizations are ramping up efforts to offer vital support to affected communities.

stories.title: MHA seeks reports from Punjab government on killings, suicide linked to anti-drug efforts
stories.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has called for detailed reports from Punjab's authorities concerning two violent occurrences linked to the fight against drugs. The first incident, the murder of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh in Mansa, ignited widespread protests. Meanwhile, an assault on Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur resulted in his death.

stories.title: Centre expands Census enumerator pool to include private school teachers, clerks
stories.summary: Under the amended rules, teachers working in educational institutions run by the government, local authorities, aided or unaided private bodies, societies and trusts can be appointed as enumerators. The eligibility list also covers clerks and other officials working for the Central and state governments, local authorities and various establishments. The Census Rules were first published in the Gazette of India on December 31, 1990.

stories.title: ‘Police can break bones, not satyagraha’: Rahul Gandhi alleges Delhi Police refused to file FIR over assault on student protesters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged that Delhi Police failed to register an FIR regarding the assault on student protesters. He mentioned two young women were among those harmed, prompting legal action against police officers. Detentions occurred ahead of a proposed Tiranga rally in Connaught Place, highlighting increased security measures in the area. Police cited restrictions and prior agreements while detaining activists to maintain public order.

stories.title: Michigan Court Upholds 2012 Survivorship Deed, Rejects Daughter’s Claim to Troy Home
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court has confirmed the validity of a survivorship deed that granted ownership of a house to Jessica Rae Harless. The ruling asserts that Shirley Ann Page's 2012 deed established a joint tenancy with rights of survivorship. Despite Anita Lanctot's challenge regarding the absence of the term 'joint' in the deed, the court affirmed that Page's intent was unmistakably conveyed, ensuring Harless retains sole ownership of the property.

stories.title: China asks Katie Zacharia to visit more often as press secretary says China did not have proper toilets
Valid ID cards, 'impartial' reporting, basic first-aid: Press Council issues guidelines for journalists covering anti-SIR protests
Thieves steal 30,000 wine bottles worth $5.8 million using winery’s forklifts
‘Racism isn’t welcome’: Australian MP condemns anti-Indian stickers with ‘Remigration now’ message
Georgia renter warned landlord about tree; after it crushed his home, appeals court revived claims
stories.summary: William Frank Jennings, a Lindale, Georgia resident, became paralyzed after a tree fell on his house, despite having warned his landlord about its dangerous state. The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that his claims against Romulus Investments were improperly dismissed, noting significant conflicting evidence regarding hazard notifications. This ruling enables Jennings to pursue his case further to potentially establish liability and seek damages for his injuries.

stories.title: John Griffin sells Regent’s Park mansion at £9.2m loss
stories.summary: John Griffin, the mind behind Addison Lee, experienced a substantial loss after selling his lavish London mansion for £11.5 million, down from the £20.7 million he paid in 2013, incurring a staggering loss of £9.2 million. This sale reflects the broader downturn in London's property landscape, impacted by economic instability and new tax regulations.

stories.title: Henry Nowak murder case: Sikh man's mother may be released early under new UK prison rules
MEA confirms Jaishankar-Rubio talks in Mumbai after Rahul’s jibe over India visit
stories.summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal announced the engagements while responding to a question from news agency ANI about whether Jaishankar was expected to hold any meetings in Mumbai next week. He also explained that hosting foreign dignitaries outside the national capital was not unusual, pointing to previous engagements held in different Indian cities.

stories.title: ‘Ensure safety of Indian nationals’: MEA’s strong message to US after alleged Hindu temple attack plot
stories.summary: Authorities in Aurora thwarted a disturbing mass-shooting scheme aimed at a local Hindu temple. In light of this, the Indian ministry of external affairs voiced alarm over the rise in hate crimes in the United States. A 19-year-old suspect now faces charges for threatening the temple while armed. Meanwhile, Indian-American organizations are mobilizing to spotlight anti-Indian sentiment and exploring collective response strategies.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: CJP's Dipke detained, Rajnath alleges regime change bid and Rahul's cryptic Rubio post
75,000-year-old Neanderthal remains reveal possible fatal spear attack and signs of care
stories.summary: A Neanderthal who lived 75,000 years ago survived a severe facial injury for at least a year before suffering a possibly fatal spear wound. Researchers studying remains found in Iraq’s Shanidar Cave identified a 15mm hole in the shoulder blade, suggesting a wooden spear injury. The findings also point to possible care from other Neanderthals.

stories.title: 'I am alone': CJP's Dipke argues with cops during detention ahead of Tiranga march - watch
stories.summary: Dipke, earlier today, had defended the party's protests, asserting that peaceful demonstrations were a democratic right. He accused the government of restricting citizens' freedoms and disrupting business activities through shutdowns, Internet suspensions and movement restrictions. "I'm alone, what law did I break," Dipke asked before he was detained. The court had directed the CJP to refrain from causing any public disturbance for a period of one year.

stories.title: Ladakh administration announces Sankoo as eighth district
stories.summary: The authorities in Ladakh have announced the formation of Sankoo as its eighth district, fulfilling a long-awaited aspiration. Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena underscored this decision as part of the government's commitment to progress. Various local organizations, notably Anjuman-e-Sahib Zaman led by Syed Mohammad Razvi, played a crucial role in this development.

stories.title: 'Protesters ignorant of ground realities': Delhi traders write to PM Modi over losses
stories.summary: The traders urged the authorities to ensure a transparent assessment of the losses suffered by shopkeepers following the October 10 protest and recover full compensation from the principal organisers and participants responsible, rather than place the financial burden on traders already struggling with lost business. It said shop earnings supported traders' families and employees, while covering shop rents, children's education and medical expenses for elderly parents.

stories.title: ‘Regime change’ remark row: BJP chief Nitin Nabin says opposition’s ‘true agenda’ exposed
'Don't try to bulldoze another Constitutional Amendment Bill': Kharge writes to PM Modi
‘Refrain from actions prejudicial to citizens’ rights’: Delhi Police notice to CJP's Abhijeet Dipke ahead of Tiranga march
New York pays $28.25 million for land around abandoned nuclear plant, plans public access
stories.summary: New York has purchased nearly 750 acres surrounding the former Shoreham Nuclear Power Plant on Long Island for $28.25 million. The acquisition, the largest in the history of the state's Department of Environmental Conservation on Long Island, will permanently protect coastal forests, wetlands and wildlife habitats. The state also plans to develop public trails, parking facilities and beach access in the coming years.

stories.title: ‘True character of protests exposed’: Dharmendra Pradhan attacks Rahul Gandhi over regime change remark
stories.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan criticized Rahul Gandhi for allegedly exploiting student protests to undermine India's democratic structure. He claimed these actions indicated a desire to create instability comparable to the situation in Bangladesh. In response, the Congress party maintained that their focus is on achieving a regime change through democratic elections. Ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar also contributed to the controversy surrounding the electoral process.

stories.title: Trump calls Ukraine attack on Russian oil refineries 'a disgrace', irks Zelenskyy
stories.summary: The Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was little indication that Moscow was ready to end the war and warned that Kyiv needed to prepare for the coming winter. "We want to end this war as quick as possible. We don't see now signals from the Russian side that they are ready for this, to end this war, that's why we have to prepare for the winter," Zelenskyy said.

stories.title: Indian student Deepak Sandhu convicted of murdering woman at London Airbnb after she confronted him over stolen £500
Queensland protects 396,000 hectares of cattle stations, safeguarding wetlands and threatened birds
stories.summary: Queensland proudly announces the acquisition of three significant cattle properties, expanding its protected area network by almost 396,000 hectares. These lands are essential for wildlife conservation, providing critical habitats for various threatened species. Funded by the federal government through a biodiversity initiative, this move contributes to Australia's ambitious target of safeguarding 30 percent of its land and oceans by 2030.

stories.title: She started making soda in her kitchen; a decade later, PepsiCo bought her brand for $1.95 billion
stories.summary: Allison Ellsworth began making homemade soda in her Texas kitchen to address her digestive concerns before selling it at farmers’ markets. After appearing on Shark Tank and building Poppi through social media, her business grew to over $500 million in annual revenue. In 2025, PepsiCo acquired the prebiotic soda brand for $1.95 billion.

stories.title: 'Jagga Jasoos': Congress mocks Rajnath Singh over opposition demanding regime change
Colorado ninth-grader Peter Daniell wins $100,000 education contribution for food insecurity essay
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, Peter Daniell of Colorado has clinched victory in the 2026 National Civics Bee by tackling the pressing issue of food insecurity with impressive civic insights. Competing against 20,000 students nationwide, Daniell's essay underscored the vital role of community engagement and public service in ensuring food access. For his dedication, he was awarded a $100,000 education prize and expressed heartfelt gratitude for the backing he received.

stories.title: 99-year-old Helga Duffy breaks wing-walking record, raises £1,300 for air ambulance

A Maine couple grew their own wedding flowers in a backyard garden
stories.summary: Mariah Reading and David Mainero chose to grow their wedding flowers instead of buying them to save expenses. They planted a garden in Hampden, Maine, with various blooms including dahlias and amaranth. The couple learned about gardening while preparing for their September wedding and received help from friends and family. Reading picked her bouquet from this garden, adding a personal touch to their celebration.

'FriYAY plans? We got ideas for you!' CJP issues call for Tiranga march at 5pm as CP park shut
Indiana man builds 60,000-gallon backyard water park
stories.summary: Cory Johnson of Cromwell decided to elevate his backyard experience, opting for a private water park after a frustratingly long pool installation wait. His dream evolved from a basic pool design, famously sketched on a napkin, into a spectacular 60,000-gallon water park featuring special attractions. With rentals at $140 per hour and a steady stream of bookings, he's also eyeing future upgrades like a steam cave and relaxing hot spring.

Martin Phipps and Paramour to vacate San Antonio building after $1.2M fraud verdict
Virginia protects 2,211 acres at Buffalo Mountain with new conservation area
Barbra Streisand’s $10 million gift helps women’s heart centre treat 1,700 patients annually
stories.summary: Barbra Streisand's generous donation of $10 million to Cedars-Sinai has paved the way for the creation of the Women’s Heart Center. This groundbreaking facility aims to delve into the disparities in cardiovascular health among women, addressing unique diagnostic and treatment challenges. Annually, over 1,700 women benefit from specialized cardiac care, emphasizing tailored medical approaches for heart disease, ultimately showcasing the critical need for research in women's health.

stories.title: At 11, UK-based Aneeshwar Kunchala to receive Junior Jane Goodall Earth Medal for wildlife conservation
stories.summary: Aneeshwar Kunchala, a passionate young wildlife educator, is set to receive the prestigious Junior Jane Goodall Earth Medal in 2026. His journey into conservation began at just four years old when he learned about the devastating effects of plastic on whales. Celebrated for his remarkable contributions to wildlife advocacy through media, he has initiated citizen science projects and engaging educational presentations that inspire children to connect with nature.

stories.title: 'Hope better sense prevails': SC flags traders' livelihood concerns as Delhi braces for CJP's Tiranga march
10-year-old New Jersey girl writes poem on Colombian heritage, makes it to Top 10 in poetry contest
stories.summary: A 10-year-old girl from New Jersey has been named among the Top 10 winners of Creative Communication’s national poetry contest. Luisa Gonzalez’s poem, All Stitched Together, was selected from thousands of entries. Inspired by the Colombian flag, the poem reflects her cultural identity and pride in her heritage. She had previously received honourable mentions in the competition.

Trans teen accused of Hindu temple attack plot to receive hormone shots in jail
California students invented a cooling device for firefighters and farmworkers
stories.summary: Students at Calistoga Junior/Senior High School developed a cooling device targeting hot working conditions. They presented their invention at EurekaFest and the California State Capitol. The project utilized a $7,500 grant from the InvenTeams initiative to support their research and development. Their invention gained recognition as a finalist for the SXSW Innovation Awards. The InvenTeams program aims to inspire students to address real-world problems through practical inventions.

ICMR picks 7 centres to develop priority medical devices, diagnostics
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has chosen seven prominent research centres within leading institutions to spearhead the development of innovative medical devices and diagnostic solutions. These projects, which include collaborations with IIT Bombay, IISc Bengaluru, and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, will target critical areas like portable screening, biomaterials, and treatments for eye diseases.

stories.title: ‘The name is George Soros’: American singer Mary Millben alleges US funding behind Delhi protests against CEC
stories.summary: Mary Millben alleges that billionaire George Soros is financially backing protests in India with the intention of undermining Prime Minister Modi's government. She urges young Indians to stand with Modi to actively challenge what she deems as disruptive protests. Millben also criticizes Rahul Gandhi of Congress and Abhijeet Dipke of the Cockroach Janta Party for their involvement, while emphasizing that having clear objectives is crucial for impactful change.

stories.title: Michael Douglas keeps his Mallorca estate as family retreat
stories.summary: Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones enjoy their historic estate, S'Estaca, located in Mallorca. The property, set on 190 acres, features multiple buildings and stunning views of the Mediterranean Sea. Douglas originally purchased the estate in 1990 with his first wife, Diandra Luker, and they later became the sole owners. The couple has created cherished family memories there, raising their two children while entertaining numerous famous guests.

stories.title: Washington captures record 2.16 million invasive green crabs, but experts warn invasion is far from over
stories.summary: Washington state removed more than 2.16 million invasive European green crabs during fiscal year 2025-26. First detected in the state in 2016, the species threatens native marine life, including clams, oysters and eelgrass. Despite more than $8 million in state funding, no established populations have been eradicated, and researchers warn the invasion could worsen.

stories.title: Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr help erase $550 million in medical debt, support LA wildfire survivors
stories.summary: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel and wife Miranda Kerr are helping erase $550 million in medical debt for more than 261,000 Californians and supporting Los Angeles wildfire survivors. Spiegel recalled watching his childhood home burn during the January 2025 fires. The couple's philanthropy also includes community relief, long-term health research and encouraging their children to give back.

stories.title: Elvis Presley’s former Beverly Hills home sells for $25.5 million after decades of renovations
stories.summary: In 1967, Elvis and Priscilla Presley acquired an opulent home in Beverly Hills' Trousdale Estates for $400,000. Their tenure at the estate lasted until 1973, marking the period when their daughter Lisa Marie was born. After significant renovations, the property was sold in 2019 for an impressive $25.5 million, showcasing the lasting allure of celebrity residences and the historic value they carry.

stories.title: Owens Backs Carlson Claims: She accuses Ben Shapiro of hostile view of Christians; feud over Noahide Laws
stories.summary: Candace Owens has backed Tucker Carlson in his dispute with Ben Shapiro over the Noahide Laws. Owens accused Shapiro of holding a hostile view of Christians and criticized his past relationship with Charlie Kirk. Shapiro rejected Carlson’s claims, arguing that his comments about Judaism had been misunderstood. The disagreement has become a public clash over religion and personal accusations.

stories.title: London council seeks public help identifying fly-tippers as illegal dumping cases rise across England
stories.summary: Hillingdon Council in west London is urging residents to identify suspected fly-tippers through CCTV images shared on Facebook. The enforcement drive has resulted in more than 300 fixed penalty notices worth around £134,000. England recorded over 1.26 million fly-tipping incidents last year, a 9% increase, with serious offenders facing prison sentences.

stories.title: Thrift Find Becomes Windfall: £20 charity-shop jars confirmed as Qing porcelain; auction brings £58,000
stories.summary: A casual ceramics collector stumbled upon two seemingly ordinary porcelain jars in a London charity shop priced at just $25. After a detailed assessment, experts revealed these jars were actually rare 18th-century Qing Dynasty artifacts adorned with imperial designs and intricate floral patterns. The jars sparked considerable interest and fetched an astonishing £58,000 at auction, translating to over $74,000, significantly benefiting the charity involved.

Taylor Swift donated 6,000 books to a library in 2011, helping it serve 27,452 people in 2025
stories.summary: In 2011, Taylor Swift generously donated 6,000 books to bolster local libraries in Berks County amid looming budget cuts. This pivotal support allowed the Reading Public Library to enrich its programs and attract thousands of community members. By 2025, the library circulated over 182,000 items and continued to foster engagement through various initiatives, proving Swift’s contribution remains vital for the region's library services to this day.

stories.title: Kansas couple transforms backyard into a 100,000-gallon tropical lagoon with six waterfalls
stories.summary: Melissa and Mike Morris dedicated nearly a year to constructing a stunning 100,000-gallon swimming lagoon in Olathe, Kansas. Inspired by the beauty of Tahiti, they created a coastal paradise at home, complete with granite rocks, flowing waterfalls, and vibrant tropical fish. Their captivating project drew attention online, leading to requests for exclusive photo sessions and events, while they relish their private backyard oasis as they finalize the landscaping.

stories.title: Scientists make cells from an 80-year-old donor appear young, advancing ageing research
stories.summary: Scientists have reprogrammed blood-cell precursors from an 80-year-old donor into neural stem cells with an epigenetic age below 20, according to a study published in Aging Cell. The process unfolded gradually over more than 100 days, offering researchers a way to investigate cellular rejuvenation and its potential implications for ageing and Alzheimer's research.

stories.title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Palm Beach mansion rises from $725,000 to $36 million
stories.summary: El Solano, a captivating mansion nestled in Palm Beach, was acquired by music legend John Lennon and his partner Yoko Ono in 1980. Following Lennon’s untimely passing, Yoko executed extensive renovations before offloading the property in 1986. The illustrious estate changed hands several times, skyrocketing in value, and ultimately fetched $36 million in 2020. Today, it stands as a cherished landmark, intertwining Lennon’s artistic legacy with architectural history.

stories.title: Microsoft president Brad Smith says it's ironic that White House targeted his company the same day it gave a medal to former H-1B Satya Nadella
Mahomes and Kelce’s jerseys sold for $250,000, helping raise $3.97 million for childhood cancer
stories.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs stars, Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, showcased their commitment to charity by donating signed jerseys that sold for a remarkable $250,000. This generous contribution is part of the Big Slick Celebrity Weekend, which successfully raised $3.97 million for pediatric cancer initiatives at Children's Mercy Hospital, bringing total donations to over $21 million since the event's launch in 2010.

stories.title: Shark tours make people 40% more likely to protect sharks
stories.summary: Shark populations are declining significantly due to human activities and a third of species are threatened. Participation in shark ecotourism leads to increased conservation efforts among tourists and the public. After two years, those who engaged in ecotourism showed a 40% increase in conservation activities. Educational experiences during these tours provide vital information about the role of sharks in the ecosystem.

stories.title: Michigan woman seeks $250 refund after $350 deep clean, claiming poor service and a missed re-clean
stories.summary: Michigan woman Kimberly Kemper is seeking a $250 refund after paying $350 for a deep clean. She says dishes, walls and baseboards were left dirty and the cleaner failed to return for a promised re-clean. Business owner Cecilia Bodart offered a $100 refund, apologised for poor communication and maintained the work warranted payment.

stories.title: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours
stories.summary: Yemen armed forces reported conducting 1,250 targeting operations against Houthis in one day. These strikes coincided with Houthi attacks on Aden’s presidential palace, resulting in casualties. Houthi spokesperson denied claims of missile strikes towards Medina, asserting their innocence. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted several missiles aimed at its territories amid ongoing tensions. Overall, hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have intensified over recent months.

stories.title: Indiana teen brothers, 15 and 14, rescue grandmother and two children from pond; toddler revived
stories.summary: During a tense moment in Carmel, Indiana, two brothers displayed extraordinary bravery by rescuing a grandmother and her grandchildren from a pond. Their ordeal began when a pushchair slipped into the water, triggering panic. The older brother dove in, employing life-saving measures that successfully revived a two-year-old boy who had momentarily lost consciousness. The brothers will receive community recognition for their courageous actions at the next city council meeting.

28-foot statue of biblical pharaoh who enslaved Israelis discovered by Egyptian farmer
stories.summary: A farmer in Behbeit El Hagar, Egypt stumbled upon a remarkable royal statue of Ramses II while tilling his land. In a swift response, local antiquities officials began an excavation to retrieve the statue along with other artifacts. They uncovered a substantial head of Ramses II and several smaller statues embellished with inscriptions. This discovery is expected to deepen our knowledge of ancient Egypt's cultural and political legacy.

‘Will stand with Pakistan if US attacks’: Rajasthan BJP chief’s remark sparks Congress backlash
stories.summary: Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore stated that India would align with Pakistan in a potential US-Pakistan conflict. This statement has drawn significant criticism from Congress leaders, including Shama Mohamed. Mohamed questioned the BJP's stance and asked for clarification from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rathore also accused Rahul Gandhi of inciting unrest and mentioned foreign interference in India's stability.

stories.title: US midterms: Trump warns voters Democrats will 'destroy' America, backs Andy Biggs in Arizona governor race
China, Pakistan hold high-altitude army drills with Beijing-supplied arms
stories.summary: In a landmark move, China and Pakistan have kicked off their inaugural joint military exercise, dubbed Karakoram 2026, in the high-altitude region of Xinjiang. This operation emphasizes counter-terrorism strategies, utilizing advanced Chinese military technology. The participating forces aim to refine their skills in mountainous terrains, thus fortifying the strategic partnership between the two nations. The exercise promises improved synergy as troops navigate shared operational standards.

stories.title: SC Bar Association files criminal contempt plea against Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle
stories.summary: Attorney General R Venkataramani has since granted consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against the two under the Contempt of Courts Act. The statements came after Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request last week from a delegation of opposition parties to meet him in person. The CJI said the delegation could instead file a petition before the court.

stories.title: ‘Big items are done’: Envoy Gor hints major boost in India-US trade negotiations
stories.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor confirmed that negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement are advancing rapidly. Both sides have resolved major issues and are close to finalizing the agreement. Gor emphasized that the pace of negotiations is unusually swift compared to previous trade deals. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also indicated that progress ensures a positive outcome is imminent.

stories.title: ‘Her misconceptions’: India rejects US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter rolls
After 50 years of fighting, Austin may secure Muny’s 141 acres while UT develops 190 acres nearby
stories.summary: Austin residents have passionately defended the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course for years, opposing potential developers. A new proposal seeks to officially hand over ownership of the golf course to the city, safeguarding its future. In return, the University of Texas would gain revised development regulations for neighboring properties on Lake Austin Boulevard. Officials assert that this arrangement effectively balances the need for green spaces with urban expansion.

stories.title: IGL rolls out AI system to check CNG cylinder safety at pumps
stories.summary: Indraprastha Gas Ltd has implemented an AI-enabled vehicle recognition system at various CNG stations in Delhi. This technology checks the hydrotest status of CNG cylinders to enhance safety measures. It ensures that vehicles with invalid certifications are alerted and refuelling is halted. The initiative follows a cylinder blast incident, prompting stricter enforcement of safety norms. The system will soon be deployed at all CNG stations managed by IGL.

stories.title: Renewable energy expansion needs to be aligned with transmission readiness: Experts
US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
stories.summary: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

stories.title: Is Dhanush ready to make his political debut? Fan club's new avatar sparks buzz
stories.summary: Dhanush's fan club has evolved into the Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam, signaling possible political ambitions. The organization plans to set up local welfare units in five assembly constituencies within Coimbatore district. This transition involves the introduction of a new logo and flag, streamlining its identity. Although comparisons with Vijay's political path are inevitable, Dhanush has not made any official announcements regarding his political intentions, fueling speculation about his future moves.

stories.title: Families await return of 3 Indians killed in Germany fire; Kerala CM assures help with repatriation
Van Gogh’s hidden 1890 masterpiece resurfaces after 60 years, with a $180 million auction estimate
stories.summary: Vincent van Gogh's exquisite painting, Châtaigniers en fleurs, has resurfaced after being tucked away for over sixty years and will soon hit the auction block in New York. With an estimated value of around $180 million, this piece could shatter records. Once acquired in 1975, it has remained within the Blaquier family collection, drawing excitement from collectors, particularly during the recent preview in Hong Kong.

stories.title: Delhi Police signals conditional nod for flag-waving, anthem at CJP's Oct 16 march amid curbs
In 2013, friends launched RXBAR with $10,000; Kellogg bought it for $600 million four years later
stories.summary: In 2013, aspiring entrepreneurs Peter Rahal and Jared Smith launched RXBAR while searching for nutritious protein bars. Starting from Rahal's parents' basement, they sold directly to customers. Their venture gained tremendous traction, culminating in a $600 million acquisition by the Kellogg Company in 2017, highlighting a significant trend towards clean-label snacks. Rahal remained CEO for two years post-acquisition before transitioning out.

stories.title: Brazil plants 840,000 trees to restore 607 hectares of Atlantic Forest
stories.summary: Brazil's Atlantic Forest is undergoing remarkable restoration efforts, spearheaded by World Land Trust and Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu. With 840,000 trees planted over 20 years, 607 hectares of degraded land have been revived into verdant forest. This initiative has created a vital wildlife corridor, facilitating the return of over 220 bird species to the previous wetland, while striving to protect and enhance the Guapiaçu watershed's remaining forest.

stories.title: 8-year-old Indian-origin girl dies of myocarditis after doctors missed warning signs; Australian coroner finds death preventable
Amit Shah vows to eliminate every trace of Naxalism after five decades of tribal suffering
stories.summary: Amit Shah highlighted the importance of eradicating Naxalism to restore growth in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. He noted that significant efforts had been made in this regard by local tribal leadership. Shah mentioned a distribution program of assistive devices benefiting over 3,600 disabled individuals, particularly Naxal violence victims. He emphasized the need to heal the wounds from years of suffering while maintaining that Naxalism's end does not restore dignity immediately.

stories.title: US not to livestream execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan
stories.summary: Former US Army Major Nidal Hasan is scheduled for execution by firing squad on December 3, for the 2009 shooting at the US Army's Fort Hood base in Texas. Donald Trump stated that the execution will not be livestreamed, despite previous announcements from the Pentagon. Howevr, immediate family members of the victims may attend in person, if they choose.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea to hold protest organisers liable for damage
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has requested responses regarding a plea to hold protest organizers accountable for damages. This includes potential liabilities for loss of life, injuries, and property damage incurred during protests. Additionally, the plea advocates for designated protest locations to minimize disturbances in densely populated areas. It proposes that protest organizers disclose their funding sources to ensure transparency.

stories.title: France begins implementing agreement to protect Saudi oil facilities; what it means
stories.summary: France has started deploying military resources to Saudi Arabia to protect its oil facilities from regional attacks. This decision follows an agreement aimed at enhancing defense cooperation, especially amid increased drone and missile threats. President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the deployment, which includes soldiers and defense systems to bolster security. Recent attacks by Houthi militants have escalated tensions in the area, raising concerns for energy stability.

stories.title: Donald Trump is looking for a replacement of Susie Wiles; 'She's burned a lot of people': Report
J&K HC restricts motorboat operations on Dal Lake
stories.summary: The high court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has ordered a ban on fuel-powered motorboats and jet skis on Dal Lake. Authorities are directed to enforce this prohibition strictly to protect the lake from pollution. The court suggested exploring solar-powered boats as an alternative for tourism-related activities. Emergency services and safety operations are exempt from this ban. A comprehensive policy on motorised boat operations is expected for further review.

stories.title: Bought in 2014, Magnolia’s Waco site grew from to 5.3 acres, adding shops, a ball field and church
stories.summary: In a remarkable transformation, Chip and Joanna Gaines have converted a historic cottonseed mill site in Waco into a buzzing tourist hub. Spanning 5.3 acres, the revitalized Magnolia property now features an array of shops, dining venues, and lush green spaces. Guests can experience restored historic buildings like the Old Church, while the newly built Katy Ballpark commemorates the original Katy Park.

stories.summary: A sandwich idea at 15 led Miami student Gabriella Rothberg to develop genetically engineered tomatoes designed to produce heme, an iron-containing molecule associated with meat flavour. Now 17, she is listed alongside her father on a US patent issued in June 2026. The project remains experimental, with taste and nutritional benefits yet to be established.

stories.title: Police shooting, water shortages, rising costs: Mauritius extends curfew amid unrest
stories.summary: Mauritius has extended a curfew for two additional nights after protests erupted over police violence. The unrest followed the shooting of a woman by a police officer in Camp Levieux, prompting increased tensions. Authorities reported over 100 arrests related to the disturbances and canceled school classes for security reasons. Anger over rising living costs and worsening water shortages has fueled public discontent across the island.

stories.title: IMD announces onset of winter monsoon in south Peninsular India, summer monsoon withdrawal completes on normal date
stories.summary: The southwest monsoon in India withdrew on schedule. Simultaneously, the northeast monsoon commenced, bringing rainfall to parts of south Peninsular India. Regions including Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and coastal Andhra Pradesh experienced the initial winter rainfall. Predictions indicate a normal winter monsoon may provide relief after a significant summer rainfall deficit.

stories.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
stories.summary: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.

stories.title: 13-year-old Indian-American wins $25,000 for ocean acidification solution
EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
stories.summary: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.

India has called for a US investigation into a potential mass shooting plot against a Hindu temple. The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi for undermining institutions during protests against the chief election commissioner. Congress questioned the government’s silence on Marco Rubio's planned visit to India.

stories.title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
stories.summary: Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. Soaring food prices and the increasing frequency of climate-related disasters have sharply intensified food insecurity. With around 218 million individuals in South Asia experiencing undernourishment from 2023 to 2025, urgent strategies are required to bolster access to healthy food and enhance agricultural resilience against severe weather patterns.

stories.summary: Brics began with five members and grew to eleven after the 2024 expansion, with Indonesia the newest, joining in 2025. Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of the one nation. Iran. It feared that adding the avowedly anti-West Islamic Republic would cost the group its cohesion. Like India, Brazil wants Brics to be reformist and not revolutionary, thereby limiting it to a body that argues for change inside the existing order rather than one that tries to replace it.

This vibrant digital arts hub, established by George Lucas in 2005 post-demolition, now serves as a creative haven for Lucasfilm and other innovative firms. Careful attention to open spaces fosters community interaction and leisure, showcasing a successful model for urban redevelopment and creative collaborations.

stories.title: California cement worker turned discarded bottles into 200 desert art trees along Route 66
stories.summary: California cement worker Elmer Long transformed discarded glass bottles and scrap metal into an unusual art forest along Route 66. His two-acre Bottle Tree Ranch, featuring around 200 trees and over 1,000 bottles, became a popular tourist attraction. As Route 66 celebrates its 100th anniversary in 2026, Long's family continues to preserve his creations.

stories.title: Isaiah Zagar's 3,000-sq-ft Philadelphia maze of bottles and bike wheels was saved in 2004
stories.summary: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens, a vibrant masterpiece by Isaiah Zagar, comprises stunning mosaics made from found objects that capture his personal journey and artistic influences. In 2004, when demolition loomed, local advocates banded together to form a nonprofit, securing the beloved site. Over the years, Zagar enriched the gardens with imaginative tunnels and diverse mosaics, right up to his death in 2026.

Singh previously led the Congress in Punjab and left over internal conflicts within the party. He later formed the Punjab Lok Congress which did not succeed in recent elections.

stories.title: Govt issues clarification on 'unconditional apology' in SC over internet shutdown
stories.summary: In a statement, the government reacted to the media reports that the Union home secretary Govind Mohan had tendered an unconditional apology to the Supreme Court in response to a contempt notice. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the agreement, stating it could further support Moscow's military actions.

stories.title: New York art teacher’s thrift-store painting bought for under $100 sells for £189,200 after 60 years

Hidden for decades within a family's home, the artwork, initially misattributed, is revealed to be the work of Scottish artist Francis Campbell Boileau Cadell.

stories.title: 'Your Didi is with you - today and forever!' Mamata Banerjee to detained CJP activists
stories.summary: In a message posted on X on Wednesday, Banerjee condemned the arrests of Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were sent to judicial custody, and assured young people of her support. “Your Didi is with you - today and forever!” she wrote. The arrests came amid opposition protests in Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

stories.title: 'Why are you ruining nation?' CJP's Abhijeet Dipke heckled with 'CIA agent' remark at Delhi airport
stories.summary: Dipke landed in Delhi a day after his party's co-convenors, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, surreptitiously climbed a gate at the prohibited area of Jantar Mantar to protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the government, which has denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Wall Street titan lists bulletproof Upper East Side mansion for $80 million; property could become the neighbourhood’s priciest
stories.summary: John Mack and his wife Christy are putting their lavish Upper East Side townhouse on the market for a staggering $80 million. Selling at this price would establish a new benchmark for townhouses in New York City. Since purchasing it in 2009, they have extensively renovated the property, resulting in a 16,000-square-foot masterpiece that boasts upscale features such as a wellness club and exclusive guest quarters.

stories.title: Erin French rebuilt her life after losing her first restaurant; her Maine eatery now receives 60,000 reservation postcards a year
stories.summary: Erin French's remarkable journey saw her battling through addiction, enduring depression, and facing a heartbreaking divorce that led to the closure of her restaurant. Returning to her roots in Freedom, she innovatively launched pop-up dining events, rekindling her culinary passion. In 2014, she triumphantly reopened The Lost Kitchen in a refurbished mill, emphasizing seasonal, locally sourced goods, with a unique postcard reservation system that draws about 60,000 requests each year.

India seeks Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests: Rajnath Singh

Notably, the National Social Assistance Programme will be renamed PM Shayata Yojna to reinforce this updated branding strategy.

A USDA-funded trial demonstrated that cardboard beds reduced weed coverage compared to tilled beds. Farmers found that using cardboard made weeding easier and more efficient after two growing seasons. The results from the trial showed varied crop yields when grown in different bed types.

Additionally, the organization points to possible misuse by criminal organizations and the challenges posed by a foreign service potentially flouting local laws.

'Abhijieet Dipke, CJP funded by US donors': Singer Mary Millben backs PM Modi; pushes for counter-movement
stories.summary: Mary Millben has alleged that US-based donors are funding individuals opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She encouraged young Indians to rise up against disruptive forces and defend democracy. Millben highlighted a pattern among some US donors targeting conservative leaders globally. BJP leaders have raised questions about the funding of the Cockroach Janta Party and its founder. Dipke has denied allegations of receiving foreign funds, challenging government oversight.

stories.title: Polyethylene Microplastics And Liver Risk: Texas A&M links exposure to fatty liver signs; questions remain for human health
stories.summary: New research from Texas A&M University indicates that polyethylene microplastics may affect liver health negatively. The study observed significant signs of fatty liver disease linked to polyethylene exposure and a high-fat diet. Researchers found changes in gene activity related to fat metabolism and tissue repair. Future investigations will focus on whether these pollutants contribute to more severe liver damage.

stories.title: Two Arizona brothers, aged 10 and 12, vanished into the desert; a helicopter-assisted search found them safe after eight hours
stories.summary: On October 11, a frantic search ensued for two young brothers, Atom and Jack Ward, who vanished while playing outside. Their worried father alerted authorities when they didn't return home. A collaborative effort involving local businesses and rescue teams, along with aerial support from the Arizona Department of Public Safety, led to their discovery six miles from home, with one boy still barefoot.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance rover breaks Mars driving record, covering 28.1 miles in five years
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a new distance record on Mars, traveling 28.10 miles in its mission, eclipsing the previous record of 28.06 miles set by Opportunity in nearly 15 years. This remarkable feat, achieved over five and a half years, showcases Perseverance's advanced autonomous navigation system as it investigates ancient geological structures and collects rock samples to enhance our scientific insights.
